# Perform

Status: draft

Perform works on the whole pattern at once and live: nothing you do here is written into the steps. Twelve slots each hold one effect, and a pad press punches it in on the tracks you chose. You choose the tracks by holding `Shift` and using the top row of pads, not with screen keys. Three scenes, **HALF** and **DOUBLE** time, **NEXT PAT**, a pattern of its own for single tracks and **RESET** are new in track3r-os, and so is switching **LATCH** off. `Perform` pressed again opens the DJ page, which has [its own chapter](perform_dj.md).

## What it is for

Use Perform to change how the pattern sounds while it plays, with your hands, and to put it back by letting go. Press `Perform` to open it. Perform opens on the page you left it on: **SLOTS** the first time, or the [DJ page](perform_dj.md) if you left it there. Press `Perform` again to turn to the other page.

## How it works

### Live, not written

A Perform effect is a hand on the mixing desk, not a note in the pattern. The pattern keeps playing exactly as it was written, and the effect changes how it sounds while you hold it. An export never carries an effect.

- **Live:** which effects are acting now, the value you turn in with the encoder while a pad is down, and which tracks are on.
- **Stored with the project:** each slot's effect, its chosen row and its three values, the three scenes, and the **LATCH** switch.
- **Ends:** `F8` (**RESET**), the top pad of a slot, or leaving the screen for any screen except the Mixer (`Master`) and Song. Leaving also switches every track off. The chosen rows stay, so a latched value acts again as soon as you switch a track back on. `Play` and `Stop` do not end an effect.

Example: hold a low-pass pad over a drum loop. The notes in the pattern do not change, and when you let go the loop sounds as it did.

### Pads: a slot for each column, a row for each value

The 48 pads are a grid of four rows by twelve columns. Each column is one slot, and the slot holds one effect, named above it. Count the pads from 1, left to right, top row first. Pad 4 is slot 4 on the top row, and pad 16 is slot 4 on the second row.

The top row is **OFF**. The three rows below each keep a value. A new project starts them with three useful values for each effect, from mild to strong: **LOWPASS**, for example, has -30, -60 and -90, and **STUTTER** has 1/4, 1/8 and 1/16. A project you saved keeps its own values, 0 included.   The screen draws 0 as `---`, except for three effects that name their values: **PLAYBACK** draws it `>>>`, **STUTTER** draws **OFF** and **PLAYMODE** draws **FWD**. Press a pad and its row becomes the slot's chosen row, and the value goes to the tracks that are on. Turn the encoder while you hold the pad to change the value of the held slots.

Example: pad 4 is **LOWPASS** on its top row. Press it and the filter ends. Press pad 16 and turn the encoder left, and the filter closes while you hold. A negative value closes a low-pass filter and a positive one opens it. Not checked against the original firmware.

### Hold or latch

Turn the encoder and let go, and what happens depends on whether a value is stored. A value turned on its own is live: it lasts while the pad is down, and the pad's own stored value comes back when you let go (a stored 0 ends the effect). To keep a value, press `Rec` first. **EDIT** appears in the strip, and now the encoder stores the value in the row.

With **LATCH** on (the default), a row that holds a value stays on after you let go, until you press another row of its slot or the top pad. With LATCH off (`F6`), the effect ends at the release, stored value or not. The switch is saved with the project.

Example: store -40 in pad 16, with LATCH on. A tap on it keeps the filter closed with both hands free. A tap on pad 4 opens it. LATCH off is new in track3r-os, and so is the rule that a value turned in live ends at the release. Whether a live value should outlive the pad with LATCH on is an open question.

### Which tracks are affected

The boxes at the bottom, **T1** to **T12**, show **ON**, **OFF** or **MUTED**, or the number of the pattern a track plays when you have given it another one (see [Give single tracks another pattern](#give-single-tracks-another-pattern)). An effect acts only on the tracks that are **ON**. Hold `Shift` and the pads become the TRACKS layer: the top row switches each track on or off, row 2 mutes, row 3 sets the mute mode, and row 4 solos. A track that you switch on gets every effect that is on, latched ones included, at once, and one you switch off gets them all ended. Which tracks are on is not saved, and leaving Perform for most screens switches them all off. Different from the official manual, which uses screen keys.

Example: switch on T1 and T2, your drums. A low-pass now closes the drums and leaves the bass open.

### Which effects act

Up and Down in EDIT choose a slot's effect from a list of 21. All of them act. The three filters (**LOWPASS**, **HIPASS**, **BANDPASS**) block each other. Each effect has its own range.

| Effect | What it does |
|---|---|
| **VOLUME** | cuts the tracks, down to silence at -100. It never boosts. |
| **PANNING** | moves the tracks left or right of their own pan. |
| **TUNE** | moves the pitch from -48 to +48 semitones. Sampler instruments only. |
| **SMP POS**, **SMP END** | start the next notes later in the sample and stop them earlier, as a share of the sample (or of the slice the note names). A positive value counts from the start, a negative one from the end: SMP POS +25 starts a quarter in, -25 plays only the last quarter; SMP END +75 stops at three quarters, -25 cuts off the last quarter. A note that sounds is not moved. A looped sample starts inside its first pass and ignores SMP END. Sampler instruments only: granular and wavetable instruments ignore both. |
| **PLAYBACK** | `<<<` plays the next notes backward, from the last frame to the first, and stops there; `>>>` (0) is the normal direction. It works on one-shot samples and on a beat slice (within the slice), and with **SMP POS** and **SMP END** it plays that part backward. A looped sample, a granular or wavetable instrument, the Amiga engine and module instruments ignore it. A note that sounds is not turned round; the next one is. The step effect Reverse (26) with 1 does the same, and a Reverse that is held when you press `Stop` stays on its track until the next fresh `Play`, as the other held step effects do, so pad notes you play after `Stop` are still backward. New Community OS behaviour.   |
| **LOWPASS**, **HIPASS**, **BANDPASS** | the three filters. |
| **VOL LFO**, **PAN LFO**, **TUNE LFO**, **FLT LFO**, **POS LFO** | change how fast the track's LFO runs for the volume (tremolo), the pan (auto-pan), the pitch (vibrato), the filter cutoff and the wavetable window or granular position. The value moves the speed up (+) or down (-) the instrument's speed list, from -23 to +23 for VOL LFO and -28 to +28 for the others. If the instrument already has an LFO there, its shape and amount stay and only the speed moves. If it does not (that target is Off or an envelope), the effect runs an LFO for the track at 1 step plus the value, with the shape and amount stored on the instrument's LFO rows (a new instrument: triangle, 50 %; a stored amount under 5 %, as older projects and imported instruments often have, runs as a triangle at 50 %); at 50 % VOL LFO swings the volume between silence and half, a peak of -6 dB, so raise the amount for more. FLT LFO needs a filter that is on (the instrument's own, or a held LOWPASS, HIPASS or BANDPASS), POS LFO only moves wavetable and granular instruments. The LFOs follow the tempo and keep running when the song is stopped. A step with the Filter LFO FX (35) on the same track gives way to FLT LFO while it is held. Sampler instruments only. |
| **DELAY**, **REVERB** | open or close the track's send, -100 to +100. |
| **STUTTER**, **PLAYMODE**, **PAT LEN** | repeat steps, play forward, back, ping-pong or random, and force a pattern length. |
| **BITDEPTH**, **OVERDRV** | crush or distort the notes. 0 is clean. |

A new slot of the five LFO speeds reads -8, -3 and +3: slow, medium and fast. The way **VOLUME**, **PANNING**, **TUNE**, the five LFO speeds, **DELAY**, **REVERB**, **PLAYBACK**, **BITDEPTH** and **OVERDRV** act, and the four names of **PLAYMODE**, are new in track3r-os. The names **STUTTER** and **PAT LEN** follow the official manual. Not checked against the original firmware: what the effects do there.

### Scenes

A scene is a snapshot of the twelve slots: the effect, the chosen row and the three values of each. It does not keep the tracks that are on. `Shift` + `F1` to `F3` store scene 1 to 3, and `F1` to `F3` recall them. New in track3r-os.

## Try it

1. Press `Perform`. If the strip says **PAGE DJ**, press `Perform` once more. All 12 slots read **OFF** and no track is on.
2. Hold `Shift` and press pad 1 and pad 2. Release `Shift`. **T1** and **T2** read **ON**.

   (Picture: Perform, SLOTS page: T1 and T2 are ON; the track boxes at the bottom show it.)

3. Hold pad 16. The cell reads -30, the first value of **LOWPASS**. Turn the encoder left until it reads -40. **LOWPASS** closes the filter on T1 and T2 while you hold.
4. Let go. The -40 was not stored, so the cell goes back to its own -30 and stays lit.

   (Picture: Perform: after the release the cell of pad 16 is chosen and reads -30, the value it holds.)

5. Press `Rec`. Hold pad 16, turn the encoder left until it reads -40 and let go. Press `Rec` again. The value is stored, so the cell stays lit and reads -40.

   (Picture: Perform: the cell of pad 16 stays lit at -40 after the release, because the row holds a value.)

6. Hold `Shift` and press `F1` (**STORE 1**). The strip says **SCENE 1 STORED**.
7. Press `F8` (**RESET**): every slot goes back to **OFF**. Press `F1` (**SCENE 1**): **LOWPASS** is on at -40 again, and the key row marks **SCENE 1**.

   (Picture: Perform: LOWPASS is back at -40 and SCENE 1 is marked on the key row.)

Not yet checked on the unit.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Perform, SLOTS page: twelve slot columns with their pads, the track boxes at the bottom and the key row from SCENE 1 to RESET.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Status line | **PERFORM**, the transport, **TRACKS** with the number of tracks that are on, and **EDIT** while EDIT is on. |
| Header | The caption **SLOTS** and a hint: whether LATCH keeps the row after you let go. |
| Main area | 12 slot columns: the slot's number, its effect, and four cells, **OFF** and three values. Under them, the boxes **T1** to **T12**. A box shows **ON**, **OFF** or **MUTED**; a track on another pattern shows that pattern (**07**), and one that waits to change shows **>07**, blinking. |
| Info line | In EDIT it names the slot. With no track on it tells you to hold `Shift` and use the top row of pads. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F3` are the scenes (dim while empty). `F4` to `F8` are in the keys table below. |
| Marks under the keys | The scene in force, the rate you hold, LATCH on, and NEXT PAT while it waits. |
| Shift row | **STORE 1**, **STORE 2**, **STORE 3**, then **PICK -**, **PICK +**, **TRK PAT**, **TRK NEXT** and **TRK SONG**. |

## More tasks

### Store a scene

Start on the Perform screen, with slots set the way you like.

1. Hold `Shift`. Press `F1` (**STORE 1**), `F2` or `F3`.
2. Release both keys. The release recalls nothing.

You should see **SCENE 1 STORED** in the strip. A store replaces what the scene held, and Perform has no undo. Holding the plain key for about one second stores too. Scenes are saved with the project.

### Recall a scene

Start on the Perform screen, with a scene stored.

1. Tap `F1` (**SCENE 1**), `F2` or `F3`.

You should see the scene's mark under its key. On an empty scene the strip says **SCENE IS EMPTY: HOLD THE KEY TO STORE**.

### Change the effect of a slot

Start on the Perform screen.

1. Press `Rec`. **EDIT** appears in the strip.
2. Press `Left` or `Right` to pick the slot. The info line names it.
3. Press `Up` or `Down` to change its effect. The list wraps, and the slot's three rows get the new effect's starting values.
4. Press `Rec` to leave EDIT.

Use `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` to swap the slot with its neighbor. `Copy` copies the slot and `Shift` + `Copy` pastes it onto the picked slot.

### Play at half or double time

Start on the Perform screen with the pattern playing.

1. Hold `F4` (**HALF**) for half speed, or `F5` (**DOUBLE**) for double.
2. Hold `F4` and `F5` together for the song's own speed.

The mark under the key shows the rate. When you let go the pattern is back at its own speed.

### Queue the next pattern

Start on the Perform screen with the song playing.

1. Press `F7` (**NEXT PAT**). The pattern after this one in the song order starts when the pattern now playing ends.
2. Press `F7` again while it waits to cancel.

At the last pattern it goes back to the first. If it cannot queue, the strip says **NOT PLAYING**, **SONG IS EMPTY** or **PATTERN IS NOT IN THE SONG**.

### Give single tracks another pattern

Start on the Perform screen with the song playing and the tracks you want to change switched on (hold `Shift` and use the top row of pads).

1. Press `Shift` + `F7` (**TRK NEXT**) to send the tracks that are on to the next pattern of the song order. Or press `Shift` + `F4` or `F5` (**PICK -** or **PICK +**) until the strip shows the pattern you want, then press `Shift` + `F6` (**TRK PAT**).
2. Watch the track boxes. A box that waits shows **>07** and blinks. Each track changes at the end of its own loop, so tracks of different lengths change at different times.
3. Press `Shift` + `F8` (**TRK SONG**) to send the tracks that are on back to the pattern of the song.

A track that is off is not touched and shows **OFF**, not a pattern number. The same press again takes a waiting change back. Queueing the pattern a track already plays pins it at once, so it keeps that pattern when the song goes on. A track that has changed keeps its pattern when the song goes on, until you press **TRK SONG**, stop, or restart the transport (`Play` while it plays, or resume). A random track has no loop end, and a track longer than its pattern is restarted when the pattern ends. Both change at the end of the song's pattern. A pick that is no longer a pattern of the project says **PATTERN IS GONE: PICK ANOTHER** and queues nothing. Nothing is saved in the project. With the song stopped the strip says **NOT PLAYING**; with no track on, **NO TRACK IS ON: HOLD SHIFT + TOP PADS**.

New in track3r-os. Not yet checked on the unit; how the original firmware does it is an open research question.

### Turn every effect off

1. Press `F8` (**RESET**). Every slot goes to **OFF**. The tracks that are on stay on.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **SCENE 1** | **STORE 1** |
| `F2` | **SCENE 2** | **STORE 2** |
| `F3` | **SCENE 3** | **STORE 3** |
| `F4` | **HALF** | **PICK -** |
| `F5` | **DOUBLE** | **PICK +** |
| `F6` | **LATCH** | **TRK PAT** |
| `F7` | **NEXT PAT** | **TRK NEXT** |
| `F8` | **RESET** | **TRK SONG** |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Perform` | opens Perform; again, the DJ page | - |
| `F1` (**SCENE 1**), `F2`, `F3` | a tap recalls the scene; holding for about one second stores it | QA-PRF-003 |
| `Shift` + `F1` (**STORE 1**), `F2`, `F3` | stores the scene at once; the release recalls nothing | QA-PRF-002 |
| `Shift` + `F4` (**PICK -**), `F5` (**PICK +**) | pick the previous or next pattern of the project for **TRK PAT** | QA-PRF-147 |
| `Shift` + `F6` (**TRK PAT**) | queues the picked pattern on the tracks that are on, at each track's loop end; again cancels | QA-PRF-147, QA-PRF-001 |
| `Shift` + `F7` (**TRK NEXT**) | queues the next pattern of the song on the tracks that are on | QA-PRF-147 |
| `Shift` + `F8` (**TRK SONG**) | sends the tracks that are on back to the song's pattern | QA-PRF-147 |
| `F4` (**HALF**), `F5` (**DOUBLE**) | while held, half or double speed; together, the song's own speed | - |
| `F6` (**LATCH**) | switches LATCH | - |
| `F7` (**NEXT PAT**) | queues the next pattern; again cancels | - |
| `F8` (**RESET**) | every slot off; the tracks stay on | - |
| a pad | picks the pad's row on its slot and holds the slot | QA-PRF-025 |
| the encoder | changes the value of the held slots | QA-PRF-025 |
| hold `Shift` | the pads become the TRACKS layer | - |
| `Rec` | EDIT on or off | - |
| `Left`, `Right`, `Up`, `Down` (in EDIT) | pick a slot, change its effect | - |
| `Shift` + `Left`, `Right`; `Copy`, `Shift` + `Copy` (in EDIT) | swap, copy, paste a slot | - |

The DJ page has its own key row: `F1` **BANK -**, `F2` **BANK +**, `F3` **CURVE**, `F4` **FILTER**, `F5` **SCR**, `F6` **LATCH**, `F8` **RESET**, and nothing on `F7`. See [Perform: the DJ page](perform_dj.md).

## Good to know

- A value you turn live ends when you let go. A row with a stored value (stored with `Rec` in EDIT) stays on after you let go while **LATCH** is on, which is the default. It ends when you press another row of the slot or the top-row pad, or `F8` (**RESET**). Not checked against the original firmware: an open research question.
- `F1` to `F3` recall a scene. Hold `F1` to `F3` for one second to store the current settings in it, or press `Shift` + `F1` to `F3` to store at once. `F4` is **HALF** time, `F5` is **DOUBLE** time, `F6` is **LATCH**, `F7` is **NEXT PAT** and `F8` is **RESET**. Choose the tracks with `Shift` and the top row of pads. The info line says so when no track is on.
- While `Shift` is held, `F4` to `F8` are the per-track pattern keys (see above). They do not run the plain key under them.
- **TUNE** adds to the instrument's tune and fine tune, and a sounding note follows at once. Amiga-engine instruments and modules do not follow it.
- An effect that is on stays on through `Play`, `Stop`, the Mixer and Song, and an export is the same with and without it. When a held **VOLUME** -100 or a closed send ends, the sound is back within a few milliseconds, with no click.
- **PLAYMODE** **PING** bounces over the track: 0 1 2 3 2 1 0 on four steps, so the end steps play once per pass. A different pattern, a pattern switch or a jump starts it again, and so does resuming after a pause. Not yet checked on the unit.
- A pad you hold while you go to the Mixer (`Master`) or Song is let go when you lift it there, so its value does not stay on.
- A project that uses **BITDEPTH** or **OVERDRV** shows those two slots empty in an older build.
- Not yet checked on the unit. Not checked against the original firmware, except where a line above says otherwise.

> **Careful**: Leaving Perform for any screen except the Mixer (`Master`) or Song switches every track off, so every effect ends, with no message. The chosen rows stay.

> **Tip**: `F8` is **RESET** here, not undo.

## See also

- [Perform: the DJ page](perform_dj.md): crossfade two groups of tracks, filter, kill bands, scratch.
- [Mixer](mixer.md): levels and sends that the effects add to.
- [The panel](panel.md): where the keys are on the unit, and the Shift layer of the pads.

# Perform: the DJ page

Status: draft

The DJ page turns the pattern that plays into something you mix by hand. You put some tracks in group A and some in group B, and a crossfader fades between the two groups, with a filter, band kills, stutters, a scratch and transitions to the next pattern. The page is new in track3r-os, and everything on it is live: nothing is written into the song or the project.

## What it is for

Use the DJ page to play a set from one pattern after another: drums on A and a melody on B, a filter sweep into the next pattern, a stutter at the end of a bar. Press `Perform` to open [Perform](perform.md); it opens on the page you left it on, so the strip may already say **PAGE DJ**. If it shows the slots, press `Perform` again. Once more goes back to the slots.

## How it works

Everything on this page is **live** and ends when you leave it. Only the groups stay, until you switch the unit off. Nothing of the DJ page is saved in the project, and an export never carries it. New in track3r-os. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Groups: who gets faded

A group is a set of tracks that the crossfader moves together. `Shift` + a pad of the top row sets the group of that pad's track: **THRU**, **A**, **B**, then **THRU** again. A track that is **THRU** is never touched. The screen names the groups, and the pad lights are off, dim and bright for THRU, A and B. Tracks 1 to 12 can be grouped.

Example: drums (tracks 1 and 2) in A, the lead (track 5) in B. A bass on THRU plays through every fade.

### The crossfader and the curve

The crossfader is the bar at the bottom. The encoder moves it, and one turn is the whole way from **A** to **B**. With `Shift` held the steps are small. The bottom row of pads jumps it: pad 37 is all A, pads 38 to 41 are 10 to 40 %, pads 42 and 43 are both the centre, pads 44 to 47 are 60 to 90 %, and pad 48 is all B. The jump takes 20 milliseconds, which the encoder cannot do. The fader only cuts: it never makes a track louder, and it cuts the track's delay and reverb with it.

`F3` (**CURVE**) picks how it cuts. **SMOOTH** fades with equal power, so both groups are 3 dB down at the centre. **CUT** keeps a group at full level until the last step, like a scratch fader.

### Filter and kills: the whole mix

Hold `F4` (**FILTER**) and turn the encoder. Left closes a low-pass filter over the whole mix, right closes a high-pass filter, and the middle is off. When you let go the filter springs back. A tap on `F4` alone moves nothing and the strip says **FILTER: HOLD, TURN THE ENCODER**. Pad 28, **FILT**, does the same.

The pads **KILL LOW**, **MID** and **HI** (pads 25 to 27) cut one band while you hold them: below about 180 Hz, between 180 Hz and 2.8 kHz, above 2.8 kHz. The rest of the mix stays.

**LATCH** (`F6`) changes the rule for all the holds: a filter stays where you left it, and a kill, **ECHO** or **CUT** pad stays on after a tap until you tap it again. A **REP** pad stays on until you tap another **REP** pad of its group. `F8` (**RESET**) ends them and the filter but keeps **LATCH**.

### Pad effects: REP, ECHO and CUT

Row 2 acts on one group at a time. The six pads on the left are group **A** and the six on the right are group **B**, mirrored, so each hand has the same order from the outside in: **REP 1/4**, **REP 1/8**, **REP 1/16**, **REP 1/32**, **ECHO**, **CUT**. Hold a pad to use it. **REP** repeats the last note of each track of the group, as a stutter. It repeats notes, not audio. With two **REP** pads down in one group, the later one decides. **ECHO** opens the group's delay send, and one beat later cuts the group, so only the echoes ring out. **CUT** silences the group. ECHO needs the master delay level up, or the strip says **DELAY LEVEL IS 0**.

### Pattern row, tempo and transitions

The top row of pads is the pattern row: the twelve patterns of a bank, with **NOW** and **NEXT** on the screen. A tap queues a pattern for the end of the one that plays, so no step is cut. `Left` or `Right` held nudges the tempo 4 % slower or faster and gives it back exactly at the release.

A transition is an effect that ends on the switch to the next pattern. **TRANS HP** and **TRANS LP** (pads 29 and 30) close a filter slowly over the time left to the queued pattern, and the filter snaps open when it starts. **TRANS ECHO** (pad 31) sends the whole mix into the delay in the last beat. A sweep always lasts at least one bar.

### Scratch and tape stop

`F5` (**SCR**) puts your hand on the record. The encoder becomes the platter, the mix goes quiet like a held record, and a full turn is 1.8 seconds of sound, and the encoder no longer moves the crossfader. The song keeps playing underneath, so when you tap `F5` again the mix is live at the place it has reached. Backwards it stops at the oldest sound kept, up to 4 seconds. Hold **TAPE STOP** (pad 32; with **SCR** on the strip says **SCRATCH IS ON**) and the whole mix slows to a stop over one beat; while you hold it, turn the encoder to make the stop shorter or longer, from 1/8 beat up to 4 beats (the screen shows the length, and the stop carries on from the speed it has; the next hold starts with the length you left). Let go and it is live again. Not yet checked on the unit: the platter, the backspin and the detents.

### What leaving the page ends

Pressing `Perform`, or any other screen button, ends every effect of this page at once with no click: the fader goes to the centre, **CURVE** to **SMOOTH**, **LATCH** off, and the filter, kills, pad effects, nudge, transition and scratch end. A queued pattern stays queued.

## Try it

1. Press `Perform`. If the strip does not say **PAGE DJ**, press `Perform` again. The strip says **PAGE DJ**, the twelve track boxes read **THRU**, and the fader is in the middle.
2. Hold `Shift` and tap pads 1 and 2 once, and pads 5 and 6 twice. Release `Shift`. Tracks 1 and 2 are group **A**, tracks 5 and 6 are group **B**.
3. Tap pad 48, the last pad of the bottom row. The fader jumps to the end of B, and the gains read `A 0%  B 100%`: group A is silent.

   (Picture: Perform, DJ page: the fader is at the B end, so the gains read A 0% and B 100%.)

4. Press `F8` (**RESET**). The fader goes back to the middle, and the groups stay.
5. Hold `F4` (**FILTER**) and turn the encoder right three clicks. The filter row reads **FILTER HP 30**.

   (Picture: Perform, DJ page: the filter row reads FILTER HP 30 with the knob right of the middle, and F4 is marked.)

6. Let go of `F4`. The filter springs back and the row reads **FILTER OFF**.
7. Hold pad 15 and pad 24. A line under the gains reads `A  REP 1/16` and `B  REP 1/4`. Let go and both end.

   (Picture: Perform, DJ page: while two REP pads are held, the line under the gains names A REP 1/16 and B REP 1/4.)

With the pattern playing, you hear the filter close and open, and the stutters on tracks 1 and 2 and on tracks 5 and 6. Not yet checked on the unit.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Perform, DJ page at rest: twelve THRU track boxes, the pattern row, the gains, the filter and kill rows and the crossfader.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Status line | **PERFORM**, the transport, **PAGE DJ**, the curve (**SMOOTH** or **CUT**) and the tempo. |
| Track boxes | **T1** to **T12** with their group: **THRU**, **A** or **B**. |
| Pattern row | **NOW**, **NEXT** and **BANK**, and the twelve pattern numbers of the bank. |
| Group lines | The tracks of each group, the gains of A and B, and a line for the pad effects in force. |
| Filter and kill rows | **FILTER** with its value and a bar from **LP** to **HP**; **KILL** with **LOW**, **MID** and **HI**. |
| Tape stop line | While **TAPE STOP** is held, its length above the crossfader (`TAPE STOP 1 BEAT`). |
| Crossfader | The bar from **A** to **B** with its knob. |
| Key row | **BANK -**, **BANK +**, **CURVE**, **FILTER**, **SCR**, **LATCH**, blank, **RESET**. The Shift row is blank.  |

## More tasks

### Fade between two groups with a hard edge

Start on the DJ page, with tracks in A and B.

1. Press `F3` (**CURVE**). The chip in the strip reads **CUT**.
2. Turn the encoder from A to B. A group stays at full level until the last step of the fader.

Press `F3` again for **SMOOTH**.

### Cut a band and keep it

Start on the DJ page.

1. Press `F6` (**LATCH**). The strip says **LATCH ON: FILTER AND PAD EFFECTS STAY**.
2. Tap pad 26 (**KILL MID**). The **KILL** row keeps **MID** lit and reads **LATCHED**.
3. Tap pad 26 again to bring the band back.

Both hands are free for the fader and the filter. `F8` (**RESET**) ends every kill and filter and keeps **LATCH**.

### Queue a pattern from another bank

Start on the DJ page with the song playing.

1. Press `F2` (**BANK +**). The pattern row moves up one bank. If the pattern that plays is in bank 1, the screen reads **BANK 2** and shows patterns 13 to 24.
2. Tap a pad of the top row. The pad blinks and **NEXT** names the pattern.
3. Tap the blinking pad again to cancel.

Stopped, a tap picks the pattern to edit, as the pads on Pattern do.

### Nudge the tempo

Start on the DJ page with the pattern playing.

1. Hold `Right`. The strip shows **NUDGE +4%** and the new tempo. Stopped, it says **NUDGE NEEDS PLAY**.
2. Let go. The tempo is exactly what it was.

`Shift` + `Left` or `Right` changes the song's tempo by 0.1 BPM and keeps it in the project, between 40 and 800 BPM.  With the clock set to MIDI slave, both leave the tempo alone and the strip says **MIDI SLAVE: THE CLOCK SETS THE TEMPO**.

### Leave with a transition

Start on the DJ page, playing.

1. Tap a pad of the top row to queue the next pattern, or leave it. With nothing queued, the song's next slot is queued for you, so you need a song that holds the pattern that plays. Without one the strip says **SONG IS EMPTY** or **PATTERN IS NOT IN THE SONG**, and nothing starts.
2. Tap pad 29 (**TRANS HP**) or pad 30 (**TRANS LP**). The **NEXT** line reads `TRANS HP 8 %` and counts up. Stopped or in the count-in, the strip says **TRANS NEEDS PLAY** or **TRANS NEEDS THE COUNT-IN OVER**.
3. Wait. When the pattern ends the new one starts and the filter opens at once.

Tap the same pad again to cancel. The queued pattern stays queued. If less than a bar is left, the pattern plays once more first.

### Scratch and spin back

Start on the DJ page, playing, with no loop recording.

1. Tap `F5` (**SCR**). The strip says **SCR ON: THE ENCODER IS THE PLATTER**.
2. Turn the encoder. The mix moves with it, and a turn back plays the mix backwards. The platter has a little weight, about a fortieth of a second: a very slow turn is a smooth glide, and a stop or a start is a short curve, never a click or a step. A quick forth-and-back scratch returns to the same place, within about one click, and a turn back after a hard flick follows the new direction at once.
3. To backspin, flick the platter fast backwards and tap `F5` while it still spins. The record brakes in about half a second and the mix is live. A slow turn, or a hand held still, lets go at once.

If the looper is recording, the strip says **NO ROOM: LOOPER IS RECORDING**; without free sample memory it says **NO ROOM FOR THE SCRATCH**.   Until the scratch ends, opening a project says **END THE SCRATCH FIRST**.

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` (**BANK -**), `F2` (**BANK +**) | the pattern row moves one bank of twelve | QA-PRF-120 |
| `F3` (**CURVE**) | **SMOOTH** or **CUT** | QA-PRF-103 |
| hold `F4` (**FILTER**) + the encoder | the filter; it springs back at the release | QA-PRF-109 |
| `F5` (**SCR**) | the encoder becomes the platter | QA-PRF-133 |
| hold **TAPE STOP** (pad 32) + the encoder | the length of the stop, 1/8 to 4 beats | QA-PRF-144 |
| `F6` (**LATCH**) | filter, kills and pad effects stay | QA-PRF-111 |
| `F8` (**RESET**) | fader to the centre, filter, kills, pad effects and transition off | QA-PRF-105 |
| the encoder; `Shift` + the encoder | the crossfader; small steps | QA-PRF-101 |
| `Shift` + a top-row pad | sets the group of that track | QA-PRF-104 |
| row 1 pad | queues that pattern | QA-PRF-119 |
| row 2 pads | **REP**, **ECHO**, **CUT** of group A and B | QA-PRF-123 |
| row 3 pads 25 to 32 | **KILL LOW**, **MID**, **HI**, **FILT**, **TRANS HP**, **TRANS LP**, **TRANS ECHO**, **TAPE STOP** | QA-PRF-115 |
| row 4 pad | jumps the fader, pad 37 all A, 42 and 43 the centre, pad 48 all B | QA-PRF-102 |
| hold `Left` or `Right`; `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` | nudge the tempo; change it by 0.1 BPM | QA-PRF-121 |

## Good to know

- A kill takes the middle of its band down by 40 dB or more and falls away at 24 dB an octave. At the very edge it is only 6 dB down, so the band does not end like a wall.
- The effects of row 2 are the Perform effects **STUTTER**, **DELAY** and **VOLUME**, put above the slots while the page is in view. A slot's own effect comes back when the pad ends.
- `Shift` + `F1` to `F8` do nothing here and show no label.
- Pads 33 to 36 of row 3 do nothing. A held pad that you let go of after the page changed does no harm.
- New in track3r-os. Not yet checked on the unit: the filter, the kills, the transitions, the scratch and tape stop. Not checked against the original firmware.

## See also

- [Perform](perform.md): the slots, the scenes and the Shift layer of the pads.
- [Record](record.md): the looper, which the scratch cannot run beside.
- [Mixer](mixer.md): the delay and reverb levels that ECHO uses.

# Sample load

Status: draft

Sample load takes a sound file from the card into an instrument slot. It reads WAV, AIFF and 8SVX files by what is inside them, not by their name, and it can load one channel of a stereo file. The official manual accepts plain WAV only and brings every file to 44.1 kHz, 16-bit, one channel. Here a file keeps its own rate.  Not checked against the original firmware: the keys.

## What it is for

Use Sample load to put a sound file from the card into an instrument. Browse the folders, move the cursor to a file, and press `F1` (**LOAD**). You reach the screen from a free slot on the Instrument screen: press `F1` (**SAMPLE**). When the load is done, the screen returns you to the instrument.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Sample load: two folders first, then AIFF, 8SVX, WAV and WT files together in one list.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header | **NAME** at the left, then **TARGET INSTRUMENT** and the number of the instrument that gets the file. At the right, **WAV**. |
| Main area | The folders and files of the card, folders first. The cursor marks one row. |
| Info line | How many entries the folder has, and the keys that work in the list, starting with **pad: target**. |
| Strip | Messages, for example **IMPORT <NAME> FAILED**. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F8`, with the labels in the table under "Keys on this screen". |
| Shift row | The jumps through the list and **INST -** / **INST +**, drawn while `Shift` is held. |

> **Try this**:
> 1. Start on Sample load. Press `F3` (**ENTER**) on the `/AIFF` folder, then put the cursor on `afsp_16bit_stereo.aif`.
> 2. Press `F1` (**LOAD**).
> 3. The instrument takes its name from the file.

## More tasks

### Choose the instrument that gets the file

The header always says which instrument `F1` loads into: **TARGET INSTRUMENT 07**, for example. The card on the right shows what that slot holds now: its name, **MODULE** and a name for a module instrument, **MIDI** and a name for a MIDI instrument, or **-- empty --** for a free slot. A WAV cannot go into a module slot or a MIDI slot: the strip says **SLOT IS MIDI: INSTRUMENT, SHIFT+F4 DELETE**, and the instrument stays. Any other slot, 49 to 64 too, can take the file.

The card also shows the sample memory: a bar of how much of it is used, and under it **ARENA** with the used and free figures in KB, for example **3284 KB USED  4908 KB FREE** (rounded down; Config shows the same free figure). The line turns the accent colour when less than 4 KB is free. This is new in the Community OS.

Loading over an instrument that already has a sample can give its memory back: when the new sample is not longer than the room the old one had, a project's own sample included, then once playback has stopped and the pads are let go the new sample moves into the old one's room and **USED** goes back. The room the old sample does not need stays with that instrument; it is not given to the others until you load a project again. This does not happen when the new sample is longer than about 3 seconds (131,072 frames), when the instrument is a beat-sliced one, or while something still holds the old sample: you copied the instrument, pasted it, or loaded it from an instrument file a moment ago, so that Undo can bring the old sample back. In those cases the old sample stays and the figure stays up. Saving the project and opening it again frees everything that is no longer used. This is new in the Community OS.

1. Press a pad to make its instrument the target. The pad also plays that instrument for as long as you hold it, so you hear what the slot holds now; a file you loaded a moment ago is heard after the hand-over (the card says **SOUNDS WHEN STOPPED**). Or hold `Shift` and press `F8` (**INST +**) for the next instrument, `F7` (**INST -**) for the one before. After 64 it goes round to 1.
2. Press `F1` (**LOAD**).

A question about the old target (**REPLACE 03 KICK: F1 AGAIN**) goes away when you change the target.

### Hear a file before you load it

Start on Sample load, with the cursor on a `.wav` file.

1. Hold `F5` (**PLAY**). The file starts at once and plays for as long as you hold the key.
2. With `F5` still held, press `Up` or `Down`. The sound of the first file ends and the file now under the cursor starts. On a folder it stays quiet until the cursor reaches a `.wav` again.
3. Let go of `F5` to stop.

A long file starts before it is all read from the card. If the card fails in the middle of the file, the strip says **PREVIEW FAILED** and the part that was read goes on playing.

New Community OS behaviour. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Load a sample file

Start on Sample load. The cursor must be on the file, not on a folder.

1. Move the cursor onto the file with `Up` and `Down`.
2. Press `F1` (**LOAD**).

If the instrument in view already holds something, nothing is replaced yet. The strip asks, for example **REPLACE 03 KICK: F1 AGAIN**, and `F1` reads **REPLACE?**. Press `F1` again within four seconds to load. A free instrument loads at once, with no question. A module instrument (the TB-303, for example) is never replaced: the strip says **SLOT HAS A MODULE: INSTRUMENT, SHIFT+F4 DELETE**. Delete it on the Instrument screen first. A load that was asked for cannot be undone, but it leaves the undo history of your pattern and song as it was. Only the undo of that instrument's own parameter edits ends, and the strip says so.

You should see the instrument named after the file. A one-shot file plays once. A file that says it loops plays in a loop, forward or ping-pong. The file plays at the pitch of the rate it was recorded at.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Open a folder

Start on Sample load, with the cursor on a folder.

1. Press `F3` (**ENTER**). The list shows what is in the folder.
2. Press `F2` (**UP**) to go back to the folder above. When the list is read, the cursor stands on the folder you just left (new Community OS behaviour). At the top of the card, the strip says **ALREADY AT THE TOP**.
3. Press `F6` (**RESCAN**) to read the folder again, for example after you changed the card on a computer. When the list is read, the strip says how many items it holds, for example **READ AGAIN: 12 ITEMS**.

On a file, `F3` says **NOT A FOLDER**. `F1` on a folder says **A FOLDER: PRESS ENTER**.

If you visit the File screen and come back, Sample load is in the same folder and the cursor is on the same file again once the list is read (new Community OS behaviour).

### Add a file to a free instrument

Start on Sample load, with the cursor on a file.

1. Press `F4` (**ADD**). The file goes to the first free instrument slot of the 64, not to the one in view.

If every slot is used, the strip says **NO FREE INSTRUMENT**. With files marked, `F4` loads the marked files instead (next section).

### Load several files in one go

Start on Sample load, in a folder with the files you want. New: the official firmware loads one file at a time here, or marks files with `Shift` and the arrows; this firmware marks with `Shift` + `Right`, because `Shift` + `Up` and `Down` are the page keys.

1. Put the cursor on the first file and press `Shift` + `Right`. A solid square marks the file and the cursor steps down, so pressing it again marks the next file. The info line counts them (**3 marked**) and `F1` and `F4` read **LOAD 3** and **ADD 3**.
2. To take a mark back, put the cursor on the file and press `Shift` + `Right` again. `Shift` + `Left` clears every mark.
3. Choose the target instrument if you want to start somewhere else (a pad, or `Shift` + `F7` and `F8`).
4. Press `F1` to load from the target on, or `F4` to load from the first free instrument.

The marked files load one after the other, in the order of the list, each into the next free instrument. An instrument that is already there is skipped, never replaced, and the search stops at instrument 64: it does not go round to 1. When it is done the strip says **LOADED 3 OF 3**. A second `F1` while it runs says **A MULTI-LOAD IS RUNNING**.

If the free instruments run out, the strip says how many came in and why the rest did not, for example **LOADED 3 OF 5: NO FREE INSTRUMENT**. The two files left over stay marked. A file that cannot be read is skipped and counted (**LOADED 2 OF 3: 1 FAILED**), and the others still load.

The marks go when the folder changes, when you press `F6` (**RESCAN**) and when you leave the screen. While the folder is still being read, the strip says **LIST STILL READING** and nothing is marked: wait for the list to finish first.

### Find a file in a long folder

Start on Sample load, in a folder with more files than fit on one screen. A page is 16 rows.

1. Press `Shift` + `Down` to move down one page. Press `Shift` + `Up` to move up one page.
2. Press `Shift` + `F3` (**2/4**) to go to the middle of the list. `Shift` + `F1` goes to the start (**0/4**), `Shift` + `F2` to **1/4**, and `Shift` + `F4` to **3/4**.
3. Press `Shift` + `F5` (**END**) to go to the last entry.

You should see the cursor move. These keys do not load a sample.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Load one channel of a stereo file

Start on Sample load. Put the cursor on a stereo file. Its name shows **ST** at the right. A mono file does not.

1. Press `F8` (**CH MIX**). Each press moves on: **CH LEFT**, then **CH RIGHT**, then **CH MIX**.
2. Press `F1` (**LOAD**). The instrument gets only the channel the key shows.
3. Press `F1` on another stereo file. The key still shows the same choice.

You should see the strip say what the file will load: **STEREO FILE LOADS: LEFT**, **STEREO FILE LOADS: RIGHT** or **STEREO FILE LOADS: MIX (L+R)/2**. **CH MIX** loads the mix of both channels, (left + right) / 2. **CH LEFT** and **CH RIGHT** load one channel alone, with no mixing.

The choice is not saved with the project. It lasts until the unit is switched off.

(Picture: Sample load, stereo file: the cursor is on a file tagged ST, and F8 reads CH MIX. Press it to change the channel.)

### Play a stereo file in stereo

An instrument holds one channel, so a stereo file cannot play in stereo from one instrument. You can get the stereo image with two instruments and two tracks. Stereo instruments are planned, not built yet.

Start on Sample load. Put the cursor on a stereo file.

1. Press `F8` until it reads **CH LEFT**. Press `F1` (**LOAD**) to load the file into one instrument.
2. Pick a second free instrument as the target (see above). Press `F8` until it reads **CH RIGHT**, then press `F1` to load the same file.
3. Press `Pattern`. Write the notes on one track with the first instrument. Select the steps and press `Copy`, then move to another track and press `Shift` + `Copy` to paste them. Set the **Instr** column of the second track to the second instrument.
4. Press `Master`, then `F1` (**MIXER**). Set the **PAN** of the first track to 0 and the **PAN** of the second to 100 (see [Mixer](mixer.md)). Leave the pan of both instruments at the centre: the instrument's pan moves the track's, so an instrument off the centre is not hard left or right.
5. Press `Play`.

You should hear the left channel from the left output and the right channel from the right output. Each note uses two voices, because each track plays one instrument. A voice is one playing sound; the unit has a fixed number of them (see the [glossary](glossary.md)). Not yet checked on the unit.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **LOAD** | **0/4** |
| `F2` | **UP** | **1/4** |
| `F3` | **ENTER** | **2/4** |
| `F4` | **ADD** | **3/4** |
| `F5` | **PLAY** | **END** |
| `F6` | **RESCAN** | - |
| `F7` | **WT AUTO** | **INST -** |
| `F8` | **CH MIX** | **INST +** |

`F7` and `F8` show a setting, so their labels in the table are the first of several. `F7` shows the wavetable mode: **WT AUTO**, **WT LEN**, **WT 256**, **WT 512**, **WT 1024**, **WT 2048** or **WT OFF**. `F8` shows **CH MIX**, **CH LEFT** or **CH RIGHT** while the cursor is on a stereo file, **CH MONO** on a mono file (the key then says **ONLY FOR A STEREO FILE**), and `--` when there is no file. When the screen lists instrument files (`.pti`), `F4`, `F5`, `F7` and `F8` show `--`.

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Up`, `Down` | Move the cursor one row. | QA-SLD-016 |
| `Shift` + `Up`, `Shift` + `Down` | Move the cursor one page (16 rows). It stops at the first and last entry. | QA-SLD-016 |
| `F1` (**LOAD**) | Load the file under the cursor into the instrument. | QA-SLD-003, QA-SLD-012, QA-SLD-013 |
| `F2` (**UP**), `F3` (**ENTER**) | Go up one folder, or open the folder under the cursor. | QA-SLD-026 |
| `F4` (**ADD**) | Load the file into the first free instrument. | none yet |
| `F6` (**RESCAN**) | Read the folder again. The strip says **READ AGAIN: n ITEMS** when it is done. | QA-SLD-025 |
| `F7` (**WT AUTO**) | Choose how the next WAV is read as a wavetable: **AUTO** (a Serum-style table by its windows), by length, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048 frames, or **OFF**. The strip names the choice. | QA-SLD-018 |
| `F5` (**PLAY**) | Audition the file under the cursor, without loading it: it starts at once and plays while you hold the key. Move the cursor with the key held to hear the next file. | QA-SLD-006, QA-SLD-023 |
| `F8` (**CH MIX**) | Choose the channel of a stereo file: **CH MIX**, **CH LEFT**, **CH RIGHT**. On a mono file the key shows `--`. | QA-SLD-011, QA-SLD-013 |
| `Shift` + `F1` (**0/4**) | Jump the cursor to the start of the list. | QA-SLD-015 |
| `Shift` + `F2` (**1/4**), `F3` (**2/4**), `F4` (**3/4**) | Jump the cursor to that quarter of the list. | QA-SLD-015 |
| `Shift` + `F5` (**END**) | Jump the cursor to the last entry. | QA-SLD-001, QA-SLD-015 |
| `Shift` + `F7` (**INST -**), `Shift` + `F8` (**INST +**) | Step the target instrument down or up over 1 to 64. After 64 it goes round to 1, and before 1 to 64. | QA-SLD-021 |
| `Shift` + `F6` | Does nothing. The key shows `-`. | QA-SLD-001 |
| `Shift` + `Right` | Mark the file under the cursor (or take its mark back) and step down one row. `F1` and `F4` then load the marked files. | QA-SLD-032, QA-SLD-033, QA-SLD-034 |
| `Shift` + `Left` | Clear every mark. | QA-SLD-032 |

## Good to know

- `Up` and `Down` move the cursor one row, and the encoder does too; turn it quickly and it moves 4 rows a detent, then 8 (new Community OS behaviour, the same in the `File` lists; the numbers are being tuned). `Shift` + the encoder pages a detent at a time. `Left` and `Right` jump by the first letter of the name.
- A file name longer than 32 characters is cut in the middle: the first 25 characters, a **~**, then the last 6, so the end of the name (for example `take2.wav`) stays readable. A stereo file keeps three cells for **ST**, so its name is cut to 29. The card keeps the full name, and Sample load finds the file by it. This is new in the Community OS.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- Sample load does not delete. To clear a slot, go to the Instrument screen and press `Shift` + `F4` (**DELETE**). It asks nothing, and one `F8` (**UNDO**) brings the instrument back. The pattern steps stay.
- To copy an instrument, press `Shift` + `F2` (**COPY**) on the Instrument screen, then `Shift` + `F3` (**PASTE**) on a free slot. The copy shares its audio with the source and keeps playing when the source is deleted.
- The file's header decides its format, not its name. An AIFF named `.wav` loads as an AIFF.
- Audition (`F5`) on a file that is not `.wav` says **NO PREVIEW OF THIS TYPE: LOAD IT**.
- A file that is neither format says **IMPORT <NAME> FAILED** and changes nothing.
- A damaged file says **IMPORT <NAME> FAILED: DAMAGED FILE**.
- An AIFF with its sound data before its format header says **AIFF: SSND BEFORE COMM NOT SUPPORTED**. This is a known limit. It is not a damaged file.
- AIFF files with NONE or sowt compression load. Another compression says **IMPORT <NAME> FAILED**.
- An 8SVX file takes the name stored in the file. A repeat part loops forward.
- AIFF and 8SVX loading is **Not yet checked on the unit**.
- A sample at a rate other than 44,100 Hz plays at the pitch of its own rate. Earlier builds played it too high. A sample loaded before this change may sound lower now. Retune its **TUNE** once.
- A sample saved at another rate reloads at that rate and keeps its pitch.

## See also

- [Sample edit](sample_edit.md): change a loaded sample with normalise, DC removal and the Amiga conversion.
- [Instrument](instrument.md): the instrument you load into, its play modes and its name.

# Sample edit

Status: draft

Sample edit changes the sample itself: crop, normalize, reverse, the fades and the volume. Each process is one undo step. It differs from the original firmware's editor in three small ways. **NORM** always takes the loudest point to full scale, and has no level setting. **AMP** sets the volume as a percentage, from 10 to 800. A pad picks the instrument (so does `Shift` + `F5`, the next one, and holding `Instrument` opens the list of sample instruments), and `F7` (**PREVIEW**) plays it. New in track3r-os, on the Shift row: the Amiga conversion with its 8-bit option (`Shift` + `F1`, `F2` and `F3`), DC removal (`Shift` + `F4`), **NEXT INS** (`Shift` + `F5`) and **SAVE WAV** (`Shift` + `F6`), and a second page, **FX**, with a **FILTER** and a **COMPRESSOR** (press `Sample Edit` again).

There is no preview before an edit is applied: an edit applies at once. Each edit is one undo step, and three steps are kept. To compare, apply the edit, hold `F7` (**PREVIEW**) to listen, and take the edit back with `F8` (**UNDO**).

## What it is for

Use Sample edit to change a loaded sample: crop, normalize, reverse, fade, change its volume, remove its DC offset, filter it, compress it or convert it to an Amiga rate. Open it with the `Sample Edit` button. A process acts on the selection, or on all of the sample when nothing is selected. `F8` takes it back, up to three steps.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Sample edit: a sample on screen and the key row from CROP to UNDO.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header | **SELECTION**, and at the right the instrument you are editing (**INSTRUMENT 05 BREAK_A**) with the reminder `pad / Shift+F5: change`. |
| Main area | The sample, the selection, the **AMP** percentage, the length selected, the undo and redo steps left and how much sample memory is free (for example **4908 KB FREE**, rounded down: the same sample memory as the Sample load card and Config show; new in the Community OS). An effect needs a work buffer as big as the sample. When no buffer set aside earlier is free and big enough, the effect sets a new one aside (at most four), and the figure drops by that much, also when you cancel the effect; a cancelled effect's buffer is used again by the next effect. The buffers are given back when a project loads, on New project with **ALL** and at power-on; New project with **KEEP INSTRUMENTS** keeps them.  |
| Info line | The selection in frames, or "no selection". |
| Strip | Messages, for example **EDIT DC REMOVE** or **NOTHING TO NORMALISE**. |
| Key row and Shift row | See "Keys on this screen". |

## More tasks

### Select a part

Start on Sample edit. With no selection, a process acts on all of the sample.

1. Turn the encoder. A selection appears and the encoder moves its start edge.
2. Press `Right` for the end edge, `Left` for the start, and turn the encoder. `Shift` + the encoder moves 16 times as far. `Up` and `Down` zoom.

You should see the selection in frames on the info line. `Delete` clears it.

### Normalize and take it back

1. Press `F2` (**NORM**). The loudest point of the range goes to full scale.
2. Press `F8` (**UNDO**) to get the sample back exactly. `Shift` + `F8` (**REDO**) does it again.

If the sample is already at full scale or silent, the strip says **NOTHING TO NORMALISE**.

### Crop, reverse, fade or change the volume

1. Select the part. Press `F1` (**CROP**) to keep it.  Press `F3` (**REVERSE**), `F4` (**FADE IN**) or `F5` (**FADE OUT**).  The strip says, for example, **EDIT REVERSE DONE**.
2. Press `F6` (**AMP**) to multiply the range by the **AMP** percentage, which starts at 200 %. Loud peaks are clipped, not wrapped.
3. `Shift` + `Up` or `Down` sets **AMP**, from 10 to 800 in steps of 10. It only sets the factor for the next `F6`: the sample is not touched.
4. Hold `F7` (**PREVIEW**) to hear it. `Shift` + `F7` (**PRV EDGE**) plays from the edge.

**CROP** needs a selection that is smaller than the sample, or it refuses and makes no step. A crop moves the instrument's points and slices to the new length. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Remove the DC offset

A DC offset means the sample sits above or below its centre line. Press `Shift` + `F4` (**DC REM**).  The strip says **EDIT DC REMOVE** and **DONE**. A centred range says **NO DC OFFSET TO REMOVE**, and a full-scale one **NO ROOM: SAMPLE AT FULL SCALE** or **DC PARTLY REMOVED: FULL SCALE LIMIT**.

### Filter or compress

New in track3r-os (the original firmware's editor has neither). Both act on the selection, or on all of the sample when nothing is selected, run as a job with a progress bar in the strip, and are one undo step each. A result that is too loud is clipped at the top, like **AMP**.

1. Make the selection on the edit page, then press `Sample Edit` again. This is the **FX** page.
2. Press `Up` or `Down` to pick a row and turn the encoder to change its value. `Shift` + the encoder changes it in bigger steps.
3. For the **FILTER**, set **TYPE** (low pass, high pass or band pass), **CUTOFF** in Hz and **RESONANCE** (the Q: 0.5 to 15). Press `F1` (**FILTER**). A low pass takes away what is above the cutoff, a high pass what is below.
4. For the **COMPRESSOR**, set **THRESHOLD** (dB), **RATIO**, **ATTACK** and **RELEASE** in ms, **MAKEUP** (**AUTO**, or 0 to 24 dB) and **DETECTOR** (**PEAK** or **RMS**). Press `F2` (**COMPRESS**). Above the threshold the level comes down by the ratio. **AUTO** makeup brings a full-scale peak back to full scale.
5. Press `F8` (**UNDO**) to take it back. Press `Sample Edit` again to return to the edit page.

A long process, such as the compressor on a sample of tens of seconds, can be stopped: while the strip shows its progress the key row reads **CANCEL** on `F8`. Press it and the strip says **EDIT COMPRESSOR CANCELLED**. The sample stays exactly as it was and nothing is added to the undo steps. When the process has ended, `F8` is **UNDO** again.

The filter starts from silence at the first frame of the selection, so a selection that starts in the middle of a loud sound may click at its start. The exception is a looping instrument whose processed range starts at its loop start (in practice a loop that starts at the first frame, with the whole sample or a selection from 0): the filter and the compressor first run over the end of the loop, so the loop wraps without a click. Edge handles do not snap to the loop markers. If the loop starts in the middle of the sample (a sustain loop) and you process the whole sample, a click can remain at the wrap; process from the loop start instead.  A long sample takes a while, the compressor longer than the filter (the time is not yet measured on the unit). Both are not yet checked on the unit: listen to the result before you keep it. The values you set stay until you switch the unit off.

### Convert to an Amiga rate

1. Press `Shift` + `F1` (**AMG 8K**) for 8,287 Hz, or `Shift` + `F2` (**AMG 16K**) for 16,574 Hz.  All of the sample is converted in one step, and the strip says **EDIT AMIGA 8287 DONE**.
2. `Shift` + `F3` (**Q8**) switches the 8-bit option on and off for the next conversion. The line under the sample and the strip say **8-BIT ON** or **OFF**.

The sample still plays at its original pitch.  Not yet checked on the unit.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Sample edit | FX page | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **CROP** | **FILTER** | **AMG 8K** |
| `F2` | **NORM** | **COMPRESS** | **AMG 16K** |
| `F3` | **REVERSE** | - | **Q8** |
| `F4` | **FADE IN** | - | **DC REM** |
| `F5` | **FADE OUT** | - | **NEXT INS** |
| `F6` | **AMP** | - | **SAVE WAV** |
| `F7` | **PREVIEW** | **PREVIEW** | **PRV EDGE** |
| `F8` | **UNDO** | **UNDO** | **REDO** |

(Picture: Sample edit, Shift row: AMG 8K, AMG 16K, Q8, DC REM, NEXT INS, SAVE WAV, PRV EDGE, REDO.)

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` (**CROP**) | Keep only the selection. | none yet |
| `F2` (**NORM**) | Normalise the selection, or the whole sample if there is none. | QA-SED-002 |
| `F3` (**REVERSE**), `F4` (**FADE IN**), `F5` (**FADE OUT**) | Reverse or fade the selection, or the whole sample. | none yet |
| `F6` (**AMP**) | Change the volume by the **AMP** percentage. `Shift` + `Up` and `Down` set it. | none yet |
| `F7` (**PREVIEW**) | Play the sample while held. | none yet |
| `Left`, `Right`, the encoder, `Delete` | Pick an edge, move it, clear the selection. | none yet |
| `F8` (**UNDO**, **CANCEL** while a process runs) | Take back the last process; while a process is running, stop it and leave the sample as it was. | QA-SED-004, QA-SED-023 |
| FX page: `F1` (**FILTER**), `F2` (**COMPRESS**) | Filter or compress the selection, or the whole sample. `Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right` pick a row, the encoder changes it. | QA-SED-019, QA-SED-020, QA-SED-021 |
| `Shift` + `F1` (**AMG 8K**) | Convert to the Amiga rate of 8,287 Hz. | QA-SED-001 |
| `Shift` + `F2` (**AMG 16K**) | Convert to the Amiga rate of 16,574 Hz. | QA-SED-001 |
| `Shift` + `F3` (**Q8**) | The 8-bit option of the Amiga conversion. | QA-SED-001 |
| `Shift` + `F4` (**DC REM**) | Remove the DC offset of the selection, or of the whole sample. | QA-SED-001, QA-SED-003 |
| `Shift` + `F5` (**NEXT INS**) | Edit the next instrument, 64 round to 1 (a slot that holds no sample says **NO SAMPLE IN THIS INSTRUMENT** to an effect). A pad picks one of 1 to 48 directly. | QA-SED-001, QA-SED-017 |
| `Shift` + `F6` (**SAVE WAV**) | Save the sample, as it is now, as a mono WAV file in the `Samples` folder of the card, named `SMP_001.wav`, `SMP_002.wav` and so on, at the instrument's rate. | QA-SED-001 |
| `Shift` + `F7` (**PRV EDGE**) | Preview from the edge of the selection. | QA-SED-001 |
| `Shift` + `F8` (**REDO**) | Do the process again after an undo. | QA-SED-001, QA-SED-004 |

## Good to know

- Each process is one undo step, up to three.
- `Left` and `Right` pick the start or the end of the selection. The encoder moves the picked edge one column of the view a click (one frame only at full zoom), and `Shift` + encoder moves it 16 columns at a time. `Delete` clears the selection. `Up` and `Down` zoom the view.
- `F7` (**PREVIEW**) plays the instrument while you hold it. `Shift` + `F7` (**PRV EDGE**) plays from the picked edge while you hold it.
- The Amiga conversion refuses a wavetable: **A WAVETABLE CANNOT BE CONVERTED**. A sample converted with **AMG 8K** reloads at 8,287 Hz on the Amiga engine.
- **SAVE WAV** with no card write layer says **NO CARD WRITE LAYER**, and with no sample **NO SAMPLE IN THIS INSTRUMENT**. It writes nothing then.
- Not yet checked on the unit: the processes and the Amiga keys. Not checked against the original firmware: the keys on this screen.

## See also

- [Sample load](sample_load.md): bring the sample into an instrument.
- [Wave and Chop](wave.md): the play mode and the slices.

# Wave and Chop

Status: draft

The play mode of a sample is also set on this screen, as well as on the **PLAY MODE** row of Instrument. `Shift` + `F1` (**MODE**) opens a list of eight modes, and the mode decides the view: the slice modes open the CHOP page, and WAVETABLE and GRANULAR have views of their own. The WAVETABLE and GRANULAR views are described by the official manual, and their key labels were not compared with an official unit.

## What it is for

Use Wave to see how a sample plays: its mode and the part of it that sounds. Use CHOP to place the slices of a slice mode. Press `Sample Play` to open it.

## How it works

The play mode is a property of the instrument, saved with the project. It tells the voice how to read the sample: once, in a loop, in slices, or as a one-cycle oscillator. The screen follows the mode: ONE SHOT and the loops show the WAVE page, with points to move. SLICE and BEAT SLICE show CHOP, where pad n plays slice n. WAVETABLE shows a window that moves over a table, and GRANULAR shows a grain that you place and shape.

What you move is stored in the instrument. What you hear on `F6` (**PREVIEW**) is live and ends when you let go. `F8` (**UNDO**) takes back Wave edits only.

The loop marks on the waveform and the LOOP START and LOOP END values count only in the loop modes (LOOP FWD, LOOP BWD, PING-PONG): in ONE SHOT the marks are not drawn and the two values are dim, and you can still move them.

Loop start and end, the wavetable position and the grain position take effect at once. The start, the end, the slices and the play mode reach the sound when the transport is stopped and the pads are let go. New in track3r-os.

Example: load a file of many single-cycle windows, choose WAVETABLE, hold a pad and turn **POSITION**: the tone changes window by window.

## Try it

1. Press `Sample Play` on a sample instrument. The WAVE page opens.
2. Press `Shift` + `F1` (**MODE**). The eight modes appear, and **NOW** marks the instrument's own.

   (Picture: Wave: the list of play modes, with NOW on the instrument's own mode.)

3. Press `Down` until the cursor is on **WAVETABLE**: six times from **ONE SHOT**, the first mode. Then press `F1` (**SELECT**). The view shows the window on the sample.

   (Picture: Wave, WAVETABLE view: the window is marked on the sample.)

4. Press `F2` (**WINDOW**) and turn the encoder down one click. The window halves, and the same part stays marked.

5. Press `Shift` + `F1`, `Up` twice and `F1`. The CHOP page opens with no slices.

6. With a sample loaded, press `F2` (**EVEN**). The sample is cut in equal parts, drawn as lines. Pad n plays slice n.

Not yet checked on the unit.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Wave: a sample on the WAVE page, with the key row and the play mode in the header.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header | The pages **WAVE** and **CHOP**, then **MODE** and the play mode, then **SHIFT+F1: CHANGE**. |
| Main area | The sample, with its points or slices, or the window or grain. |
| Info line | The length in frames and the rate in Hz, or a hint. |
| Strip | Messages, for example **NO SAMPLE INSTRUMENT HERE**. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F8`, labelled for the view you are on. |
| Shift row | **MODE** on `F1`, **PRV SEL** on `F6`, **REDO** on `F8`. |

## More tasks

### Change the play mode

Start on the Wave screen, on a sample instrument. A MIDI instrument or an empty slot has no play mode.

1. Press `Shift` + `F1` (**MODE**). The list opens with the eight modes: ONE SHOT, LOOP FWD, LOOP BWD, PING-PONG, SLICE, BEAT SLICE, WAVETABLE and GRANULAR.
2. Press `Up` or `Down`, or turn the encoder, to move to a mode.
3. Press `F1` (**SELECT**) to keep the mode.

While the list is open the key row shows only its own keys: `F1` reads **SELECT**, `F8` reads **BACK**, and the other keys are blank because they do nothing there.

The cursor starts on the instrument's own mode, which is marked **NOW**. You should see the view of the new mode. WAVETABLE and GRANULAR have views of their own. The slice modes show the CHOP page. The other modes show the WAVE page.

On a MIDI instrument or an empty slot, the strip says **NO SAMPLE INSTRUMENT HERE** and the list does not open.

### Set the window of a wavetable

Start on the Wave screen, in the WAVETABLE view. To get there, change the mode as above.

1. Press `F2` (**WINDOW**) to select the WINDOW row.
2. Turn the encoder down one click. The window halves, from 2048 to 1024 samples. Its position doubles, so the same part of the sample stays marked.
3. Keep turning down to make it smaller. It stops at 32 samples. Hold `Shift` to turn in bigger steps.

The window fits the sample. It is at most 2048 samples, and never longer than the sample. `Delete` sets the row back to its default. A sample shorter than 32 frames cannot use WAVETABLE. The strip says **WAVETABLE NEEDS A SAMPLE OF 32 FRAMES**.

### Play a wavetable

Start on the Wave screen. A wavetable is a WAV file of many windows, one after another. Load it with [Sample load](sample_load.md). The file is in the `WTABLE` folder of the card.

1. Set the mode to WAVETABLE, as in "Change the play mode".
2. Hold a pad. The pad plays the window as an oscillator.
3. Press `F1` (**POSITION**), then turn the encoder. The window changes one step at a time.

You should see the waveform of the table, with the window marked. The POSITION row reads `n OF 0..N-1`, where `N` is the number of windows. The timbre changes as the window changes.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Move the start, loop or end point

Start on the WAVE page of a sample instrument.

1. Press `F1` (**START**), `F2` (**LOOP S**), `F3` (**LOOP E**) or `F4` (**END**). That row is highlighted.
2. Turn the encoder. The point moves. A loop point is pushed ahead of the start and pulled in behind the end by the same edit.
3. Press `F5` (**ZC**) to switch zero-crossing snap on or off. With it on, the encoder jumps to the next zero crossing in the direction you turn.
4. Hold `F6` (**PREVIEW**) to hear the instrument. It stops when you let go.
5. Press `F7` (**ZOOM-**) to widen the window, or `Up` to zoom in around the picked point.

`F8` (**UNDO**) takes the edit back, and `Shift` + `F8` does it again.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Show the CHOP page

Start on the Wave screen, on a sample instrument.

1. Press `Shift` + `F1` (**MODE**), choose **SLICE** or **BEAT SLICE**, and press `F1` (**SELECT**).

You should see the CHOP page, with the keys **AUTO**, **EVEN**, **ZC**, **ADD**, **DEL**, **PREVIEW**, **ZOOM-** and **UNDO**.
A slice mode with no slices says, for example, **SLICE: NO SLICES, AUTO OR EVEN ON WAVE** in the strip. Here WAVE means this screen: the keys are on its CHOP page.

### Cut a sample into slices

Start on the CHOP page of a sample instrument.

1. Press `F1` (**AUTO**) to let the unit choose the slices from the sound. Or press `F2` (**EVEN**) to cut the sample into equal parts. `Shift` + `Up` and `Shift` + `Down` set how many parts, from 2 to 48.
2. Press `F4` (**ADD**) to split the selected slice in two, at the middle between its start and its end (the zoom does not matter; with no slices yet, the first press puts one at the middle of the whole sample). Press `F5` (**DEL**) to remove the selected slice; the selection moves to a neighbour.
3. Press `Left` or `Right` to pick a slice, and turn the encoder to move it. `Shift` + the encoder moves faster. `F3` (**ZC**) makes it land on a zero crossing, where the sound crosses the centre line.

You should see the slices as lines on the sample. The strip says **PLAY MODE: BEAT SLICE**, and pad n plays slice n. A sample holds up to 48 slices. Each change is one undo step: `F8` (**UNDO**). Not checked on the unit.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | WAVE | CHOP | WAVETABLE | GRANULAR | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **START** | **AUTO** | **POSITION** | **POSITION** | **MODE** |
| `F2` | **LOOP S** | **EVEN** | **WINDOW** | **LENGTH** | - |
| `F3` | **LOOP E** | **ZC** | - | **SHAPE** | - |
| `F4` | **END** | **ADD** | - | **LOOP** | - |
| `F5` | **ZC** | **DEL** | - | - | - |
| `F6` | **PREVIEW** | **PREVIEW** | **PREVIEW** | **PREVIEW** | **PRV SEL** |
| `F7` | **ZOOM-** | **ZOOM-** | **ZOOM-** | **ZOOM-** | - |
| `F8` | **UNDO** | **UNDO** | **UNDO** | **UNDO** | **REDO** |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Shift` + `F1` (**MODE**) | opens the list of play modes | QA-WAV-001, QA-WAV-003 |
| `Shift` + `F6` (**PRV SEL**) | previews from the selected point. If that point is out of view, from the left edge of the window | QA-WAV-001 |
| `Shift` + `F8` (**REDO**) | does the last undone Wave edit again | QA-WAV-001 |
| `Shift` + `F2` to `F5`, `Shift` + `F7` | nothing | QA-WAV-001 |
| `F1`, `F2`, `Left`, `Right` (WAVETABLE and GRANULAR) | pick the row. `F2` is **WINDOW** on WAVETABLE | QA-WAV-007 |
| the encoder (WAVETABLE and GRANULAR) | changes the selected row. `Shift` turns in bigger steps | QA-WAV-007 |
| `Up`, `Down` (play mode list) | move the cursor | QA-WAV-003 |
| `F1` (**SELECT**) (play mode list) | keeps the cursor's mode | QA-WAV-003 |
| `F8` (**BACK**) (play mode list) | closes the list, and nothing changes | QA-WAV-003 |
| WAVE page: `F1` to `F4` (**START**, **LOOP S**, **LOOP E**, **END**) | pick the point that the encoder moves | QA-WAV-010, QA-WAV-011 |
| WAVE page: `F5` (**ZC**) | snaps the moved point to a zero crossing, on and off | QA-WAV-012 |
| `F6` (**PREVIEW**) | plays the sample while held. `Shift` + `F6` plays from the selected point, or from the left edge of the window when no point is selected | QA-WAV-013 |
| `F7` (**ZOOM-**), `Up` | zoom out; `Up` zooms in | QA-WAV-014 |
| CHOP page: `F1` to `F5` (**AUTO**, **EVEN**, **ZC**, **ADD**, **DEL**) | slice keys, see "Cut a sample into slices" | QA-WAV-017, QA-WAV-018, QA-WAV-019, QA-WAV-020, QA-WAV-021 |
| the encoder, `Left`, `Right` | move the selected point or slice, and pick the next one | QA-WAV-015 |
| a pad (CHOP page) | plays slice n and selects it. `Shift` + pad selects it silently | QA-WAV-024 |
| `F8` (**UNDO**) | takes back the last point or slice edit | QA-WAV-016 |
| `F6` to `F8` (WAVETABLE and GRANULAR) | **PREVIEW**, **ZOOM-** and **UNDO**, as on the WAVE page; `F3` to `F5` are blank on WAVETABLE, and `F5` on GRANULAR | QA-WAV-022, QA-WAV-023 |

## Good to know

- On the CHOP page `F1` to `F5` are **AUTO**, **EVEN**, **ZC**, **ADD** and **DEL**. `Left` and `Right` choose the slice, and a pad press selects it too. The encoder moves the start of the chosen slice.
- **ADD** (`F4`) splits the selected slice at the middle of its start and end, at any zoom. The new slice is selected. With no slices yet, the first press cuts the whole sample in two. Not yet checked on the unit.
- **AUTO** (`F1`) and **EVEN** (`F2`) replace the slices without a question. Each is one undo step, so `F8` (**UNDO**) brings the old slices back.
- A pad pressed straight after **EVEN**, **ADD**, **AUTO**, **DEL** or an undo plays the new slices, even while the transport runs. Not yet checked on the unit.
- A beat slice sounds until the next note on its track starts, which cuts it. A slice with no note after it plays to the end of the slice. New in track3r-os. Not checked against the original firmware.
- `F8` (**UNDO**) takes back the last Wave edit only.
- On a MIDI instrument or a free slot the mode list does not open. The strip says **NO SAMPLE INSTRUMENT HERE**.
- A sample under 32 frames cannot use WAVETABLE. The window is at most 2048 samples and never longer than the sample.
- GRANULAR: **LENGTH** runs from 44 to 44,100 samples, 11 a click. **SHAPE** is Square, Triangle or Gauss. **LOOP** is Forward, Backward or PingPong.
- The Shift row is the same on WAVE and CHOP. While the mode list is open the key row shows only **SELECT** and **BACK**.
- Not checked against the original firmware: the Shift row, the WAVE and CHOP keys. Not yet checked on the unit: wavetable playing.

## See also

- [Sample load](sample_load.md): load a sample or a wavetable file.
- [Sample edit](sample_edit.md): normalise, fade or convert a sample.
- [Instrument](instrument.md): the sound that plays the sample.
