# Record

Status: draft

The Record screen is a looper as well as a sampler. Set the **LOOP** row to 1 to 16 bars and a take records exactly those bars, then repeats in time with the pattern while you add layers on top of it. Save the result and it becomes an instrument. The three pages, **SOURCES**, **RESAMPLE** and **RADIO**, and the take, trim and save flow are the screen's other half. New in track3r-os: the looper.

## What it is for

Use Record to capture sound into a sample, or to build a loop over the pattern. Open the screen with the `Sample Rec` button. Come here when you want to sample a line input, the microphone, the radio or the computer, or to resample your own mix.

(Picture: Record, SOURCES page: the LOOP row is the last row, and sets the loop length.)

## How it works

A loop pedal repeats what you played and lets you play over it. The looper does the same, except that its length is a number of pattern bars and it restarts on the bar, so it stays in time with the pattern.

### A loop: live, stored and ended

With **LOOP** on, press `F1` and the take waits for the next bar. It records exactly the bars you set, then ends by itself on the bar.

- **Live:** the loop sits in the sample memory and plays in time with the sequencer, on whatever screen you are on. It is not written to the project.
- **Stored:** only when you press `F3` (**SAVE**). The loop, with its layers, goes into the first free instrument slot, for example **LOOP 4B**, with play mode LOOP FWD over the whole sample.
- **Ended:** by `F4` (**DISCARD**), by a project load or NEW, or by saving it. A Stop of the transport only fades it out, and Play brings it back on the first bar.

Example: set **LOOP** to 4 BARS over a four-bar drum pattern, play a bass line into the line input, and the bass repeats against the drums on every pass.

### A layer: what an overdub adds

A layer is one pass of overdub: the sound you add to a loop while it repeats. Press `F1` (or `Rec`) in the loop review and what the input carries is written onto the loop where it plays. You hear the new layer from the next pass. Press `F1` again to end it.

**FEEDBACK** decides what happens to the old sound under the new. At 100 nothing fades and every layer stays. At 0 the new input replaces the old. In between, older layers fade each pass.

Example: record a one-bar kick loop, then overdub a hat for one pass. At FEEDBACK 100 you keep both. Press `F5` (**UNDO LYR**) and the hat goes. Layers add up, so a loud layer on a loud loop can clip.

### What the loop listens to

The loop takes its sound from the source it was made from. On **RESAMPLE** that is your mix before the loop. While the loop exists, the **SOURCE**, **TAP**, **FREQUENCY** and **REGION** rows are dim, because its source is locked.

If you want to know more:

- **UNDO LYR** takes back one layer: the last overdub session. A new session drops the old undo.
- **LOOP VOL** sets the loop's level, from 0 to 100.
- The loop goes to the line out after the master chain. It is not in the meters, the stems or any take.

(Picture: Record, loop review: the header reads REVIEW with the loop length, and the key row offers OVERDUB, SAVE, DISCARD, UNDO LYR and LOOP ON.)

## Try it

1. Press `Sample Rec`, then `Down` to **LOOP**, and turn the encoder to **1 BAR**.
2. Press `Play`, then `F1`. The header says **ARMED - LOOP 1 BAR**.
3. Play a sound into the input. The take ends on the bar: the header says **REVIEW - LOOP 1 BAR** and the loop repeats.
4. Press `F1` (**OVERDUB**), play a second sound for one bar, then press `F1` again.

   (Picture: Record, overdub: the header shows OVERDUB and the key F1 is lit.)

5. Listen: both sounds play on the same bar. Press `F5` (**UNDO LYR**) and the second one goes.
6. Press `F3` (**SAVE**) to keep the loop as an instrument, or `F4` (**DISCARD**) to throw it away.

The simulator has no recorder, so its scenario `record_walk.txt` checks only the screen and the page turn (the `Sample Rec` button), not these steps, and this walk-through has no pictures of its own: the three above come from the screen's gallery. Not yet checked on the unit.

## The screen at a glance

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header | The state of a take or loop, for example **REVIEW - LOOP 4 BARS**. |
| Rows | The settings of the page. `Up` and `Down` move the cursor; the encoder, or `Left` and `Right`, changes the value. |
| Strip | Short messages, for example **RECORDING IN 4.. 3.. 2.. 1..**. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F8`. Under a loop review the whole row changes. |
| Shift row | The labels drawn while `Shift` is held. See the table under "Keys on this screen". |

## More tasks

### Record a sample

Start on the **SOURCES** page.

1. Press `Down` to **SOURCE** and turn the encoder: **LINE**, **LINE L**, **LINE R**, **MIC LG**, **MIC HG**, **RADIO** or **USB**. The **RESAMPLE** page has **TAP** in its place (**MASTER**, **REC BUS** or **TRACK**) and the **RADIO** page has **FREQUENCY** and **REGION**.
2. Press `Down` to **GAIN** and turn the encoder from 0 to 100 %. Each input type keeps its own gain. It reads **--** for **USB**.
3. Press `Down` to the start row, **START ON**, and turn the encoder. Choose **FREE** to start at once, **STEP**, **BAR** or **PATTERN** to wait for that point, or **LEVEL** to start when the sound reaches a level (see "Start a take on a level" below).
4. Press `F1`. With the transport running, the take waits for that point, and the strip counts down: **RECORDING IN 4.. 3.. 2.. 1..**.
5. A Stop of the transport before the take starts gives the take up.
6. Press `F1` again to end the take. With **STOP AT** on **STEP**, **BAR** or **PATTERN** it ends at that point, and a second `F1` ends it at once. With **STOP AT** on a number of bars, it ends by itself.
7. The screen says **TAKE: TRIM, THEN SAVE**. Set **TRIM START** and **TRIM END**. Press `F3` to save the window into an instrument (the keyboard opens at once over its name, **RECORDING**: type a name and press `F8`, or press `F7` to keep **RECORDING**; the take is saved either way), or `Shift` + `F3` (**CROP**) to cut the take down to the window and keep working on it, or `F4` to throw it away (with nothing recorded, `F4` says **NOTHING RECORDED**). `F4`, a new take with `F1` and **CROP** each ask first (**TAKE NOT SAVED: F4 AGAIN**, **CROP KEEPS THE WINDOW ONLY: SHIFT+F3 AGAIN**): press the same key again within four seconds. A take you have written with `F7` (**SAVE WAV**) is saved, so it needs no question until you move a marker.

`F7` (**SAVE WAV**) writes the trimmed window as a 16-bit mono WAV at 44,100 Hz into the `Samples` folder of the card, as `REC_001.wav`, `REC_002.wav` and so on. The strip says **SAVE REC_001 DONE** and the take stays in review, so `F3` can still make an instrument of it. With no take it says **NO TAKE TO SAVE: F1 RECORDS ONE**, with no card write layer **NO CARD WRITE LAYER**, and on a write-protected card **CARD IS WRITE PROTECTED**. Not yet checked on the unit.

Press `F2` (**MONITOR**) on the **SOURCES** page to hear the input through the output. It still works while a take is armed or recording. On **RESAMPLE** it does nothing. New in track3r-os.

While the take records, **MEM** in the top bar reads 100 %, because the take holds all the free sample memory. When the take ends, **MEM** drops to the memory that was in use before, plus the size of the take. `F4` gives that memory back at once and **MEM** returns to the level from before the take; `F3` keeps it in the instrument.

The card beside the rows shows **TIME LEFT**, the longest take you can still make: before the take it is the free sample memory in seconds, while the take records it counts down, and at zero the take ends (**THE SAMPLE MEMORY FILLED: THE TAKE ENDED**). It is gone under the review, and a loop does not show it, because a loop is as long as its bars. This is new in track3r-os; the official firmware does not show a maximum.

### Start a take on a level

New in track3r-os: the official firmware has no such start.

Set **START ON** to **LEVEL** and two rows join the page under it. **THRESHOLD** is the level the sound must reach, from **-60 DB** to **-6 DB** in steps of 3 (`Shift` + encoder moves 9 dB). It starts at **-30 DB**. **PRE-ROLL** is how much sound from before the level the take keeps: **0**, **10**, **20**, **50** or **100 MS**. It starts at **50 MS**. `Delete` puts the row under the cursor back to its default. The rows are on all three pages, and only while **START ON** is **LEVEL**.

1. Set **START ON** to **LEVEL**, then **THRESHOLD** and **PRE-ROLL**.
2. Press `F1`. The card says **WAITING FOR LEVEL**, and the clock stays at 0. Nothing is recorded yet, but the last **PRE-ROLL** of sound is kept all the time.
3. When the sound reaches **THRESHOLD**, the take starts and the card says **RECORDING**. The take begins **PRE-ROLL** before that point, so the start of the sound is not cut off.
4. Press `F1` to end the take, as for any other take. Press `F1` while it still waits for the level to cancel: nothing is kept, and no take is made.

**LEVEL** does not need the transport. It works with the transport stopped, and it does not count in, even when **COUNT-IN** is on. It never falls back to **FREE** (the other waiting starts do when the transport is stopped). The two rows are runtime settings only: nothing is stored, and a restart puts them back to **-30 DB** and **50 MS**. They are not shown while a take is under review: save it (`F3`) or throw it away (`F4`) to change them.

With **LOOP** on, a loop must start on a bar, so **START ON** reads **BAR** (as it does for any loop), the two rows are hidden and **F1** waits for the bar. **LEVEL** itself is kept and is back when **LOOP** is off.

Limits:

- The level is read on the sound that the take is made of: the REC bus, the master (**MAIN**) or the track the page taps, the same signal as the two meters beside the rows. It is not the level at the codec input.
- One sample at or above **THRESHOLD** starts the take: there is no hysteresis and no hold, so a click can start it.
- The start comes from the sound, not from the sequencer. A step of the sequencer that falls in the same short block (64 frames, about 1.5 ms) as the level is not counted, so a **STOP AT** of **STEP**, **BAR** or **PATTERN** ends one boundary later when its boundary is in that block.
- **PRE-ROLL** is kept at least: it is rounded up to an even number of frames, and one frame more can be kept. If the level arrives less than **PRE-ROLL** after `F1`, nothing was heard before it: the first frames of the take are silence, and **TRIM START** starts after them.
- A Stop of the transport does not end a take that waits for a level, because it does not need the transport. `F1` ends it, and it ends with no take.
- With the sample memory nearly full, `F1` says **NO ROOM IN THE SAMPLE MEMORY**: **LEVEL** needs room for the pre-roll and about a second of take.
- Not checked on the unit yet.

### Record what the computer plays

The **USB** source records the sound that the computer plays into the Tracker. The unit must be connected to the computer, with **USB AUDIO** and **USB RETURN** both **On** on the USB page of [Config](config.md). They are On by default.

Start on the **SOURCES** page.

1. Press `Down` to **SOURCE** and turn the encoder to **USB**. **GAIN** reads **--**, because USB has no gain. The take has the level that the computer plays.
2. Play the sound on the computer, to the Tracker as its audio output.
3. Press `F1` to start the take, and `F1` again to end it. The take is mono: the left and right sides are averaged.
4. The screen says **TAKE: TRIM, THEN SAVE**. Press the pad at the take's own pitch (**C-4**, pad 12) to hear it. Press `F3` to save it, or `F4` to throw it away (it asks first: press `F4` again).

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Record a loop

Start on the **SOURCES**, **RESAMPLE** or **RADIO** page. The loop row is on all three.

1. Press `Down` to **LOOP** and turn the encoder to the number of bars, from **1 BAR** to **16 BARS**. Hold `Shift` and turn it to move four bars at a time.
2. Press `Play`, then `F1`. The header says **ARMED - LOOP** and the number of bars. The take starts on the next bar.
3. Wait. The take records exactly the bars you set. It ends by itself on the bar, and the screen shows **REVIEW - LOOP** and the number of bars. The loop repeats on the bars.

(Picture: Record, loop review: the header reads REVIEW with the loop length, and the key row offers OVERDUB, SAVE, DISCARD, UNDO LYR and LOOP ON.)

### Add a layer (overdub)

Start on the review of a loop.

1. Press `F1` (or `Rec`). The header gains **- OVERDUB**. The screen says **OVERDUB: LAYERING**, and `F1` is lit.
2. Make the sound the loop was recorded from. Each pass adds it on top of the loop, and you hear the new layer from the next pass.
3. Press `F1` again to end the layer.

> **Tip**: With the transport stopped, `F1` starts it.

With the transport stopped, `F1` first counts in when **COUNT-IN** is 1 or 2 bars (set on the Config screen). The count-in plays the pattern that `Play` starts. Nothing is recorded during it. The layer begins on the loop's first bar after the count-in, and fades in over a very short ramp. With **COUNT-IN** Off, the transport and the layer start together. Not yet checked on the unit.

(Picture: Record, overdub: the header shows OVERDUB and the key F1 is lit.)

### Set how much a layer keeps

Start on the review of a loop. FEEDBACK is used only while overdub is on.

1. Press `Down` to **FEEDBACK**, the last row, and turn the encoder. It goes from 0 to 100. The default is 100.
2. Hold `Shift` and turn the encoder to move in steps of 5. Press `Delete` to set 100.

The change is heard from the next pass, and only while overdub is on.

### Undo the last layer

Start on the review of a loop, after an overdub.

1. Press `F5` (**UNDO LYR**). It is dim while the loop has no layer.
2. Wait. The loop fades out. The header says **- UNDO**, and the screen says **UNDOING THE LAYER**.
3. When the restore is done, the loop fades in on its next restart. You hear the loop without the last layer.

### Mute the loop

Start on the review of a loop.

1. Press `F8`. The key reads **MUTED**, and the header gains **- MUTED**. It keeps its place on the bars.
2. Press `F8` again. The key reads **LOOP ON**, and the loop is heard where the bars have it.

### Save the loop as an instrument

Start on the review of a loop.

1. Press `F3` (**SAVE**).
2. The loop, with its layers, goes into the first free instrument slot, named for example **LOOP 4B**, in LOOP FWD over the whole sample. The keyboard opens over that name: type a new one and press `F8`, or press `F7` to keep it. The looper is then free.

If no instrument slot is free, nothing is saved and the strip says **NO FREE INSTRUMENT SLOT**.

### Discard the loop

> **Careful**: Discard throws away the loop, its layers and its undo. Nothing brings them back.

Start on the review of a loop.

1. Press `F4` (**DISCARD**). The strip asks **TAKE NOT SAVED: F4 AGAIN**; press `F4` again. The strip says **TAKE DISCARDED**. The loop fades out within one block.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Record | Loop review | Loop review, muted | `Shift`, SOURCES and RESAMPLE | `Shift`, RADIO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **REC/STOP** | **OVERDUB** | **OVERDUB** | - | - |
| `F2` | **MONITOR** | **MONITOR** | **MONITOR** | - | - |
| `F3` | **SAVE** | **SAVE** | **SAVE** | **CROP** | **CROP** |
| `F4` | **DISCARD** | **DISCARD** | **DISCARD** | - | - |
| `F5` | **SEEK-** | **UNDO LYR** | **UNDO LYR** | - | **CH-10** |
| `F6` | **SEEK+** | - | - | - | **CH+10** |
| `F7` | **SAVE WAV** | **SAVE WAV** | **SAVE WAV** | - | - |
| `F8` | **PREVIEW** | **LOOP ON** | **MUTED** | - | - |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Up`, `Down` | Move the cursor between the rows. | QA-REC-012 |
| `Left`, `Right` | Change the value of the row under the cursor, one click of the encoder down or up. New in track3r-os. | QA-REC-060 |
| `Shift` + `Left`, `Shift` + `Right` | The same in the coarse step, as `Shift` + the encoder. | QA-REC-061 |
| `Sample Rec` (again) | Turns the page through SOURCES, RESAMPLE and RADIO, and wraps after RADIO. Each page keeps its row. `Left` and `Right` never turn the page. | QA-REC-012, QA-REC-062 |
| the encoder | Change the value of the row under the cursor. | QA-REC-020, QA-REC-031 |
| `Shift` + the encoder | LOOP: moves four bars. FEEDBACK: moves in steps of 5. | QA-REC-020, QA-REC-031 |
| `Delete` | LOOP: OFF. FEEDBACK and LOOP VOL: 100. | QA-REC-020, QA-REC-022, QA-REC-031 |
| `F1` | Arms a take. Under a loop review: **OVERDUB**, on and off, with the count-in if it is on. | QA-REC-010, QA-REC-021, QA-REC-028, QA-REC-032 |
| `Rec` | Under a loop review: the same as `F1`. | QA-REC-022, QA-REC-028 |
| `F2` (**MONITOR**) | Hear the input through the output, on and off. Nothing on RESAMPLE. | QA-REC-037 |
| `F3` (**SAVE**) | Save the loop as an instrument. | QA-REC-025, QA-REC-030 |
| `F4` (**DISCARD**) | Throw the loop away. It asks first: press `F4` again. | QA-REC-026, QA-REC-040 |
| `F5` (**SEEK-**), `F6` (**SEEK+**) | RADIO page: the radio's own seek, down and up. Nothing on the other pages. | QA-REC-038 |
| `F7` (**SAVE WAV**) | Write the take's window as a WAV on the card. | QA-REC-039 |
| `Shift` + `F3` (**CROP**) | Cut a take under review down to its window. It asks first. Not for a loop. | QA-REC-041 |
| `F5` (**UNDO LYR**) | Undo the last layer. Dim with no layer. | QA-REC-022, QA-REC-029 |
| `F8` (**LOOP ON** / **MUTED**) | Mute or unmute the loop. | QA-REC-024 |
| `Play` | Start and stop the transport. The loop follows it. | QA-REC-023 |

The Shift row of the Record screen:

| Key | SOURCES and RESAMPLE | RADIO | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Shift` + `F5` | nothing | **CH-10**: tunes ten channels down, with no seek | QA-REC-001, QA-REC-011 |
| `Shift` + `F6` | nothing | **CH+10**: tunes ten channels up, with no seek | QA-REC-001, QA-REC-011 |
| `Shift` + `F3` (**CROP**) | cuts the take down to its window | the same | QA-REC-001, QA-REC-041 |
| any other `Shift` + `F1` to `F8` | nothing | nothing | QA-REC-001 |

On the RADIO page, the plain `F5` (**SEEK-**) and `F6` (**SEEK+**) ask the radio chip for the next station down or up, wrapping at the end of the band. The page reads **SEEKING** while the chip looks, then **LISTENING**, and the frequency is what it found. Under a loop review `F5` is **UNDO LYR** and `F6` does nothing. Not yet checked on the unit: a real station needs an antenna.

## Good to know

- New in track3r-os: the loop, the overdub and the undo layer. Not yet checked on the unit: the looper.
- Not checked against the original firmware: the sources, the take and trim flow and the radio page.
- The loop keeps playing on other screens, like a loop pedal. `F8`, `F3` and `F4` work only on this screen.
- The LOOP row is frozen while a take runs. With LOOP on, **START ON** reads **BAR** and **STOP AT** reads **LOOP**, both dim. Editing either says why.
- A loop is refused at `F1` if it cannot fit the free sample memory: **NO ROOM IN THE SAMPLE MEMORY FOR THE LOOP**. A take that ends early, or fills the sample memory, is given up with **THE LOOP TAKE ENDED BEFORE ITS LAST BAR: GIVEN UP** or **THE SAMPLE MEMORY FILLED: THE TAKE ENDED**. A project load, NEW or a kit gives it up with **TAKE LOST: A PROJECT WAS LOADED UNDER IT**.
- A Stop fades the loop out in under a millisecond. After Play, a loop starts again from its first bar, not from where it stopped. A tempo change keeps the loop's length: a faster tempo cuts it short, a slower one leaves a gap. The header then says **- TEMPO CHANGED**.
- During an undo restore, `F1` and `F3` say **UNDO IN PROGRESS**. `F4` and `F8` still work.
- If the transport does not start after the count-in, the strip says **THE COUNT-IN DID NOT START** or **THE TRANSPORT DID NOT START**. The overdub ends again, with no layer.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- If the sound does not answer when you press `F3` (**SAVE**) during an overdub, the keys ignore presses for up to half a second. Then the strip says **SAVE TIMED OUT: TRY AGAIN**. Nothing is saved, and the loop stays on the screen. Once the sound runs again, the overdub is over, and `F3` saves the loop as usual. It cannot be made to happen by hand on the unit, so it is checked by the host tests only.
- The loop goes to both channels of the line out after the master chain. The master volume scales it. It is not in the meters, the stems or any take.

## See also

- [Sample edit](sample_edit.md): change a sample after you record or save it.
- [Sample load](sample_load.md): bring a sample from the card into an instrument.
- [Config](config.md): the count-in, which plays before a take when it is on.

---

# File

Status: draft

File lists the projects on the card, and one part of it is new in track3r-os: a project can be exported in the original firmware's format.  The card can also go to a computer as a disk, which [USB disk](usb_disk.md) describes. The screen itself, its keys and its messages are not checked against the original firmware.

## What it is for

Use the File screen to work with projects on the card. A project holds your patterns, song order, instruments and samples, in its own folder. Open the screen with `File`. It opens the PROJECTS page, where you open, save, start, name and delete projects.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: File, PROJECTS page: RECENT rows on top, the open project named in the header, and the key row from OPEN to EXPORT.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Header | At the right, **PROJECT** and the project's title, then the page name (**OPEN**) at the far right. A project with no title shows its folder name. While the project has changes that no save has taken, **UNSAVED** stands where **PROJECT** was (**UNSAVED** alone for a project with no name); a save, NEW or OPEN clears it.  |
| Main area | The project list. The first rows are **RECENT**: the last five projects you opened or saved. |
| Strip | Messages, for example **SAVE ... DONE**. Questions also appear here. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F8`: **OPEN**, **RESCAN**, **NEW**, **SAVE**, **SAVE AS**, **IMPORT**, **EXPORT**, and a blank. |
| Shift row | The labels drawn while `Shift` is held: **0/4**, **1/4**, **2/4**, **3/4**, **END**, **NAME** and **PURGE**. |

## More tasks

### Open a project

Start on the File screen, on the PROJECTS page.

1. Press `Up` or `Down` to the project. For a recent project, press `Left` or `Right` to move between the **RECENT** rows and the list.
2. Press `F1` (**OPEN**).
3. If the project has changes that no save has taken, the strip says **UNSAVED CHANGES: F1 AGAIN TO DISCARD THEM**. Press `F1` again. A move of the cursor, or any other key, takes the question back.

You should see **OPENING** and the project's name, then the Pattern screen with **PROJECT <NAME> OPENED**. If the project cannot be opened, the screen stays on File and the strip says why, for example **PROJECT <NAME> FAILED: NO PROJECT FILE** or **PROJECT <NAME> FAILED: THE FILE IS CUT SHORT**. A refused project leaves the project you had open, its undo history and the playing transport as they were.

At power-on the unit opens the project you had open last (the newest **RECENT** entry), and the strip says **PROJECT <NAME> OPENED**. If it cannot load, the unit starts with an empty project and the strip says **PROJECT <NAME> FAILED** and why, at every start until you open another project. With no card, or on the USB disk boot, nothing is opened. New in track3r-os. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Save a project, save a copy, or name it

Start on the PROJECTS page.

1. Press `F4` (**SAVE**). The strip says **SAVE <NAME> DONE**, and the earlier file is kept as `project.o3pj.bak`. A project that has no folder yet is saved in the first free folder named **Track nn**, with a title or without one.
2. To save a copy, press `F5` (**SAVE AS**). The keyboard opens. Type a folder name with the pads: letters, digits, spaces and `-`, at most 31 characters. Press `F8` (**SAVE**). `F6` (**AUTO**) fills in a name for you, and `F7` leaves without saving. `F8` with no name typed says **TYPE A NAME** and the keyboard stays open.
3. To change the title shown in the header, press `Shift` + `F6` (**NAME**), type up to 32 characters and press `F8`. The strip says **PROJECT NAMED**.

**SAVE** in a project you opened from an official (OG) folder adds `project.o3pj` beside the original files and leaves them alone: a sample whose `samples/instrNN.wav` already holds the same audio is not rewritten, and only a sample you edited gets a new file (the old one kept as `.bak`).  **SAVE AS** writes a new folder and leaves the old one alone.  The folder keeps its name when you change the title. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Start a new project

Start on the PROJECTS page.

1. Press `F3` (**NEW**). The strip says **NEW PROJECT: F3 ALL, F1 KEEP INSTRUMENTS**, or **UNSAVED CHANGES: F3 ALL, F1 KEEP INSTRUMENTS** when a save is due. The key row marks the two answers.
2. Press `F1` (**KEEP INS**) to keep the instruments and their samples, or `F3` (**ALL**) to remove every instrument.

You should see **NEW PROJECT**, then the Pattern screen. With **KEEP INSTRUMENTS** the patterns, song and title are new, and a save gives the new project its own copy of each kept sample. With **ALL** the project has one empty pattern, one song position, no title and no instrument. A move, another key, leaving the screen, or 4 seconds without an answer cancels the question, and the plain key row returns. The question takes the strip at once, even from a message such as **SAVE ... DONE**; a warning or an error already there keeps its place.

> **Careful**: **ALL** removes every instrument and frees the sample memory. Save first if you want to keep them.

### Delete a project

Start on the PROJECTS page. Deleting hides a project. It does not erase it.

1. Move the cursor to the project, and press `Delete`. The strip says **DELETE <NAME>? DELETE AGAIN**.
2. Press `Delete` again. The strip says **DELETED: <NAME>**, and the project leaves the list.

The folder stays on the card, marked with an empty `.deleted` file. To list the project again, or free the space, use a computer.  You cannot delete the open project: the strip says **CANNOT DELETE THE OPEN PROJECT**.

### Remove unused instruments

Start on the PROJECTS page. This removes instruments that no step, FX or Learn binding uses.

1. Press `Shift` + `F7` (**PURGE**). The strip asks **PURGE <N> UNUSED INSTRUMENTS? SHIFT+F7 AGAIN**, or says **NO UNUSED INSTRUMENTS**.
2. Press `Shift` + `F7` again. The strip says **PURGED <N> INSTRUMENTS - F8 ON PARAMS UNDOES**.

Module instruments are never removed.  The next save leaves the removed instruments out; their sample files stay in the `samples` folder.  To bring them all back, press `F8` (**UNDO**) on the Params screen.

### Export a project in the original format (console)

New in track3r-os.  This writes the patterns and the project file into a new folder on the card, and changes nothing already there. It is not the EXPORT page (`F7`), described in [Export](export.md). Stop the transport, end any take, and open the diag console (see [Computer tools](computer_tools.md)).

1. Type `diag ogexp` and press Enter.
2. Type `diag ogexp status` until the reply says `DONE`.
3. To check, type `diag load Export/<name> OG`, with the project's name in place of `<name>`.

You should see `ogexp: DONE n/n files Export/<name> OG`. The folder, such as `Export/Mine OG`, holds one file for each pattern, the pattern names, `project.mt` and one file for each sample instrument. The project loads with the same patterns, tempo, song and track names; pattern names are not read back.

- A second export goes to `Mine OG 2`, and so on up to `OG 99`, then the reply says `NO FREE OG FOLDER NAME`. What the format cannot keep is left out, and a Sine LFO is written as Triangle; [Export](export.md) lists those kinds.
- It is refused, and writes nothing, with a reason such as `STOP THE TRANSPORT FIRST`, `A JOB IS RUNNING` or `CARD IS WRITE PROTECTED`.
- If the project changes during the export, it ends with `MODIFIED` and no `project.mt`. A full card, a cancel (`diag ogexp cancel`, or `F8` under the overlay of the OG PROJECT row) or a lost card or power can do the same. Every file with a final name is whole, loading such a folder says **NO PROJECT FILE**, and the unit never removes a folder.
- The files use the original firmware's formats, checked byte for byte by tests. An official unit has not opened them yet.

The EXPORT page's **OG PROJECT** row starts the same export from the screen: see [Export](export.md).  Not yet checked on the unit.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | PROJECTS | EXPORT | `Shift`, PROJECTS | `Shift`, IMPORT and EXPORT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **OPEN** | **EXPORT** | **0/4** | **0/4** |
| `F2` | **RESCAN** | (blank) | **1/4** | **1/4** |
| `F3` | **NEW** | (blank) | **2/4** | **2/4** |
| `F4` | **SAVE** | **SAVE** | **3/4** | **3/4** |
| `F5` | **SAVE AS** | **SAVE AS** | **END** | **END** |
| `F6` | **IMPORT** | **IMPORT** | **NAME** | **NAME** |
| `F7` | **EXPORT** | **PROJECTS** | **PURGE** | - |
| `F8` | - | (blank) | - | - |

The table shows the PROJECTS and EXPORT pages. The IMPORT page (`F6`) has a key row of its own, which changes while you use it, so it is not in the table. `F1` reads **ENTER** while the cursor is on a folder and **IMPORT** on a file. `F2` is **RESCAN**, `F3` **UP**, `F4` **SAVE**, `F5` **SAVE AS** and `F6` **PROJECTS**. `F7` shows the engine the module's commands go to: **FX AUTO**, **FX AMIGA** or **FX MODRN**. `F8` is **REPORT**, and **LIST** while the report is open. Its Shift row is the last column.

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` (**OPEN**) | opens the project under the cursor. It asks first when there are unsaved changes | QA-FIL-012 |
| `F2` (**RESCAN**) | reads the card's folder again and lists the projects anew. When it is done the strip says how many items it found: **READ AGAIN: 5 ITEMS** | QA-FIL-112 |
| `F3` (**NEW**) | asks which new project. `F3` again is **ALL**. `F1` is **KEEP INSTRUMENTS** | QA-FIL-070, QA-FIL-071 |
| `F4` (**SAVE**) | saves the project | QA-FIL-072 |
| `F5` (**SAVE AS**) | saves under a new name | QA-FIL-061 |
| `F6` (**IMPORT**) | opens the IMPORT page. Its keys are in the note above the table; the page itself is not described in this manual yet | QA-FIL-003 |
| `F7` (**EXPORT**) | opens the EXPORT page. Its keys are in the EXPORT column above; the page is described in [Export](export.md) | QA-FIL-020 |
| `Shift` + `F1` to `F4` (**0/4** to **3/4**) | move the cursor to a quarter of the list | QA-FIL-002 |
| `Shift` + `F5` (**END**) | moves the cursor to the last project | QA-FIL-002 |
| `Shift` + `F6` (**NAME**) | names the project | QA-FIL-060 |
| `Shift` + `F7` (**PURGE**) | removes unused instruments. On PROJECTS only | QA-FIL-037, QA-FIL-041 |
| `Shift` + `Up`, `Shift` + `Down` | move one page of 16 rows | QA-FIL-013 |
| `Delete` | marks the project deleted. It asks first | QA-FIL-032 |
| `Left`, `Right` | move between the **RECENT** rows and the list | QA-FIL-035 |
| `F8` | blank on the PROJECTS page | docs/ui/ui-map.md |

## Good to know

- The pads play the current instrument while you hold them, on every page of File except the on-screen keyboard and the dialogs.
- In a long list a quick spin of the encoder moves 4 rows a detent, then 8; a slow turn moves one, and the cursor stops at the ends. `Shift` + turn the encoder still moves a page. New in track3r-os.
- The EXPORT page stays open when you leave File, and a second export set starts at once; `F7` there goes back to PROJECTS.
- If the name is taken, the keyboard stays open and the strip says **A PROJECT OF THAT NAME EXISTS: TYPE ANOTHER**.
- If you pull the card, the strip says **CARD REMOVED** and the project keeps playing. A running save ends with **SAVE ... FAILED: NO CARD**. Putting the card back saves nothing.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- You cannot rename a project folder on the unit: use **SAVE AS**, then delete the old folder.
- The open project has a small square bullet left of its folder icon, in the list and in its **RECENT** row. A new project with no folder has none. New in the Community OS.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- A name longer than 32 characters is cut in the middle: the first 25 characters, a **~**, then the last 6, so names that differ at the end stay apart. The card keeps the full name. New in the Community OS.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- **RECENT** lists the last five projects you opened or saved, newest first. It is kept on the card, and a deleted project is not shown.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- If you change a sample file on a computer, the next save writes the project's sample again and keeps the replaced file as, for example, `instr01.wav.bak`.  Not yet checked on the unit.
- Not yet checked on the unit: saving, saving as, naming, a new project and deleting.

## See also

- [Export](export.md): the EXPORT page: WAV files, stems and the OG PROJECT folder.
- [USB disk](usb_disk.md): the card on a computer, at power-on or while the unit plays.
- [Getting started](getting_started.md): the first start, and turning the unit off.
- [Sample load](sample_load.md): bring a sample into an instrument.
- [Computer tools](computer_tools.md): the diag console.

# USB disk

Status: draft

The card can go to a computer as a disk. There are two ways. Hold `Shift`, `F1` and `F7` while you turn the unit on, and the unit does nothing but show its card. Or use the **CARD AS DISK** row in `Config`, and the unit keeps playing while the computer has the card. New in track3r-os.

## What it is for

Use it to copy samples, modules and projects to and from the card without taking it out of the unit. Use the power-on way when you only want the files. Use the `Config` way when you want to copy while a pattern plays, or while you record and mix.

## How it works

A card has one owner at a time: the unit or the computer. While the computer owns it, the unit never touches it. This is why the two ways differ in what the unit still does.

- **At power-on**, the unit loads no project and opens no audio outputs. It is a card reader until you eject.
- **From `Config`**, everything already in memory goes on: your pattern plays, and you can record, edit, mix and use the pads and MIDI. What stops is everything that reads or writes the card: saving, loading, the file and sample lists, exports and modules from the card. They say **CARD ON COMPUTER**.

The card is live on the computer, and nothing of it is stored in the project. The share ends when you eject.

An example: start a loop, give the card to the computer and drop a new sample on it, then eject. The loop never stopped, and the sample is in the list when the card is back.

## Try it

Start with a pattern playing. Connect the unit to the computer with USB.

1. Open `Config`, press `F5` (**USB**) and move down to **CARD AS DISK**.
2. Press `F7`. The strip asks **THE COMPUTER GETS THE CARD: SAVES STOP. F7 AGAIN**.
3. Press `F7` again. After a few seconds the computer lists the card, and the strip says **CARD ON COMPUTER - CONFIG USB: F7 EJECT**. The pattern keeps playing.
4. On the computer, copy a file to the card, then eject the disk.
5. The strip says **READING CARD** and then **CARD READY**. The card is the unit's again.

The computer could only read the card in this walk, because **READ ONLY** starts **On**. To copy to the card, set it to **Off** before step 2 (see below).

## More tasks

### Use the card on a computer at power-on

Start with the unit off and connected to the computer with USB.

1. Hold `Shift`, `F1` and `F7` together while you turn the unit on, until the strip shows **USB DISK - EJECT ON THE COMPUTER OR PRESS A KEY**. Do not hold `F8` as well: with `F8` down the **INPUT TEST** screen opens instead.
2. Let go. The computer lists the card as a disk it can read and write.
3. When you are done, eject the disk on the computer, then press a key on the unit.

The strip says **DISK EJECTED - PRESS ANY KEY TO RESTART**, and the unit restarts with the card in place. If the computer has not ejected the disk, the first key only warns: **THE COMPUTER MAY STILL BE WRITING: KEY AGAIN**. Press a key again within 5 seconds to restart. A restart during a copy waits up to 3 seconds for the write in progress (**FINISHING THE LAST WRITE - RESTARTING**).

> **Careful**: eject the disk on the computer before you unplug the cable. The computer may hold writes it has not sent yet, and a restart in the middle of a copy can leave the computer's file system to repair.

### Let the computer write to the card while the unit plays

Start on `Config`, on the USB page (`F5`).

1. Move down to **READ ONLY**. **On** (the start value) lets the computer read the card only. **Off** lets it write too.
2. Turn the encoder to **Off**. The choice stays in memory until the unit restarts, is not saved with anything, and holds for several shares in a row.
3. Go back to **CARD AS DISK** and share the card as in Try it.

Once you have shared the card, **READ ONLY** is fixed until you eject: the strip says **EJECT THE CARD TO CHANGE IT**. While the card changes hands it says **THE CARD IS CHANGING HANDS: WAIT**.

### Get the card back from the computer

Eject the disk on the computer, or press `F7` twice on the **CARD AS DISK** row. The unit warns first (**THE COMPUTER MAY STILL BE WRITING: F7 AGAIN**), because a copy still running is cut. The strip then says **READING CARD** and **CARD READY**. A card marked as not closed properly gives **CARD NOT EJECTED PROPERLY: CHECK THE COMPUTER**, and everything still works. An exFAT card shows **EXFAT CARD: READ ONLY**: the unit can read it but not save to it. The unit never lists names that start with a dot or the **System Volume Information** folder.

> **Careful**: eject on the computer before you unplug the cable. If you unplug without ejecting, the card stays with the computer until you take it back with `F7` twice.

### See what the unit refuses while the card is out

- Saving, loading, the file and sample lists, exports and modules from the card say **CARD ON COMPUTER**, and so do File `F1` (OPEN), `Delete` and `F7` (EXPORT), Sample load `F4` (ADD) and `F5` (PLAY) and the instrument LOAD. The refusal comes up on the strip at once.  A change to your settings is kept in memory and written when you get the card back. Recording works, but saving the take as a WAV file waits.
- **NO CARD** or **STOP THE EXPORT FIRST** at the first `F7` means nothing was started. **CARD BUSY: WAIT FOR THE SAVE** means a save was still running.
- In USB AUDIO mode the strip says **USB AUDIO PAUSES** until you eject.

> **Careful**: settings you change while the card is out are only in memory. If you switch the unit off before you get the card back, they are lost.

## Good to know

- Tested on Linux only. Windows and macOS are untested.
- Checked on a unit (test build v0.6.10): the power-on way, its strip, the eject and the restart, and unmounting and mounting the card on the computer.
- Not yet checked on the unit: the **CARD AS DISK** row. It is built and tested on the build computer only.
- A bench run wrote to one SD card at about 430 KiB/s. That is the rate of the unit's card writes on that card, not a speed you will see copying files, and it was measured on one card brand.

## See also

- [File](file.md): projects, saving and loading, which the card needs back.
- [Config](config.md): the USB page, where **CARD AS DISK** and **READ ONLY** are.
- [Getting started](getting_started.md#use-the-card-on-a-computer): the power-on way in the first-start steps.
- [Panel](panel.md#keys-held-when-the-unit-turns-on): the keys held at power-on.

---

# Modules

Status: draft

Modules are files on the card that add to the OS without a firmware update: sound engines for instrument slots, and apps that edit the pattern or show you what the unit is doing. The TB-303, Chip and FM engines are built in and need no card; every other module is a `.tmod` file. The **MODULES** screen lists the apps. Module instruments and apps are new in track3r-os.

## What it is for

Use a module instrument when a slot should be a synth, not a sample: pick it with `F4` (**MODULE**) on the Instrument screen. Use an app for a job on the pattern, such as a Euclidean rhythm, humanizing, or a MIDI monitor. Open the screen from the Navigator: `Shift` + `Pattern`, then **MODULES**.

## How it works

### Three kinds of module

A `.tmod` file is an **instrument** (a sound engine, one voice a track), an **effect** or an **app** (a small program with its own page). The folder says which: `modules/instruments`, `modules/effects`, `modules/apps`. The file name, without `.tmod`, is the module's name everywhere.

An effect module is read by the loader, but this version has no slot to run it, so it does nothing yet.

### A module instrument: live, stored and ended

- **Live:** the slot sounds as the module's engine. Its pages and values show on the Instrument screen, and the encoder changes them while you play.
- **Stored:** the project keeps the module's name and the values of its parameters. The `.tmod` file stays on the card. A module that the card does not have mutes the instruments that name it.
- **Ended:** `Shift` + `F4` (**DELETE**) stops its sound at once, and `F8` twice brings it back.

Example: put the TB-303 in slot 4, write a line on a track, then add a Glide to the second note. The pitch slides from the first note, as a legato note, in the Glide time. See [Step FX on module instruments](module-instrument-fx.md).

### An app: live, stored and ended

- **Live:** an app has its own page while it runs. Its key row shows its own labels. `Play` still starts the transport, and the app never sees it.
- **Stored:** the app's own rows are kept with the project (the last 12 apps): a change to them survives leaving the app, a relaunch, and a save and load. `Delete` puts a row's default back, and that is kept too. A value the project has not kept reads the app's default. The target rows (pattern, track, row and instrument) are not kept. What an app writes into a pattern is ordinary pattern data, and the edit is undoable.
- **Ended:** `F8` (**BACK**), a screen button, or `F7` + `F8` together, which leaves even a hung app.

Example: open Rhythm Gen from `F7` (**TOOLS**) on Pattern. It starts at your cursor, builds a rhythm with its rows, and **APPLY** writes it into the pattern. `F8` on Pattern takes it back.

An app asks before its first launch of a boot when it edits the project or writes files: `F1` reads **LAUNCH?** and the strip says what it will do. Press `F1` again to start it. An app that only listens asks nothing.

## Try it

1. Open the Modules screen from the Navigator, and press `F2` (**RESCAN**). The apps on the card are listed, each with its state, and the strip says how many it found, for example **READ AGAIN: 11 APPS**.

   (Picture: Modules: the apps on the card, each LOADED, with LAUNCH and RESCAN on the keys.)

2. Put the cursor on **midimon** and press `F1` (**LAUNCH**). It only listens, so it starts at once.

   (Picture: MIDI Monitor: the app's page, with its own key labels and BACK on F8.)

3. Press `F8` (**BACK**). You are on the list again.
4. Put the cursor on **rhythmgen** and press `F1`. It edits the project, so `F1` reads **LAUNCH?** and the strip asks.

   (Picture: Modules: the cursor on rhythmgen, F1 reads LAUNCH? and the strip says EDITS THE PROJECT.)

5. Press `F1` again. Rhythm Gen starts.

   (Picture: Rhythm Gen: the app's rows and its key labels.)

6. Press `Song`. The app ends and the Song screen opens.

Not yet checked on the unit.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Modules: the apps on the card with their state, the apps refused this boot at the right, and LAUNCH and RESCAN on the keys.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Main area | The apps on the card, 16 rows at a time, each with its state: **ON CARD**, **LOADED**, **QUARANTINED** (refused this boot) or **MISSING** (the project names the app and the card does not have it). At the right, **QUARANTINED THIS BOOT** lists the apps the unit refused, each with the reason. |
| Strip | The message line, for example **NEEDS NEWER OS** for an app too new for your track3r-os.  |
| Key row | `F1` (**LAUNCH**) and `F2` (**RESCAN**). |
| Shift row | Blank. No key is bound to `Shift` + `F1` to `F8` here. |

## More tasks

### Open the Modules screen

Start on any screen.

1. Hold `Shift` and press `Pattern`. The Navigator opens.
2. Turn the encoder until **MODULES** is shown.
3. Press `F8` (**GO**).

You should see the list of apps on the card.

### Put a module in an instrument slot

Start on the Instrument screen, on a free slot.

1. Press `F4` (**MODULE**). The picker opens and lists the instrument modules on the card.
2. Turn the encoder to a module. `Shift` + `Down` and `Shift` + `Up` move ten rows at a time.
3. Press `F1` to choose it.

You should see **ENGINE SET** in the strip. The slot now holds the module as its instrument. The choice is one undo step: press `F8` (**UNDO**) to take it back.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Find the controls of a module instrument

Start on the Instrument screen of a module instrument, for example the TB-303.

1. Press `F1` to `F4` to choose a page.

The key row and the page heading show the module's page names. The TB-303 has **SOUND** and **MODS**. The Chip has **TONE**, **ENV**, **PITCH** and **ARP**. The FM has **OP1** to **OP4**. Keys past the last page, and `F5`, are blank, and a blank key does nothing. The **PAGE** field in the header counts the module's pages: `P1` and `P2` on the TB-303, `P1` to `P4` on the Chip and the FM. A module without named pages shows `1-8`, `9-16` and so on.

2. Turn the encoder to change a value.

Some values show a name instead of a number. The Chip's wave shows **PULSE**, **TRIANGLE**, **NOISE LONG** or **NOISE SHORT**. Its duty shows 12.5%, 25%, 50% or 75%. The FM's algorithm shows a routing such as `4>3>2>1`. The side pane gives the range in names too.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Launch an app on the pattern you are editing

Start on the Pattern screen, with the cursor on the track and row you want to work on.

1. Press `F7` (**TOOLS**). The list holds **EXPORT PATTERN** and the tool apps, sorted by name.
2. Choose an app and press `F1`. The app opens with its rows set to your cursor: pattern, track and row.

The rows PATTERN, TRACK, ROW and ROWS (TRACKS on Humanize and Chords) are the target. In Rhythm Gen they are on the last page, reached with `Right`; in Chords, on the second page. Press `Down` to a row and turn the encoder. `Shift` + the encoder takes the coarse step. The encoder moves one step and stops at the ends of the pattern. `Delete` puts the value you opened on back. A pattern that does not exist reads **(EMPTY)**, and **APPLY** says so. **APPLY** writes at the track and rows the page shows, and nowhere else. After `F8` the rows read the cursor again. Opened from the Modules screen there is no cursor, and the rows are dim dashes.

Mutate and Morph work on a whole instrument instead. Their last row, **INSTRUMENT** (**INSTRUMENT A** on Morph), starts as the Pattern's current instrument. Turn the encoder to pick another one, 1 to 64, and the page shows that instrument's parameters. A slot that is not a sample or module instrument says **SAMPLE OR MODULE INSTRUMENTS ONLY**. `Delete` puts back the instrument you opened on, and **APPLY** changes the instrument the row shows.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### See what each shipped app does

Every app page answers the same keys. `Up` and `Down` choose a row, the encoder changes its value, `Shift` + the encoder takes the coarse step, `Delete` puts the row's default back, and where an app has pages, `Left` and `Right` change the page: Rhythm Gen, Chords (a second page) and Tap Calc (the Hz page).

| App | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| Tap Calc | Tap any pad or `F1` to measure a tempo. The BPM is the mean of the last 4 to 8 intervals between taps, so 5 to 9 taps (the AVERAGE row, 8 by default), from 20.0 to 300.0. A pause over 2 seconds starts a new series. The encoder sets the BPM by hand. `Right` shows the same notes as LFO rates in Hz. `Delete` on the BPM row goes back to 120.0 and forgets the taps. `F2` sets the project's tempo, which one undo takes back. Under 40.0 BPM it refuses. | QA-MOD-003, QA-MOD-004, QA-MOD-005, QA-MOD-006, QA-MOD-007, QA-MOD-008 |
| MIDI Monitor | Lists the MIDI that arrives on DIN and USB, newest line first, eight lines at most. A strip of 16 channel cells lights for a moment on each message. The CHANNEL and TYPE rows filter the list. `Insert` or `F1` pauses it, and `F2` (**CLEAR**) empties it. SysEx is counted, not shown. It makes no sound. | QA-MOD-010, QA-MOD-011, QA-MOD-012, QA-MOD-013, QA-MOD-014, QA-MOD-015, QA-MOD-016 |
| Loudness VU | PEAK and RMS bars in dBFS, a clip lamp with a CLIPS count, and a 24 second RMS history. The SOURCE row picks `2` MASTER (what you hear) or `1` INPUT (the line input). The HOLD row keeps the highest peak for 1 to 10 seconds. `F1` (**CLEAR**) resets the clip count, HOLD and MAX. | QA-MOD-017, QA-MOD-018, QA-MOD-019, QA-MOD-020, QA-MOD-021 |
| Tuner | Reads a held note between 30 Hz and 2.1 kHz: the note name, **FREQ**, **CENTS** and a needle, which is in tune within 5 cents. The A4 row sets the reference from 415 to 466 Hz (440 by default). SOURCE picks INPUT or MASTER. With no clear pitch it says **NO SIGNAL**. | QA-MOD-024, QA-MOD-025, QA-MOD-026, QA-MOD-027 |
| Scope Spectrum | VIEW `1` draws the wave, steady on a trigger. TIMEBASE sets the span from 2.9 to 34.8 ms. VIEW `2` draws 48 spectrum bars from 40 Hz to 20 kHz with the **PEAK** frequency under them. SOURCE picks INPUT or MASTER. | QA-MOD-028, QA-MOD-029, QA-MOD-030, QA-MOD-031, QA-MOD-032 |
| SMF Export | Open it from `F7` (**TOOLS**) on Pattern. `F1` writes the pattern, or the block, as a MIDI file in `AppExport/smfexport/` on the card. A file is never replaced: the next ones are `PAT001_001.mid` and so on. It lists the FX it cannot write. | QA-MOD-092, QA-MOD-093, QA-MOD-094, QA-MOD-096 |
| Rhythm Gen, Humanize, Chords, Mutate, Morph | The pattern tools. See [Pattern tools](pattern_tools.md). Rhythm Gen plays a lane's hits while you turn the encoder. After **APPLY** and `F8` in Rhythm Gen, Humanize or Chords, the Pattern has the cursor on the first step written and the written block selected. Mutate and Morph change instrument parameters, not steps. | QA-MOD-129, QA-MOD-131 |

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Copy a module to the card

Back up the card first. See [Installing track3r-os](install.md).

1. Get the `.tmod` file. The apps of a release come in `track3r-os-<version>-apps.zip`, in the release `apps-v<version>` on the Releases page: unpack it into the root of the card and the files land in `modules/apps`. Otherwise copy the `.tmod` file to the card. An app goes in the `modules/apps` folder. An instrument module goes in `modules/instruments`. An effect module goes in `modules/effects`.
2. Put the card in the unit.
3. For an app, press `F2` (**RESCAN**) on the Modules screen.

**RESCAN** reads the apps again, and the strip says how many it found (**READ AGAIN: 3 APPS**). It does not touch the engine picker. The picker reads the card each time you open it, so a new instrument module shows there without a rescan. The TB-303, Chip and FM are built into the firmware and are listed with no card.

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **LAUNCH** | - |
| `F2` | **RESCAN** | - |
| `F3` | - | - |
| `F4` | - | - |
| `F5` | - | - |
| `F6` | - | - |
| `F7` | - | - |
| `F8` | - | - |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `Shift` + `Pattern` (Navigator), then the encoder to **MODULES**, then `F8` (**GO**) | opens the Modules screen | QA-MOD-002 |
| `F1` (**LAUNCH**) | starts the app under the cursor | QA-MOD-002 |
| `F2` (**RESCAN**) | looks at the card again. The strip says how many apps it found: **READ AGAIN: 3 APPS** | QA-MOD-001, QA-MOD-157 |
| `Up`, `Down` | move one row | QA-MOD-060 |
| `Shift` + `Up`, `Shift` + `Down` | move one page of 16 rows. They stop at the first and last row and do not wrap. | QA-MOD-060 |
| `Shift` + `F1` to `F8` | nothing | QA-MOD-001 |
| `F8` on an app's page | leaves the app and returns to the Modules screen | QA-MOD-121 |
| A screen button (`Song`, `Params`, `File` ...) on an app's page | leaves the app and opens that screen; the settings of the app stay with the project | QA-MOD-128 |
| `F7` + `F8` together | leaves an app, even a hung one | QA-MOD-009 |

The engine picker, on the Instrument screen:

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F4` (**MODULE**) on a free slot | opens the picker | QA-INS-029 |
| `Shift` + `Down`, `Shift` + `Up` | move ten rows at a time. They stop at the ends. | QA-MOD-061 |
| `F1` | chooses the module the cursor is on (**ENGINE SET**) | QA-INS-029 |
| `F8` | closes the picker with no choice | QA-INS-208 |

## Good to know

- While the picker is open, the other keys do nothing. `Pattern` does not leave the Instrument screen.
- A module instrument cannot be copied. `Shift` + `F2` (**COPY**) says **A MODULE INSTRUMENT CANNOT BE COPIED**.
- A paste onto a slot that holds a module does nothing. The strip says **INS nn IS A MODULE: DELETE IT FIRST**, where `nn` is the slot number. Press `Shift` + `F4` (**DELETE**) first.
- `SAVE` works for sample instruments only. On a module instrument the strip says **SAMPLE INSTRUMENTS ONLY**, and the card is not changed.
- Deleting a module instrument with `Shift` + `F4` stops its sound. `F4` (**MODULE**) then says **RELOAD TO PUT A MODULE HERE**. Press `F8` twice to bring the module back.
- A module built for an older track3r-os ignores Glide and Slide. Its notes play as ordinary notes.
- Glide, Slide up and Slide down change the pitch of a module instrument. Arp plays only with a Chord in the other FX column. Chord alone plays the root. See [Step FX on module instruments](module-instrument-fx.md).

Not yet checked on the unit: the picker, the pages, the value names, the apps' kept rows, the target rows and the count after **RESCAN**.

# TB-303, FM and Chip: new parameters

Status: draft

The TB-303 has a second page, **MODS**, with a tuning, an octave shift, an accent threshold, filter tracking and an accent decay. The FM has sixteen algorithms instead of eight, and a Detune that reaches a whole octave either way. The Chip's wave and duty can now follow a MIDI controller. All of this is new in track3r-os. A project saved earlier sounds the same, because every new value starts where the old sound is.

## What it is for

Come here when a built-in sound needs more than its first page gives. Examples are a bass line that must match the tuning of a song, accents on only the hardest notes, or an FM bell that is not a whole-number multiple of the note. You reach everything on the Instrument screen of a module instrument. To put a module in a slot, see [Modules](modules.md).

## How it works

### Old projects keep their sound

A project stores the values of a module in a fixed order. The new values come after the old ones. If a project holds fewer values than the module has now, the module keeps its own starting values for the rest. Those starting values leave the old sound unchanged. There is no tuning, no transposition and no tracking. An accent starts at velocity 100 and its decay is 200 ms. When you change a new value, it is saved with the project from then on.

### The TB-303's MODS page

Press `F2` (**MODS**) on the Instrument screen of a TB-303. The page starts with **LEGATO SLIDE**, which was on the second page before. The page then lists five new values: **TUNE**, **TRANSPOSE**, **ACC THRESH**, **FILTER TRACK** and **ACC DECAY**. The first page, **SOUND**, now holds eight rows, from **WAVEFORM** to **VOLUME**.

**TUNE** moves the pitch of the next note by up to 100 cents (a cent is a hundredth of a semitone). **TRANSPOSE** moves it by up to 24 semitones. A note that is already sounding keeps its pitch until the next note starts. With both at 0 the pitch is the old one.

### Accents: ACC THRESH and ACC DECAY

On a 303 an accent is a note played harder than the rest. Here an accented note is louder and opens the filter further, by the amount of the **ACCENT** value on the **SOUND** page. The filter then falls back on its own time. A note is an accent when its velocity is **ACC THRESH** or more. The start value is 100.

A step's volume sets the velocity, up to 127. A step with no volume plays at velocity 96, so at the start value it is plain. Set **ACC THRESH** to 90 and every note from 90 up is an accent. Set it to 127 and only the hardest notes are.

**ACC DECAY** is the time that filter fall takes on an accented note, 30 to 2000 ms. The start value, 200 ms, is the time the TB-303 always had. A plain note keeps the time of **DECAY**. Both values act on the next note.

### Filter tracking

On the **SOUND** page, **CUTOFF** is one fixed frequency for every note. With **FILTER TRACK** above 0 %, the cutoff follows the pitch of the note instead: high notes open the filter, low notes close it. At 100 % it follows by one octave for every octave of the note, measured from MIDI note 48 (the C below middle C). At 50 % it follows by half as much.

The factor is set when a note starts, and a note that is already sounding keeps its filter. During a slide the factor moves with the pitch, so the filter glides to the new note with it. At 0 % the cutoff is the knob, as before.

This is new in track3r-os: the reference note is a choice of this OS, not a measurement of any other 303.

### FM: sixteen algorithms and a wide Detune

The FM has four operators, which are four sine waves. A modulator is an operator that bends the pitch of another one. A carrier is an operator you hear. The algorithm says which operators modulate which. `4>3>2>1` means 4 modulates 3, 3 modulates 2 and 2 modulates 1, and only 1 is heard. See the [glossary](glossary.md).

**ALGORITHM** on the **OP1** page now runs from 1 to 16. The first eight are unchanged, so a saved project plays the same algorithm. Algorithms 9 to 16 add new shapes. One has three modulators feeding one carrier (`4+3+2>1`). One has two modulators feeding two carriers (`(4+3)>(2+1)`). One mixes a chain with a free carrier (`4>2>1 + 3`). The Algorithm view draws each one. The value and the view's title spell it the same way, for example **ALG 14  (4+3)>(2+1)**.

**DETUNE** on each operator page now reaches 1200 cents up or down, one octave each way. It was 100 cents. A detune of 600 cents puts a modulator at about 1.41 times its note. Whole-number ratios cannot reach that, and it is the colour of a bell. Hold `Shift` and turn the encoder to move in steps of 10 cents. A MIDI Learn binding you saved on a Detune row now sweeps the wider range (24 times the old one), and Relative mode counts more detents. The values you stored sound the same.

### Chip: wave and duty from a controller

**WAVE** and **DUTY** can now be bound to a MIDI controller with Learn (`Vol` and `Fx` together, see [The panel](panel.md)). Turning the controller steps through the four waves or the four duties. Before, these two rows refused Learn.

Not yet checked on the unit: everything in this chapter.

## Try it

This walk-through uses a TB-303 in an instrument slot and a pattern with a short bass line over two octaves. A few steps have a volume of 95.

1. Press `Play` to hear the line as it is. Press `Params`, then `F2` (**MODS**). Press `Down` until the cursor is on **TRANSPOSE** and turn the encoder to 12. The next notes sound an octave higher.
2. Put **TRANSPOSE** back to 0. Move the cursor to **ACC THRESH** and turn the encoder to 90. The steps with volume 95 now sound as accents.
3. Move the cursor to **ACC DECAY**. Set 30 ms for a short blip, then 800 ms for a long sweep.
4. Press `F1` (**SOUND**), move the cursor to **RESONANCE** and set 70.
5. Press `F2`, move the cursor to **FILTER TRACK** and set 100 %.

You should hear the high notes open up and the low notes close in.

## Parameters at a glance

| Module | Value | Range | Starts at | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TB-303 | **TUNE** | -100 to 100 cents | 0 | QA-MOD-145 |
| TB-303 | **TRANSPOSE** | -24 to 24 semitones | 0 | QA-MOD-145 |
| TB-303 | **ACC THRESH** | 1 to 127 | 100 | QA-MOD-146 |
| TB-303 | **FILTER TRACK** | 0 to 100 % | 0 | QA-MOD-147 |
| TB-303 | **ACC DECAY** | 30 to 2000 ms | 200 | QA-MOD-148 |
| FM | **ALGORITHM** | 1 to 16 (was 1 to 8) | 5 | QA-MOD-149 |
| FM | **DETUNE** (each operator) | -1200 to 1200 cents (was -100 to 100) | 0, 0, 4, 0 | QA-MOD-150 |
| Chip | **WAVE**, **DUTY** | can be learned | as before | QA-MOD-141 |

## Good to know

- The five TB-303 values act on the next note, not on a note that is sounding. **ACC DECAY** acts on the next accented note.
- Transposing a note past the top or the bottom of the MIDI range holds it at the end of the range.
- None of the new TB-303 values can be driven by the modulation matrix.
- A MIDI controller bound to **DETUNE** sweeps the whole 2400 cents. Hold `Shift` while turning the encoder for steps of 10 cents.

## See also

- [Modules](modules.md): putting a module in an instrument slot, and finding its pages.
- [Step FX on module instruments](module-instrument-fx.md): which effects a module instrument obeys.
- [The panel](panel.md): where `Vol`, `Fx` and `Shift` are.

# Step FX on module instruments

Status: draft

A module instrument obeys fewer step FX than a sampler, and it obeys Glide, Slide and Arp in its own way: a slide is a legato note, not a restarted sample. This page lists which step FX the TB-303, Chip, FM and any instrument `.tmod` of the current ABI obey. Tune works on modules; Micro-tune, the Finetune LFO and tracker FX 46, 49 and 50 act on sampler or Amiga voices only. New in track3r-os.

## What it is for

Come here when a pattern with FX sounds different on a module instrument than on a sample. The FX stay in the pattern as written; nothing changes in them when the instrument is a module. Step FX themselves are in [Effects in the pattern](fx.md).

## What a module instrument does with step FX

The Sampler column is what the FX specs say; the module column is checked on the host (event stream and exact ramps). Not yet checked on the unit.

| FX | Sampler instrument | Module instrument | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Glide (19) | slides the pitch from the previous note | the note is **legato** (no new envelope) and its pitch slides from the previous note of the track in the Glide time; the first note of a track, a repeat of the same note after a release and a Glide of 0 are ordinary notes; the same note while it sounds is a tie | host tests; unit open |
| Slide up (41), Slide down (42) | slide the pitch | the pitch slides to the distance (sixteenths of a semitone) in one step of the tempo, as a legato note; on a row with no note the sounding note slides from where it is; a Slide beats a Glide; a Slide of 0 changes nothing; the end of the FX puts the note's pitch back | host tests; unit open |
| Arp (21) | plays the arpeggio | **plays the arpeggio**, but only with a Chord (14) in the other FX column (as on a sampler): each tone is a new, retriggered note. An Arp alone does nothing | host test of the event stream (OS-MODPITCH step 1); unit open. Earlier text that said Arp had no effect on a module was an FX-column mistake |
| Chord (14) | plays the root alone | plays the root alone (a module is one voice a track); use CHORDS in SPREAD mode for a chord | `QA-MOD-083` |
| Overdrive (38), Bit depth (39) | drive and bit reduction of the voice | the same curves over the module's output: the drive gain 1 + 15 (v / 100)^2, the depth cuts the low 16 minus bits bits; a value of 0 (Overdrive) or 16 (Bit depth) changes nothing; the Perform OVERDRV and BITDEPTH rows win over the FX | host tests (`QA-MOD-200..205`); unit open |
| Chance (4), Micro-move (2) | as in the Pattern chapter | not verified either way | open research question |

## Notes

- A module of ABI 1.7 or below, or a 1.8 module that does not export `pitch`, ignores Glide and Slide as before; the notes are ordinary notes.
- The TB-303's own Slide and Legato Slide parameters are for live legato keys; on a pattern note the slide time comes from the Glide value or the Slide speed.
- The FX stay in the pattern as written; nothing is changed by the instrument being a module.
- Overdrive (FX 38), Bit depth (FX 39) and the Perform OVERDRV and BITDEPTH rows shape a module instrument's sound exactly as they shape a sampler's: the same curves, applied to the module's output after its own filter. New in track3r-os.
- A module instrument has no OVERDRIVE or BIT DEPTH row of its own: its Params page shows only the module's parameters, so the amount comes from the FX or the Perform rows. Without one of them the sound is the module's, untouched.
- The shaping is applied once per audio block (about 1.45 ms) with the values in force at the end of the block, so an FX can start up to one block early, on the tail of the previous note. The Stopped state does not end a held FX 38 or 39 (as on a sampler); the next FxReset does.
- The shaping costs processor time for each shaped module track (about 0.2 to 0.5 % of the budget each, estimated; the measurement on the unit is open). It also narrows how many module notes the engine admits at once, for every module, while it runs. The export (PATT STEMS and the song export) hears the same shaping as playback, except that the Perform rows are off during an export, as for sampler tracks.

## See also

- [Effects in the pattern](fx.md): how to put an effect on a step.
- [Modules](modules.md): module instruments and apps.
- [TB-303, FM and Chip: new parameters](module-sounds.md): the built-in sounds.
