# Config

Status: draft

Config holds the unit's settings on six pages. Three things are new in track3r-os: the USB page can turn the audio device and the audio return off, CARD AS DISK hands the card to a computer while the unit plays on, and the metronome can click on the Main outputs with a count-in of one or two bars.  The rest of the PATTERN page differs from the official manual. The metronome has no time-signature rows. Live recording has the rows REC MICRO and REC VELOCITY. PAD OFFSET sets how the pad rows overlap, while the root and scale come from the held Note panel. PAT SWITCH chooses whether a pattern picked with `F1` held lands at the next step or at the end of the pattern.  A change to USB AUDIO or USB RETURN waits until you press `F7` (**APPLY**) twice, and `Shift` + `F7` puts a page back to its defaults. Not checked against the original firmware: the pages and keys.

## What it is for

Use the Config screen to change the unit's settings. Press `Config` to open it. It has six pages, one for each of `F1` to `F6`: MIDI, DISPLAY, SD, INFO, USB and PATTERN. This chapter covers the MIDI, DISPLAY, USB and PATTERN pages and the keys that work on every page. The SD and INFO pages have no rows to set. The SD page shows what the card reports (CARD, MOUNTED, FILE SYSTEM, CAPACITY and CLUSTER). Not yet checked on the unit.  The USB page also has the **CARD AS DISK** row, which gives the card to a computer while the unit keeps playing, and the **READ ONLY** row beside it: see [USB disk](usb_disk.md). The INFO page has one key, `F8` (**UPDATE**), which installs a new firmware from the card.

## How it works

A Config row is a setting of the unit, not of the project. Load another project and the rows stay as they are: they are kept in the unit's settings file on the card. The one exception is READ ONLY on the USB page, which is for this session only and is not saved.

Most rows are live. Turn the encoder and the change takes effect at once, with nothing to confirm: RETURN LEVEL moves the level the moment you turn it.  The two USB rows that change what the computer sees, USB AUDIO and USB RETURN, are different. The encoder only sets a pending value, marked with a star (\*). Nothing is written and the computer notices nothing until you press `F7` (**APPLY**) twice, because applying can make the USB port reconnect. Leaving the page, or turning to another page, throws a pending value away.

Example: set METRO to Cue and COUNT-IN to 1 bar, and the next live take starts with a click. Both rows are live and are kept until you change them. Set USB AUDIO to Off and press `F1` instead of `F7`, and the unit forgets it.

## Try it

This walk-through changes a live row, then shows a pending one that is dropped.

1. Press `Config`.
2. Press `F6` (**PATTERN**). The nine rows of the page show.

   (Picture: Config, PATTERN page: the nine rows, the cursor on the first.)
3. Press `Down` four times. The cursor is on METRO. Turn the encoder one click to the right: the row reads **Main**.
4. Turn the encoder two clicks to the left. The row reads **Off**. The Pattern screen's info line loses its METRO chip.

   (Picture: Config, PATTERN page: METRO reads Off.)
5. Press `F5` (**USB**). Turn the encoder one click to the left. USB AUDIO reads **Off\*** and the info line says it is not applied yet.

   (Picture: Config, USB page: USB AUDIO reads Off with a star, not applied.)
6. Press `F1` (**MIDI**), then `F5` again. USB AUDIO reads **On** with no star: the pending value is gone and the computer never noticed.

   (Picture: Config, USB page: USB AUDIO reads On again, with no star.)

METRO stays **Off** until you change it. Press `Delete` on the METRO row to put **Cue** back.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: Config, PATTERN page: the nine rows, from REC POLY to PAT SWITCH, with the metronome rows in the middle.)

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Main area | The rows of the page. Each row has a name and a value. |
| Info line | Notes about the page or a pending change. On PATTERN it says **live recording, metronome and pads**. |
| Strip | The message line, for example **USB RECONNECTING**. |
| Key row | `F1` to `F6` choose a page. `F7` is **APPLY** (blank on the SD and INFO pages, which have nothing to apply). On the INFO page, `F8` is **UPDATE**: it opens the firmware update dialog (new, not yet tried on a unit). |
| Shift row | `F7` is **DEFAULTS**. The other keys do nothing. |

## More tasks

### Turn USB AUDIO off, then on

USB AUDIO sets whether the unit shows an audio device to the computer. Off gives **STANDARD**: MIDI and serial only. On is the default, and adds the audio device.

Start on the Config screen. Press `F5` (**USB**).

1. Turn the encoder until USB AUDIO reads **Off**. The row shows a star (\*). The info line says the change is not applied yet.
2. Press `F7` (**APPLY**). The strip says **USB WILL RECONNECT: PRESS AGAIN**, and the key reads **APPLY?**, inverted.
3. Press `F7` (**APPLY?**) again. The strip says **USB RECONNECTING**. The star goes.

(Picture: Config, USB page: after the first APPLY, the strip says USB WILL RECONNECT: PRESS AGAIN.)

The computer sees the unit again, with MIDI and serial but no audio device. To turn USB AUDIO back on, turn the encoder until the row reads **On**, then press `F7` twice. The computer sees the audio device again, named **Track3r Audio**.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Change USB RETURN

The USB return is the stereo stream from the computer to the unit. **On** (the default) adds it. **Off** leaves capture only.

Start on the USB page.

1. Press `Down`. The cursor is on USB RETURN.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **Off**. The row shows a star (\*).
3. Press `F7` (**APPLY**). With USB AUDIO Off, the strip says **PRESS AGAIN TO APPLY**. With USB AUDIO On, it says **USB WILL RECONNECT: PRESS AGAIN**.
4. Press `F7` (**APPLY**) again. With USB AUDIO Off, the strip says **APPLIED**, and the computer sees no change. With USB AUDIO On, the strip says **USB RECONNECTING**, and the computer reconnects once.

The return needs room on the USB bus, so it is off when the unit presents 10 outputs (the Mixer's STEMS page chooses the number). The row then reads **On (10 OUT: off)**, dim. The setting stays On: with 8 outputs or fewer the return is back.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Set RETURN LEVEL

RETURN LEVEL sets how loud the USB return reaches the outputs. **100 %** is the default.

Start on the USB page.

1. Press `Down` twice. The cursor is on RETURN LEVEL.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **90 %**.

You should see **90 %** at once, with no star. `F7` is not needed. Not yet checked on the unit: the level the computer receives.

### Share the card with a computer

CARD AS DISK on the USB page shows the card to a computer while the unit keeps playing. It is new in track3r-os. The steps, the refusals and the safe way to eject are in [File](file.md), in the part about the USB disk.

1. On the USB page, press `Down` until the cursor is on CARD AS DISK, then once more to READ ONLY. It starts at **On**: the computer can read the card but cannot write to it. Turn the encoder to **Off** only if the computer needs to write. The choice is not saved, so READ ONLY is **On** again the next time.
2. Press `Up` to CARD AS DISK, then press `F7` twice. The strip says **CARD ON COMPUTER - CONFIG USB: F7 EJECT**.
3. When you are done, press `F7` on the same row twice more. The strip says **CARD READY**.

`F7` on CARD AS DISK can refuse. The strip says **NO CARD**, **CARD BUSY: WAIT FOR THE SAVE** or **STOP THE EXPORT FIRST**.  While the card is on the computer, SAVE, SAVE AS, OPEN, an export and the sample loads refuse too, and nothing is written. The strip says **CARD ON COMPUTER - EJECT FIRST** (the sample and instrument lists say **CARD ON COMPUTER**).  After the eject, **CARD NOT EJECTED PROPERLY: CHECK THE COMPUTER** shows only when the computer left the card unclean during this share.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Turn the metronome on, off or to Main

The metronome, METRO, plays a click with the beat. It is set on the PATTERN page.

Start on the Config screen. Press `F6` (**PATTERN**).

1. Press `Down` four times. The cursor is on METRO.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **Off**, **Cue** or **Main**.

The default is **Cue**. While OUT MODE on the [Mixer](mixer.md) is Stereo, Cue plays on the Main side, and the row reads **Cue (-> Main)**. **Main** reads **Main** whatever OUT MODE is.  When METRO is **Off**, the Pattern screen's info line loses its METRO chip.

With OUT MODE on **MAIN L / CUE R**, Main plays on the left jack only and Cue on the right jack only.  The click is not in a RESAMPLE take, in the USB stream or in a WAV export.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Set the metronome volume

Start on the PATTERN page, with the cursor on METRO.

1. Press `Down`. The cursor is on METRO VOL.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **80 %**.
3. Press `Delete`. The row reads **50 %**, the default.

Not yet checked on the unit.

### Set the count-in

Start on the PATTERN page. The count-in is the click before a recording starts.

1. Press `Down` six times. The cursor is on COUNT-IN.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **2 bars**. One step of the encoder reads **1 bar**.

You should see **2 bars** on the row. Now press `Shift` + `Rec` on the Pattern screen with the transport stopped. The strip counts and the pads flash each beat, brighter on the first of a bar. The play line waits on row 1 and only the click sounds. Then row 1 plays and recording starts. A pad you hit during the count-in sounds and writes nothing. `Play` never counts in.  Not yet checked on the unit.

### Keep the timing and velocity of live notes

Start on the PATTERN page. These rows apply to LIVE recording (`Shift` + `Rec` on Pattern), not to STEP.

1. Press `Down` twice. The cursor is on REC MICRO. Turn the encoder until the row reads **On**. The hint reads: late notes get m02 in FX2 and early ones snap to the step.
2. Press `Down`. Turn the encoder until REC VELOCITY reads **External**. The hint reads: keyboard velocity goes to the volume column.
3. Press `Delete` on REC VELOCITY. It reads **Off**. REC MICRO stays **On**.

You should see this on the Pattern screen. With REC MICRO **On** and REC QUANTIZE on **Playing step**, a late note gets a Micro-move in FX 2 of its step. The later the note, the larger the value. A note on the beat gets none. With REC VELOCITY **External**, a note from a MIDI keyboard sets the volume of its step. Pads do not. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Move the pad rows against each other

PAD OFFSET sets where each row of the note pads starts on the row below it. It is on the PATTERN page, the eighth row. It reads from **0** to **12**, and **12** is the default. At **12** each row carries on right after the row below it, so the four rows are one long keyboard. At a smaller number, a row starts on that note of the row below it, so the rows overlap. At **0** every row has the same notes.

Start on the PATTERN page.

1. Press `Down` seven times. The cursor is on PAD OFFSET. The hint reads: 12: rows follow on, no overlap.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **5**. The hint reads: Less: rows overlap by 12 - N.
3. Press `Delete`. The row reads **12**, the default.

You should see the new number on the row. The pads follow at the next press, with no restart: on the Pattern screen, in the pad mode **NOTES** (`Shift` + `F2`), the pads of the upper rows play the notes the new number gives. The root, the scale and the octave are not here. They are in the held Note panel and belong to the project. PAD OFFSET belongs to the unit: it is kept with the other settings on the card, and a settings file from an older build reads **12**. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Choose when a picked pattern starts

PAT SWITCH decides what happens when the pattern plays and you pick another one with `F1` held on the Pattern screen. It is on the PATTERN page, the last row. It reads **Step** or **Pattern end**, and **Step** is the default. On **Step** the new pattern takes over at the next step. On **Pattern end** the pick waits and takes over when the pattern that plays has ended, as a pad does in PATS.

Start on the PATTERN page.

1. Press `Down` eight times. The cursor is on PAT SWITCH.
2. Turn the encoder until the row reads **Pattern end**. The card on the right says what each value does.
3. Press `Delete`. The row reads **Step**, the default.

You should see the setting act at once, with no restart. With **Pattern end**, hold `F1` on the Pattern screen while a pattern plays and press a pad: the pick is queued. While `F1` is held the view stays on your pick. Let go and the view goes on with the pattern that plays, until the queue lands. Press the same pad again, or the pad of the pattern that plays, to take the queue back. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Choose where the unit listens and sends MIDI

Start on the Config screen. Press `F1` (**MIDI**). The page has nine rows. Move to a row and turn the encoder. The defaults are DIN + USB for the ports, **All** for IN CHANNEL, 1 for OUT CHANNEL and **On** for both TRANSPORT rows.

| Row | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| CLOCK IN | Internal, USB, MIDI In jack | Where the clock comes from. USB or MIDI In jack makes the unit follow that clock. |
| CLOCK SYNC | -6 to +6 pulses | A timing correction when the unit follows a clock |
| CLOCK MODE | Off, Master, Slave | With CLOCK IN on Internal: Master sends the clock, Slave follows it |
| TRANSP IN | Off, On | Off: the unit ignores Start, Continue, Stop and Song Position from the clock it follows. The default is **On**. |
| TRANSP OUT | Off, On | Off: the unit sends no Start, Continue, Stop or Song Position. The clock still goes out. The default is **On**. |
| MIDI IN | DIN, USB, DIN + USB | The ports the unit listens to for notes and MIDI Learn |
| MIDI OUT | DIN, USB, DIN + USB | The ports for clock, transport and notes of MIDI tracks |
| IN CHANNEL | All, 1 to 16 | The channel it listens to |
| OUT CHANNEL | 1 to 16 | The channel for notes of MIDI tracks |

**TRANSPORT IN and TRANSPORT OUT** (the rows read TRANSP IN and TRANSP OUT, which is as long as a caption can be) are new on this firmware. They matter when the unit sends or follows a MIDI clock (CLOCK MODE Master or Slave, or CLOCK IN on USB or MIDI In jack). With CLOCK MODE **Off** they do nothing. A row set to **On** is how every unit worked before: the clock and the transport go together.

- **TRANSPORT OUT Off**: the unit sends only the clock. A synth or sequencer that follows your clock keeps time but does not start or stop with `Play` and `Stop`. As a Slave the unit relays the clock only.
- **TRANSPORT IN Off**: the unit still follows the tempo of the clock, but a Start, Continue, Stop or Song Position from the master does nothing. Press `Play` and the unit starts on the master's next clock. A Stop from the master does not stop the unit. It stops by itself only if the master's clock goes quiet.

A change takes effect at the next `Play`. If you turn TRANSPORT OUT to Off while the unit plays, the Stop of that run is still sent, so a device that got the Start is also stopped. The choice is kept on the card. `Delete` on a TRANSP row puts **On** back. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Change the display, the pad lights and the notation

Press `F2` (**DISPLAY**). Move to a row and turn the encoder.

| Row | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| DISPLAY | Low, Medium, High | The brightness of the screen. The default is **High**. |
| PAD LIGHTS | Low, Medium, High | The brightness of the pads. The default is **High**. |
| NUMBERING | From 0, From 1, Hex | How the step rows of the Pattern screen are numbered. The default is **From 1**. |
| MIDDLE C | C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6 | The name of MIDI note 60 on the Pattern screen. The default is **C-5**. |
| THEME | Amiga, Black, White | The colours of the screens. `Shift` + `Master` also steps to the next theme. |

All five rows act at once, with nothing to apply.   NUMBERING and MIDDLE C show on the Pattern screen: with **From 0** the step rows count from 00, and with MIDDLE C on **C-4** a note that reads C-5 by default reads C-4.

Not yet checked on the unit: the MIDI and DISPLAY rows.

### Reset a page to its defaults

Start on the page to reset, after you change a row.

1. Hold `Shift`. Press `F7` (**DEFAULTS**). The strip says **SHIFT+F7 AGAIN: RESET PAGE** and the key reads **RESET?**.
2. Press `Shift` + `F7` again within two seconds.

You should see **PAGE RESET TO DEFAULTS** in the strip. Every row of the page is at its default, and the cursor stays on its row. Other pages are not changed. After more than two seconds, a press only asks again. A USB row becomes a pending value: press `F7` (**APPLY**) to apply it. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Go to another page

Press `F1` to `F6` to go straight to a page, or press `Config` again for the next page. The pages wrap after PATTERN. With `F1` to `F6` the cursor starts on the first row of the new page; with `Config` it keeps its row (the last row if the new page is shorter). `Left` and `Right` do not turn the page: they change the value under the cursor.

### Update from the unit

New in track3r-os. You can install a new firmware from the unit, with no computer. The image is a file that ends in **.ptf**. It must already be in the `Firmware` folder of the card. The unit checks the file, asks you twice, and then restarts into the update. The unit has checked a file up to the image check; the INSTALL step (step 5) is not yet checked on the unit.

Start with the **.ptf** file on the card and your project saved.

1. Press `Config`, then `F4` (**INFO**). The key row now has `F8` (**UPDATE**).
2. Press `F8`. A list opens with every **.ptf** file in the folder and its size. The first file is marked **RESET TARGET**: it is the one the reset button installs. A name too long for that row is shortened with three dots; the question in step 3 shows it whole.
3. Choose a file with `Up` and `Down`. The cursor stops at both ends.  Press `F1` (**UPDATE**). The unit asks **UPDATE TO** and the name of the file.
4. Press `F1` (**YES**). A bar shows the unit reading the file. Nothing is written yet.
5. When the file passes, the unit says **IMAGE OK**, with the length of the image and a CRC. The CRC is a code worked out from every byte of the file, so two copies of the same file give the same code. Press `F1` (**INSTALL**) within 30 seconds.
6. The screen says **UPDATING: DO NOT POWER OFF**. The unit restarts by itself with the new firmware. Config, then **INFO**, shows the new build.

> **Careful**: when the screen says **UPDATING: DO NOT POWER OFF**, no key does anything and nothing can stop the update. Do not switch the unit off.

Each question is answered by `F1` alone. Any other key takes the question back, and the list returns. During the check, `F8` (**CANCEL**) stops it. If you wait 30 seconds at the second question, the list says **THE CHECK EXPIRED: CHECK AGAIN**. Nothing is written in any of these cases.     `F8` (**BACK**) on the list closes it.  Pulling the card out during the check or at the second question, or holding the Power switch during the check, cancels the check and closes the dialog.

If the file is not a good image, the list says **NOT A VALID IMAGE**, with the reason and the place in the file.  If the list does not open, the strip says why, for example **SAVE THE PROJECT FIRST** or **THE CARD IS ON THE COMPUTER**.   If the unit says **UPDATE DID NOT START**, the update did not begin and the unit goes on with the firmware it has.    The list holds 12 files at a time, and every **.ptf** file of `Firmware` can be reached: `Down` past the twelfth file loads the next 12, and `Up` past the first file of a window loads the 12 before it.   With more than 12 files the bottom right of the dialog says where the cursor is, for example **FILE 18 / 19**.  The folder is read again each time the list moves to another 12, so a file you add or remove while the list is open shows up then.  If the card is busy at that moment, the list stays as it was and the line says **THE CARD IS BUSY: TRY AGAIN**.  *New Community OS behaviour (OS-BUG-FWLIST).*

## Keys on this screen

The key row, and the row drawn while `Shift` is held. `-` means the key does nothing.

| Key | Label | With `Shift` |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **MIDI** | - |
| `F2` | **DISPLAY** | - |
| `F3` | **SD** | - |
| `F4` | **INFO** | - |
| `F5` | **USB** | - |
| `F6` | **PATTERN** | - |
| `F7` | **APPLY** | **DEFAULTS** |
| `F8` | - | - |

| Key | What it does | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| `F1` to `F6` | goes to a page: MIDI, DISPLAY, SD, INFO, USB, PATTERN | QA-CFG-033 |
| `F7` (**APPLY**) | on a USB row: press once to say what will happen, again to write. No label and no effect on the SD and INFO pages. | QA-CFG-003, QA-CFG-004, QA-CFG-034, QA-CFG-219 |
| `F8` (**UPDATE**) | on the INFO page only: opens the firmware update list. On the other pages it does nothing. | QA-CFG-040, QA-CFG-041, QA-CFG-218 |
| `Shift` + `F7` (**DEFAULTS**) | puts the page's rows back to their defaults. Press it twice within two seconds. | QA-CFG-031, QA-CFG-032 |
| `Shift` + `F1` to `F6`, `Shift` + `F8` | do nothing, and do not reach the page keys or APPLY | QA-CFG-015 |
| `Config` (again) | goes to the next page. It wraps after PATTERN. | QA-CFG-033 |
| `Left`, `Right` | change the value under the cursor, one click of the encoder down or up. On USB AUDIO and USB RETURN they change a pending value. New in track3r-os. | QA-CFG-240, QA-CFG-242, QA-CFG-243 |
| `Shift` + `Left`, `Shift` + `Right` | the same in the coarse step, as `Shift` + the encoder | QA-CFG-241 |
| `Up`, `Down` | moves the cursor between rows | QA-CFG-005, QA-CFG-017 |
| the encoder | changes the value under the cursor. On USB AUDIO and USB RETURN it changes a pending value. | QA-CFG-002, QA-CFG-008 |
| `Delete` | puts the row's default back. On USB AUDIO and USB RETURN, the default becomes a pending value. | QA-CFG-009, QA-CFG-019, QA-CFG-028, QA-CFG-036 |

## Good to know

- The pads play the current instrument while you hold them, on every page of Config. No setting changes.
- A **pending value** is a USB row you changed but did not apply. It shows a star (\*). Changing the page or leaving it drops the pending value. Nothing is applied.
- `Delete` on USB AUDIO when it reads Off gives **On\***. The On waits for `F7`.
- Pressing `Shift` + `F7` on the SD or INFO page says **NO ROWS ON THIS PAGE**.
- REC MICRO and REC VELOCITY are new in track3r-os.
- PAT SWITCH is new in track3r-os.
- PAD OFFSET is new in track3r-os. The official manual names a row offset among the pad options of Config, and this chapter does not claim the same range.
- Not checked against the original firmware: the keys and pages in this chapter.

## See also

- [Mixer](mixer.md): OUT MODE, which decides where Cue plays.
- [Pattern](pattern.md): live recording, the count-in, and the notes that REC MICRO and REC VELOCITY write.
- [USB disk](usb_disk.md): the CARD AS DISK and READ ONLY rows, and the card at power-on.

# Computer tools

Status: draft

Three Python tools on your computer talk to the unit over USB. `o3console.py` reads the screen, runs diagnostic commands and sends a firmware file to the card. `o3audio.py` measures the audio, and `o3shot.py` turns a saved text into a screen picture. They are for testing, for reporting a problem and for updating without taking the card out. New in track3r-os.

## What it is for

The unit has a USB serial port. It runs a text console, the diag console, and it presents an audio device when USB AUDIO is on. Three Python tools on your computer use these. They read the screen, read the diagnostics, send a firmware file to the card and measure the audio. Use them when you test or report a problem.

Two tools are for a developer: `o3hil.py` runs the hardware tests and is not covered here.

## Set up Python on Linux

These tools are written for Linux. Windows and macOS are **untested**.

1. Open a terminal and run `python3 --version`. If it prints a version number, Python 3 is installed.
2. If the command is missing, install Python 3 with your package manager. On Debian and Ubuntu: `sudo apt install python3`.
3. The tools use only the standard library of Python. You install nothing else.
4. For `o3audio.py`, also install the audio recording program: `sudo apt install alsa-utils`.
5. Get a copy of the repository from GitHub. The tools need a file called `check_image.py` from the same folder, so run them from the repository folder.

Every command in this chapter starts with `python3 -I`. The `-I` option runs Python in isolated mode, as [Installing track3r-os](install.md) does. It is always the same, so you can copy the commands as they are.

To check a tool, run its self-test. The self-test needs no unit:

```
python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --self-test
```

## Connect the unit

1. Connect the unit to the computer with a USB cable. Turn the unit on.
2. List the likely ports: `python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --list`.
3. The unit shows up as a serial port called Track3r. On Linux the name is often `/dev/ttyACM0`.

If the tool reports a permission error on the port, your user may need access to serial ports.

## The diag console: o3console.py

The console takes commands. You give each command as one argument of the tool. Quote a command that has a space in it.

```
python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --port /dev/ttyACM0 version "log 30"
```

The tool sends each command, waits for the prompt `o3> ` and prints the reply. It has no interactive mode. Use `--timeout` to wait longer for a reply; the default is 2 seconds.

The exit status tells you what happened: `0` means every reply was complete, `1` means a usage or port error, and `2` means a reply did not end with the prompt before the timeout.

### The commands you can use

The console has more commands than this table. The table lists the ones that are useful to a player or a tester. Each line is the command as you type it.

| Command | What it shows or does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `help` | lists the commands | |
| `version` | the build and the USB identity | the same build as Config, INFO |
| `cpu` | the audio load: cycles per stage, underruns, jitter, and a `guard` line: how many audio blocks the player skipped (shed) because the screen and USB handling was starved by a very heavy project (normally `shed 0 blocks`) | `cpu reset` sets the peaks and fault counters back to zero, so you can measure one run, and starts the module timing again. `cpu perf off` stops that module timing. |
| `guard` | the `guard` line of `cpu` on its own, with `n`, the window: how many heavy blocks in a row the player renders before it skips blocks to give the screen and USB handling their time | `guard n 12` sets the window (1 to 255, default 64) for a test run; it is not saved, a restart goes back to 64 |
| `mem` | the memory map and the free SRAM | |
| `crash` | the crash record that the last run left | |
| `usb` | the USB counters and the AUDIO mode | also `usb audio`, `usb mode`, `usb profile` and `usb map` |
| `log` | the last lines that the boot code and the drivers wrote | `log 30` shows the last 30 lines |
| `mix` | the audio meters in dBFS and the limiter gain reduction | |
| `mon` | the line-in monitor level | `mon off`, `mon on` (level 70), or `mon 0` to `mon 100` |
| `sd` | the SD card: slot, mount, identity, speed and counters | also `sd mount` |
| `ls` | a folder of the card, read only | for example `ls Projects` |
| `fw` | the firmware files on the card, and the card's volume serial | also `fw put`, `fw rm`, `fw arm` and `fw update`. Use the tool for these, see below |
| `radio` | the FM radio state, its last failure, its registers and pins | `radio retry` tries again |
| `voices` | the sampler voices in use, the peak since boot, the steals and `advanced` | `advanced` counts the short stretches (one a block, about 690 a second for each) in which a voice on a muted track was moved along without being rendered. It stays at 0 while no track is muted. |
| `rot` | the display orientation, `rot 0` to `rot 7` | not saved |
| `state` | the app state as one `key=value` line | for example the screen, the cursor and play |
| `shot` | the screen, as framed data | the tool `--shot` option asks for it |
| `leds` | the pad LED levels, on one line | |
| `key` | presses a button: `key <button> [tap, down, up or hold <ms>]` | for testing. The unit reacts as to a real press |
| `pad` | presses a pad, `pad 0` to `pad 47` | for testing |
| `enc` | turns the encoder, `enc -64` to `enc 64` detents | for testing; a minus is left. `enc accel` shows how fast a quick spin moves a list (new Community OS behaviour: in the File and Sample load lists, the Modules list and the module picker a fast spin moves 4 or 8 rows a detent); `enc accel off` goes back to a row a detent, `enc accel 6 16 60` sets x4 after 6 detents, x8 after 16, and a run ends after 60 ms without a detent. Not saved: a restart goes back to 6 16 60 |
| `reset` | mutes the outputs and restarts the unit | |

For developers only, and not in the table: `peek` reads 32-bit words, `poke` writes one word, `bench` is for the bench image, and `stage`, `audio`, `load`, `inst`, `mod`, `input` and `cache` are for debugging.

### Take a screenshot

The tool asks the unit for its screen, checks the picture and writes a PNG file:

```
python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --shot out.png
```

Commands given after the option run first, in order. This presses `F1` and then takes the picture:

```
python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --shot out.png "key f1"
```

A picture that arrives damaged, or that changed while it was sent, is asked for again. The tool tries again up to 2 times. Its exit status is `0` when the file is written, `2` when there was no prompt or the transfer stalled, and `4` when the unit refused the request or the data was not a whole picture.

The unit can also save its own screen to the card with no computer. This is new in the Community OS. Hold **Shift**, press **Power**, then let go of both. The picture is the first screen drawn after you let go, so the key row shows its normal labels. It is written to `Screenshots/SHOT_0001.bmp` (the next is `SHOT_0002.bmp`, and a file is never overwritten). The screen freezes for a second or two while it is written and the sound goes on; the strip then says `SCREENSHOT SAVED: SHOT_0001.BMP`. With no card, the card on the computer, or a save or export running, the strip says `NO SCREENSHOT:` and the reason. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Send a firmware file to the card

Use `--put` to copy a `.ptf` file into the `Firmware/` folder of the card. The tool checks the file first.

```
python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3console.py --put track3r-os-<version>.ptf
```

1. Any SD card in the unit takes the file. To make the tool check which card it is, find the card's volume serial (the `fw` command prints it in the form `XXXX-XXXX`) and pass it with `--expect-volume XXXX-XXXX`. The tool then refuses to write to a different card.
2. The name on the card must start with a letter or a digit. It may use letters, digits, dots, underscores and dashes, up to 48 characters not counting `.ptf`, and it must end in `.ptf`. Use `--name` to give the file another name on the card.
3. The unit checks the file again after it is written. The tool prints `ok`, the name, the size, the CRC-32 and the image length.

A file on the card does not update the unit. To flash it, follow the update steps in [Installing track3r-os](install.md). The unit flashes the first `.ptf` in `Firmware/`, so keep only one.

## Measure the audio: o3audio.py

The unit shows its audio device to the computer when USB AUDIO is on. This tool records that device for a few seconds, then reports on each channel. It needs `arecord` from the alsa-utils package.

1. List the capture devices and see which one looks like the unit:

   ```
   python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3audio.py list
   ```

2. Record 3 seconds and save the recording, if you want to keep it:

   ```
   python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3audio.py record --seconds 3 --save out.wav
   ```

3. Or analyse a file you already have: `python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3audio.py analyze out.wav`.

For each channel the tool reports the peak and the RMS level in dBFS, the DC offset, whether the channel is silent, whether it clips, and the strongest pitch when there is one. Checks can make the tool fail on purpose, for example `--expect-pitch 440` (with `--cents 40`), `--not-silent`, `--max-peak -1` or `--no-clipping`. `--channel 0` checks every channel. The tool exits with `0` when every check passed, `1` when a check failed, and `2` when there was no capture.

## Take a screen from a saved text: o3shot.py

Most people do not need this. `o3shot.py` works on the same screen data as `--shot`. It has two uses:

- `decode` turns a text file of a `shot` reply, saved from a terminal, into a PNG: `python3 -I platform/mk66/tools/o3shot.py decode capture.txt out.png`.
- `compare` checks two 800 by 480 PNG files, with tolerances for the small differences between a real screen and the simulator, and writes an optional difference picture with `--diff`. It exits with `0` when the pictures agree.

## See also

- [Installing track3r-os](install.md): the update steps, the checks and the way back.
- [Getting started](getting_started.md): the card, the first start and the firmware file.
- [The panel](panel.md): the keys that the `key` command presses.
- [Glossary](glossary.md): the terms of this chapter.

---

# Glossary

Key row: the row of eight labels under the soft keys `F1` to `F8`.

Shift row: the row of labels that the unit draws while `Shift` is held. A key with no label does nothing.

Strip: the message line of the screen. Short messages appear there, for example **TRACK 03 NAMED**.

Track: one of the project's tracks. Each track has a name and a column on the Mixer.

Mute: a track setting that silences the track. Set it with `F7` (**MUTE**) on the Mixer.

Solo: a track setting, set and cleared with `F8` (**SOLO**) on the Mixer. While a track is soloed, every track that is not soloed is silent, and so are its sends. Any number of tracks can be soloed.

Master limiter: the one stage on the MASTER FX page. It is always on. It holds the loudest peaks of the master output under a ceiling, so they do not clip. Its rows are LIM THRESH, LIM ATTACK and LIM RELEASE.

On-screen keyboard: the keyboard that opens for a name, with a title such as **TRACK NAME**. It takes up to the length the name allows (20 characters for a track, 30 for a pattern).

Order list: the list of slots on the Song screen.

Slot: one entry of the order list. It holds one pattern.

Pattern: a numbered set of notes, edited on the Pattern screen. A slot on the Song screen holds one pattern.

Fill: writing notes on the steps of a track by a rule. Press `F4` (**FILL**) on the Pattern screen. The rules are EVERY N, RANDOM, EUCLID and SCALE.

Pattern name: the name you give a pattern, up to 30 characters. Set it on the Song screen with `Shift` + `F6` (**NAME**).

Pending value: a Config setting you changed but have not applied. It shows a star (\*) until `F7` (**APPLY**) writes it.

APPLY: the `F7` key on Config. On a USB row, the first press says what will happen and the second press writes the setting.

USB AUDIO: the Config row that shows an audio device to the computer. Off gives STANDARD; On is the default.

STANDARD: the USB mode of the unit with MIDI and serial only, and no audio device.

USB return: the stereo stream that the computer sends to the unit over USB audio. The USB RETURN row of Config turns it on or off.

RETURN LEVEL: the Config row for the level of the USB return at the outputs. It changes at once, with no APPLY.

METRO: the metronome. It plays a click with the beat. Set it on the PATTERN page of Config: Off, Cue or Main.

Cue: the METRO setting that plays the click on the CUE side of the line out. Main plays it on the MAIN side.

Count-in: the bars of click that play before a recording starts. Set it with COUNT-IN on the PATTERN page of Config: Off, 1 bar or 2 bars.

Live recording: recording the notes you play while the pattern plays. Turn it on with `Shift` + `Rec` on the Pattern screen.

REC QUANTIZE: the Config row that sets how a live note is placed on a step. Its values include Nearest step and Playing step.

Step FX: an effect written on one step, in one of its two Fx cells. The info line reads it in words.

FX 2: the second FX column of a step. A Micro-move is written there.

Micro-move: a command in FX 2 that records how late a live note was played inside its step. The grid shows it as m02.

Sample: a recording of sound, read from a file on the card and loaded into an instrument.

Instrument: a slot of the project that makes sound from a sample, a module or MIDI.

Card: the SD card. Sample load browses its folders and files.

Sample rate: the number of audio samples per second, in hertz (Hz). Each sample file records its own rate.

AIFF: an audio file format. Its files end in `.aif`, `.aiff` or `.aifc`.

8SVX: an 8-bit audio file format of the IFF family. Its files end in `.8svx` or `.svx`.

WAV: an audio file format. Its files end in `.wav`.

Export: writing the sound to WAV files in the `Export` folder on the card. Press `F7` (**EXPORT**) on the PROJECTS page of the File screen.

Stem: the sound of one track, or of the delay, the reverb or the whole mix, written to its own WAV file by a stem export.

OG PROJECT: the EXPORT row that writes a project folder in the original firmware's format. It is experimental.

Stereo file: a file with a left and a right channel. Sample load shows **ST** after its name.

Channel: one side of a stereo file. On Sample load, `F8` (**CH MIX**, **CH LEFT**, **CH RIGHT**) chooses what loads.

Audition: playing a file without loading it. On Sample load, `F5` (**PLAY**) auditions the file under the cursor.

Selection: the range that the Sample edit processes act on. With no selection, a process acts on the whole sample. Turn the encoder on Sample edit to make one, and move its edges with the encoder. `Delete` clears it.

Normalise: scaling a sample so that its loudest point is at full scale. On Sample edit, `F2` (**NORM**).

DC offset: a sample whose average is not at its centre line. Removing it centres the sample without clipping. On Sample edit, `Shift` + `F4` (**DC REM**).

Amiga conversion: converting a sample to the Amiga rate of 8,287 Hz (**AMG 8K**) or 16,574 Hz (**AMG 16K**), with an 8-bit option (**Q8**). On Sample edit, `Shift` + `F1`, `F2` and `F3`.

Amiga engine: one of the two sample voices. The other is the Modern engine.

Undo: taking back the last Sample edit process. `F8` (**UNDO**) undoes it, and `Shift` + `F8` (**REDO**) does it again.

Play mode: how an instrument plays its sample. The modes are ONE SHOT, LOOP FWD, LOOP BWD, PING-PONG, SLICE, BEAT SLICE, WAVETABLE and GRANULAR. Press `Shift` + `F1` (**MODE**) on the Wave screen.

Slice: a part of a sample that one pad plays. The slice modes, SLICE and BEAT SLICE, use the CHOP page.

CHOP page: the page of the Wave screen for the slice modes. It holds the slice keys.

Wavetable: a WAV file of many short windows, one after another. The WAVETABLE play mode plays one window at a time. The POSITION row chooses the window.

Window: the part of a wavetable that plays. It is at most 2048 samples, and never longer than the sample.

Granular: the GRANULAR play mode. It plays short pieces of a sample, called grains, that you set with POSITION, LENGTH, SHAPE and LOOP.

Project: the work saved as one unit: patterns, song order, instruments and their samples. Each project has its own folder on the card.

Title: the name of a project, shown in the header. It is not the folder name, and it can have up to 32 characters.

RECENT: the first rows of the PROJECTS list. They are the last five projects you opened or saved, newest first.

Purge: removing the instruments that no step, FX or Learn binding uses. Press `Shift` + `F7` (**PURGE**) on the PROJECTS page, twice.

USB disk mode: the mode in which the unit shows its card to a computer as a disk. Hold `Shift`, `F1` and `F7` together while you turn the unit on, or use the CARD AS DISK row of Config. See [USB disk](usb_disk.md).

Scene: one of the three stored scenes, SCENE 1 to SCENE 3, on the Perform screen. Keys `F1` to `F3` recall them.

Perform slot: one of the 12 columns of pads on Perform. It holds one effect and has four rows: **OFF** on top and three values.

LATCH (slots page): the switch on `F6` of the **SLOTS** page of Perform. It is on by default and saved with the project. On, a slot's row that holds a value stays on after you let go of its pad. Off, the effect ends at the release.

LATCH (DJ page): a second switch, on `F6` of the DJ page. It is off when you open the page, and leaving the page ends it. On, the filter stays where you left it, and a kill, **REP**, **ECHO** or **CUT** pad stays on after a tap until you tap it again.

EDIT: on Perform, `Rec` turns EDIT on. While it is on, the encoder stores the value in the row you hold, and `Left`, `Right`, `Up` and `Down` pick a slot and change its effect.

Crossfader: the bar on the DJ page that fades between group A and group B. The encoder moves it.

Group (DJ page): the set of tracks that the crossfader moves together: **A**, **B**, or **THRU** for tracks it never touches.

Module: a file with the extension `.tmod` on the card. It is an instrument module (a sound engine such as the TB-303, FM or Chip) or an app.

Module instrument: an instrument slot whose sound comes from a module, not from a sample or MIDI.

Engine picker: the list that opens with `F4` (**MODULE**) on a free instrument slot. It lists the instrument modules on the card.

Accent: on the TB-303, a note played harder than the rest. It opens the filter further, is louder, and lets the filter fall back on its own time. A note is an accent when its velocity reaches **ACC THRESH**.

Cent: a hundredth of a semitone. 1200 cents are one octave.

Operator: one of the four sine waves of the FM module. Each has its own ratio, detune, level and envelope.

Modulator: an FM operator that bends the pitch of another operator. You do not hear it by itself. A carrier is an operator you hear.

Algorithm: on the FM module, the choice of which operators modulate which and which are carriers. `4>3>2>1` means 4 modulates 3, 3 modulates 2, 2 modulates 1, and only 1 is heard.

Detune: a small shift of an FM operator's pitch from its ratio, in cents.

App: a module you run from the Modules screen, for example MIDI Monitor or Tuner. Apps are experimental.

Navigator: the list of screens that opens with `Shift` + `Pattern`. Turn the encoder to a screen and press `F8` (**GO**).

TOOLS: the `F7` key on Pattern. It opens a list of tools, among them EXPORT PATTERN and the apps that edit the project or write files.

Firmware file: the file with the `.ptf` extension that holds a firmware image. The unit's bootloader flashes it from the `Firmware/` folder of the card.

Workspace: the card folder that holds the project the unit loads at boot. The project is in the original firmware format.

Demo kit: four instruments and pattern 1, built in. The unit uses them when no project loads, or when the loaded project has no sample instrument.

Starter zip: an optional zip that goes next to the firmware file, with folders, samples, wavetables and demo projects. It is not part of this release.

Diag console: the text console of the unit, on its USB serial port. You type a command and it prints the reply. The computer tools send their commands to it.

Python 3: the programming language that the computer tools are written in. Install it on your computer before you use the tools.

Take: one recording made on the Record screen, from its start to its end.

Armed: the state of a take that waits for its start point, such as the next bar. The header says **ARMED**.

Review: the screen after a take ends. For a loop, you save, discard, mute or overdub it from here.

Loop: a take of a set number of bars that repeats on the bars of the pattern. Set its length on the LOOP row.

Layer: one overdub pass, added on top of a loop.

Overdub: recording on a loop that is already playing, so that each pass adds a layer. Press `F1` under a loop review.

Feedback: the Record setting, from 0 to 100, for how much of the old sound is kept on each pass of an overdub. At 100 every layer stays.

Undo layer: `F5` (**UNDO LYR**) on the Record screen. It puts back the sound from before the last layer.

Transport: the playing of the pattern. `Play` starts and stops it, and a loop follows it.

Sample memory: the memory that holds samples. A take that fills it ends.

Column: one of the four fields of a track on the Pattern grid: **Note**, **Instr**, **Vol** and **Fx**. Tap its key to select it.

Step: one row of the Pattern grid. A pattern has up to 128 steps.

Cursor: the highlighted cell that you edit. The arrow keys move it.

Block: the steps and tracks you mark with `Shift` and an arrow. Copy works on it.

Clip: the steps last copied with `Copy`. The clip stays until the next copy.

JUMP: how many steps the cursor moves after an entry or a delete. Set it on the JUMP chooser, `F3`, from 0 to 32.

LENGTH: the number of steps in the pattern, from 1 to 128. Set it on the LENGTH chooser, `F2`.

Playhead: the step that the pattern is playing now. In LIVE it has a red bar.

WATCH: the record mode in which the pads only preview and nothing is written. The chip reads **WATCH**. Browse is the same mode.

STEP: the record mode in which notes are written at the cursor. The chip reads **STEP**, in amber.

LIVE: the record mode in which notes are written at the playhead while the pattern plays. The chip reads **LIVE**, in red.

Zoom: how many tracks the Pattern grid shows: 5, 8 or 12. Hold `Note` and tap `Instr` to change it.

Undo area: the changes that one screen can take back. `F8` takes back the last change of the screen you are on. Pattern and Song have separate undo areas.

Page: one of the views of the Instrument screen. `F1` to `F5` open them on a sample instrument.

Source page: the first page of a sample instrument. It holds PLAY MODE, PLAY ENGINE and the rows of the play mode.

Play engine: the PLAY ENGINE row, which picks the engine that plays a sample: Auto, or a fixed engine. The 12-bit and 8-bit presets cap the bit depth.

Volume law: the rule that turns an instrument's VOLUME into decibels (dB). The law belongs to the project, so an older project keeps its loudness.

MIDI instrument: an instrument that sends MIDI notes and controller messages to a device, instead of playing a sample.

LFO: a low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves a destination up and down, at the tempo's rate.

Destination: a setting that an LFO can move. The MOD page lists six: Volume, Panning, Finetune, Cutoff, WT Position and Gran Position.

Velocity: how hard a note is played, as a MIDI value up to 127. The VEL> row on the VOICE page scales it.

Type chooser: the screen of an empty slot. It offers SAMPLE, MIDI, PASTE, MODULE and LOAD.

Instrument copy: the instrument copied with `Shift` + `F2`. The unit keeps one copy at a time, and `Shift` + `F3` pastes it.

Instrument file: a saved instrument, with the extension `.pti`, in the `instruments` folder of the card.

Euclid rhythm: a rhythm of E hits spread as evenly as possible over the steps of a track, with gaps that differ by at most one. The FILL dialog writes it with TYPE **EUCLID**.

Ramp: values that move in a straight line from one end to the other, such as a volume from 127 down to 0 over a track. The FILL dialog writes it with MODE **RAMP**.

Voice: one sound that is playing. Each note that sounds uses one voice, and the unit has a fixed number of voices.

---

# Cheat sheet

The keys on one page. Each table names the chapter it comes from.

## Global keys

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Play` | starts or stops the pattern, from any screen |
| `Rec` | on Pattern, turns STEP on or off; on Record, starts or stops the take |
| `Shift` + `Rec` | on Pattern, turns LIVE on or off |
| `Shift` + `Pattern` | opens the Navigator. `F8` (**GO**) opens the chosen screen; `F7` (**CLOSE**) leaves it |
| `Shift` + `Config` | opens the help page of the screen you are on. `Left` and `Right` turn the pages, `Up`, `Down` and the encoder scroll, any other key closes it |
| `Shift` + `Master` | steps to the next colour theme: Amiga, Black, White.  |
| `Shift` + `Power` | saves a screenshot to the card. `Power` held 2 seconds turns the unit off.  |
| `Master` held, then the encoder | changes the master volume, from any screen |
| `Pattern` held, then the encoder or a pad | the encoder changes the tempo, from any screen (a BPM a click, a tenth with `Shift` held first); pad taps tap the tempo. Letting go of `Pattern` after that opens nothing.  |
| `Song` held | shows Song until you let go, then goes back to the screen you came from |
| `Vol` and `Fx` together | opens Learn |
| a screen button again | opens the next page of that screen: the FX page of Sample edit, the DJ page of Perform |
| a soft key again | steps that key's windows, such as the six MOD destinations on Instrument |

| Screen button | Opens | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| `Params` | Instrument | [Instrument](instrument.md) |
| `Perform` | Perform | [Perform](perform.md) |
| `File` | File | [File](file.md) |
| `Config` | Config | [Config](config.md) |
| `Master` | Mixer | [Mixer](mixer.md) |
| `Sample Loader` | Sample load | [Sample load](sample_load.md) |
| `Sample Playback` | Wave and Chop | [Wave and Chop](wave.md) |
| `Sample Editor` | Sample edit | [Sample edit](sample_edit.md) |
| `Sample Recorder` | Record | [Record](record.md) |
| `Song` | Song | [Song](song.md) |
| `Pattern` | Pattern | [Pattern](pattern.md) |

Held at power-on, until the strip shows the mode:

| Keys | What happens |
|---|---|
| `Shift`, `F1` and `F7` | the card shows on the computer as a disk ([Getting started](getting_started.md)) |
| `Shift`, `F1` and `F8` | the INPUT TEST screen opens |

## Pattern editing

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right` | move the cursor. `Up` on step 1 goes to the last step |
| pad | in STEP, writes a note at the cursor; in WATCH, plays the sound |
| `Delete` | clears the cursor's entry, or the highlighted columns of the block |
| `Shift` + `Delete` | pulls the steps below up, to close a gap |
| `Insert` | inserts an empty step at the cursor; the steps below move down |
| `Copy` | copies the block, or the step under the cursor |
| `Shift` + `Copy` | pastes the copy at the cursor, in STEP |
| `Shift` + `Up` or `Down` | selects a block |
| `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` | grows the block one column; past the last column it takes the next track whole, then a track at a time |
| `F4` (**FILL**) | opens the Fill dialog |
| `F5` (**PREVIEW**) | sounds the note under the cursor while held |
| `F6` (**INVERT**) | reverses the steps of the block, track by track |
| `F7` (**TOOLS**) | opens the TOOLS list: DUPLICATE, EXPAND, SHRINK, export and the tool apps |
| `F8` (**UNDO**), `Shift` + `F8` (**REDO**) | take back and redo a pattern change |
| `Note`, `Instr`, `Vol`, `Fx` | select the column; hold to open its popup |
| `Note` + `Instr` | cycles the zoom: 5, 8 or 12 tracks |
| `Note` + `Left` or `Right` | moves one whole track |
| `F1` (**PATTERN**) | hold: the pattern chooser, and while the transport plays a pick switches the playing pattern at once; a tap does nothing. With it held, `Copy` copies the whole pattern and `Shift` + `Copy` writes it over the one shown |
| `F2` (**LENGTH**), `F3` (**JUMP**) | tap toggles the chooser; hold opens it |

## Shift combinations

The soft keys with `Shift` held. `-` means the key does nothing. On Pattern, `Shift` + `F1` (OCTAVE) moves the pads' lowest C up an octave, and the labels NOTES, PIANO, ISO, TRACKS, PATS and VU choose what the pads do.

| Key | Pattern | Instrument | Sample load | Mixer | File |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Shift` + `F1` | **OCTAVE** | **NAME** | **0/4** | **NAME** | **0/4** |
| `Shift` + `F2` | **NOTES** | **COPY** | **1/4** | - | **1/4** |
| `Shift` + `F3` | **PIANO** | **PASTE** | **2/4** | - | **2/4** |
| `Shift` + `F4` | **ISO** | **DELETE** | **3/4** | - | **3/4** |
| `Shift` + `F5` | **TRACKS** | **SAVE** | **END** | - | **END** |
| `Shift` + `F6` | **PATS** | **<USED** | - | - | **NAME** |
| `Shift` + `F7` | **VU** | **USED>** | **INST -** | **UNMUTE** | **PURGE** |
| `Shift` + `F8` | **REDO** | **REDO** | **INST +** | **UNSOLO** | - |

| Other `Shift` keys | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Shift` + `Play` | Pattern: starts at the cursor's row. It never counts in |
| `Shift` + `Rec` | Pattern: turns LIVE on or off |
| `Shift` + `Insert` | Pattern: goes to step 0 and clears the block |
| `Shift` + `Delete` | Pattern: pulls the steps up. Instrument: sets every row to its default. Song: cuts the slot, or the selected cells in the track map |
| `Shift` + `Up` or `Down` | on lists: moves one page of 16 rows |
| `Shift` + `Right` or `Left` | Sample load: marks the file under the cursor and steps down (Right), or clears the marks (Left). **LOAD** and **ADD** then load every marked file |
| `Shift` + `Right` or `Left` | Instrument: the row's coarse step up or down, as `Shift` + encoder. Plain `Right` and `Left` are one click |
| `Shift` + `Note`, `Instr`, `Vol`, `Fx` | Pattern: jumps to a quarter of the pattern. On Song `Shift` + `Note` jumps to the previous slot with the same pattern |
| `Shift` + pad | Instrument: selects the instrument on that pad |
| `Shift`, held alone | Pattern: the pads show the TRACKS layout while held |

| `Shift` + encoder | One click moves |
|---|---|
| Pattern, Note column | one octave |
| Pattern, Instr column | 8 instruments |
| Pattern, FX1 (volume) column | 10 |
| Pattern, FX2 column | 16 |
| Pattern, browsing in WATCH | one page of 16 rows |
| Instrument, CHANNEL row | 4 |
| Instrument, other rows | a coarse step |
| Mixer | a coarse step |
| Song | a fine step |

## Screens

The soft keys `F1` to `F8`, left to right, as the key row shows them.

| Screen | Button | F1 to F8 |
|---|---|---|
| [Pattern](pattern.md) | `Pattern` | **PATTERN**, **LENGTH**, **JUMP**, **FILL**, **PREVIEW**, **INVERT**, **TOOLS**, **UNDO** |
| [Instrument](instrument.md) | `Params` | **SAMPLE**, **VOICE**, **FILTER**, **MOD**, **SENDS**, **<INS**, **INS>**, **UNDO** |
| [Sample load](sample_load.md) | `Sample Loader` | **LOAD**, **UP**, **ENTER**, **ADD**, **PLAY**, **RESCAN**, **WT AUTO**, **CH MIX** |
| [Sample edit](sample_edit.md) | `Sample Editor` | **CROP**, **NORM**, **REVERSE**, **FADE IN**, **FADE OUT**, **AMP**, **PREVIEW**, **UNDO** |
| [Record](record.md) | `Sample Recorder` | **REC/STOP**, **MONITOR**, **SAVE**, **DISCARD**, **SEEK-**, **SEEK+**, **SAVE WAV**, **PREVIEW** |
| [Mixer](mixer.md) | `Master` | **MIXER**, **ROUTING**, **MST FX**, **STEMS**, **CUE LVL**, -, **MUTE**, **SOLO** |
| [File](file.md) | `File` | **OPEN**, **RESCAN**, **NEW**, **SAVE**, **SAVE AS**, **IMPORT**, **EXPORT**, - |

| Screen | Changes to |
|---|---|
| Instrument | `F1` reads SAMPLE, SLICE, WT or GRAIN; `F6` and `F7` show the neighbours, such as `<06` and `08>` |
| Sample edit, FX page (`Sample Editor` again) | `F1` **FILTER**, `F2` **COMPRESS** |
| Record, loop review | `F1` **OVERDUB**, `F5` **UNDO LYR**, `F8` **LOOP ON** or **MUTED**; `F6` does nothing |
| Perform, DJ page | `F5` **SCR** (the encoder is the platter), `F6` **LATCH**, `F8` **RESET**; `Shift` + `F1` to `F8` do nothing |

---

# Export

Status: draft

Export writes what the unit plays to WAV files on the card, and the tools are spread over three screens: the EXPORT page of File, the TOOLS list of Pattern and the TOOLS dialog of Song. Song, pattern and stems exports work as the official manual describes. The stems are one WAV for each audio track that plays a note, plus the DELAY, REVERB and MIX files. The files are named differently: `Export/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_Song0001.wav`, and a second render takes the next number instead of a new folder.  **OG PROJECT** writes a folder in the original firmware's project format and is marked EXPERIMENTAL. Not checked against the original firmware: whether an official unit opens it.

## What it is for

Export writes what the unit plays to files on the card, in the folder `Export/<PROJECT>`. You can export the whole song, some slots of the song, one pattern, a block of a pattern, or the separate tracks (stems). These exports are WAV files.

**OG PROJECT** writes a folder in the project format of the original firmware. It is **EXPERIMENTAL**. See the last section.

Exports never change the project. Starting an export stops the transport.

## How it works

An export is an offline render: the unit renders the song, a pattern or a block without playing it aloud and writes the result as 16-bit stereo, 44,100 Hz WAV files in `Export/<PROJECT>` on the card. Nothing is live. Your project is not changed.

While it runs, only `F8` (**CANCEL**) works. The pads, `Play`, `Rec` and the screen buttons do nothing; nothing is queued for later. Cancelling, or the end of the render, gives the keys back. A second export never writes over the first: it makes `_0002`.

Example: to bring one drum pattern into another program, choose **PATTERN nn** and press `F1`. To mix it there, choose **PATT STEMS nn** instead, and you get one file for each audio track that plays a note, plus the DELAY, REVERB and MIX files.

## Try it

This walk-through exports one pattern.

1. Press `File`. The File screen opens on the PROJECTS page.
2. Press `F7` (**EXPORT**). The EXPORT page opens with the cursor on the row you used last. Press `Up` until it stops on **SONG**, the first row.

   (Picture: File, EXPORT page: five rows, the cursor on SONG, F1 reads EXPORT.)
3. Press `Down`. The cursor is on **PATTERN nn**. The screen says what you get: the pattern once, with its tail. Turn the encoder to choose another pattern if the project has one.

   (Picture: File, EXPORT page: the cursor on PATTERN, the lines under the rows say what F1 will make.)
4. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**). A progress overlay shows while it renders.
5. When it ends, the strip says `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_P<n>_0001.WAV`. The file is on the card.

## The screen at a glance

(Picture: File, EXPORT page: the rows to choose from, and the file name that F1 will make.)

| Row | What `F1` makes |
|---|---|
| SONG | The whole song, as one WAV file. |
| PATTERN nn | The pattern nn, as one WAV file. |
| SONG STEMS | One WAV file for each audio track that plays a note, and the DELAY, REVERB and MIX files. |
| PATT STEMS nn | The same set, for the pattern nn. |
| OG PROJECT | A project folder in the original firmware's format. EXPERIMENTAL. |

The page is on the File screen, on the PROJECTS page, with `F7` (**EXPORT**). The card under the rows shows the file name `F1` will make. From the Pattern screen, the same WAV exports are in the TOOLS list.

## More tasks

### Export a pattern from the EXPORT page

Start on the File screen, on the PROJECTS page.

1. Press `F7` (**EXPORT**), then `Up` until the cursor stops on **SONG**. The page keeps the row you used last.
2. Press `Down` to **PATTERN nn**. The nn starts at the pattern you were on.
3. Turn the encoder to the pattern you want. It moves to the next pattern that exists.
4. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**).

You should see `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_P<n>_0001.WAV` when it ends. Exporting again makes `_0002`, and never writes over the first file.

### Export the pattern on screen from the Pattern screen

Start on the Pattern screen, with the transport stopped.

1. Press `F7` (**TOOLS**). The list opens, with **EXPORT PATTERN** first.
2. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**) on **EXPORT PATTERN**.

The file is `<PROJECT>_P<n>_0001.WAV`, as on the EXPORT page.  While the view follows the play line (WATCH while playing, or LIVE), the list does not open and the strip says **STOP PLAYING TO OPEN TOOLS**. Press `Play` to stop, then `F7`.

### Export a block of the pattern

Start on the Pattern screen, in **STEP**.

1. Select the block with `Shift` and the arrows.
2. Press `F7` (**TOOLS**). The list shows **EXPORT SELECTION** below **EXPORT PATTERN** and the three pattern tools.
3. Press `Down` four times to **EXPORT SELECTION**, then `F1` (**EXPORT**).

You should see `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_SEL0001.WAV`. The file holds only the tracks of the block, from its first row to the end of its last row. The other tracks are muted in the file. A block that covers only some columns of a track still exports that track's whole steps.

> **Tip**: The selection ends at the first silence after the block. **EXPORT PATTERN** keeps the tail of its reverb and delay.

### Export some slots of the song

Start on the Song screen. The transport may be playing: the export stops it.

1. Pick the slots. With the cursor on **PAT**, `Shift` + `Down` or `Up` extends a range of slots. With no range, the export takes the slot under the cursor.
2. In the track map, `Shift` + `Left` or `Right` also picks tracks. With no range of tracks or slots selected, the export takes every track. A range of slots with no range of tracks, picked in the map, renders only the track under the cursor.
3. Press `F6` (**TOOLS**). On the **OP** row, turn the encoder, or press `Left` or `Right`, to **EXPORT WAV**. The row below it goes, and the footer names the slots and the tracks.
4. Press `F1` (**APPLY**).

The progress overlay reads **EXPORTING THE SLOTS**. You should see `SAVED EXPORT/<PROJECT>/<PROJECT>_S<a>-<b>_0001.WAV`. The numbers are the Song screen's slot numbers, so the first slot is `S0`. A second export of the same slots is `_0002`, and nothing is written over.

The file runs from the first slot to the end of the last, then keeps the tail of the delay and the reverb, as the song export does. It holds the tracks you picked, or every track. A muted or soloed track you picked does sound. If the slots hold an Order jump that goes back inside them, the export loops as the song does, until it stops with `TOO LONG FOR A WAV (100 MIN)`; `F8` (**CANCEL**) stops it sooner.

> **Tip**: The SONG row of the EXPORT page is not changed. It still writes the whole song as `<PROJECT>_Song0001.WAV`.

**Not yet checked on the unit.** The host tests pass.

### Export the stems

Start on the File screen, on the EXPORT page.

1. Press `Up` until the cursor stops on **SONG**, then `Down` three times to **PATT STEMS nn**. For the song, press `Up` once, to **SONG STEMS**.
2. For a pattern, turn the encoder to the pattern you want.
3. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**).

You should see `SAVED n STEMS` when it ends. The files are `<PROJECT>_P<n>_S0001_T01.wav` and so on, then `_DELAY`, `_REVERB` and `_MIX`. For the song, the name uses `Song` in place of `P<n>`.

Which files a set has: one track file for each audio track that plays a note. A track with no notes, a MIDI track and a MIDI instrument have no file. DELAY and REVERB appear only when that bus can sound. MIX is always there, and it is the last file.

All the files of a set have the same length. A second set gets the next number, `S0002`, and it never writes over the first set.

### Cancel an export

1. Press `F8` (**CANCEL**) while the progress overlay is up.

The strip says **EXPORT CANCELLED**, or `CANCELLED: n OF m STEMS SAVED` for a set. The files already finished stay on the card. The file being written is not left on the card.

### Export the project for the original firmware (EXPERIMENTAL)

Start on the File screen, on the EXPORT page.

1. Press `Down` until the cursor stops on **OG PROJECT**, the last row. The row reads **EXPERIMENTAL**.
2. Read the card. It shows the folder name, the size, and the list **LOSES**. The list says what the export would leave out. While it says **COUNTING...**, there is no size or list yet.
3. Press `F1` (**EXPORT**). If something would be left out, the strip says `LOSES <n kinds>: F1 AGAIN`. Press `F1` again to go on. If the count is not done, the strip says `COUNTING WHAT THE EXPORT LOSES: WAIT`, and `F1` starts nothing.
4. Wait for the end. The strip says **SAVED**, and it names any kinds that were not kept.

You should see the folder `Export/<NAME> OG` on the card. A second export makes `<NAME> OG 2`, and so on up to `OG 99`. Nothing already on the card changes.

> **Careful**: `F8` stops the export. The finished files stay, but there is no project file until the last file is done. The folder is then not a project.

The export asks first only when something would be left out. Any other key, a move, leaving the screen or waiting 4 seconds takes the question back. If the project changes while the question is up, `F1` counts again and asks with the new count.

The export refuses while a take is armed or recording, while a job, a load or a save runs, and on a card it cannot write (no card, a write-protected card or an exFAT card). Any other SD card with a FAT volume works. The strip gives the reason, and no folder is made. `F1` stops the transport before it starts.

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `File` | Opens the File screen. |
| `F7` (**EXPORT**) | On the PROJECTS page, opens the EXPORT page.  |
| `Up`, `Down` | Choose a row. They stop at the first and the last row.  |
| encoder | On PATTERN and PATT STEMS, moves to the next pattern that exists. On the song rows it does nothing.  |
| `Shift` + encoder | On PATTERN, moves eight patterns a turn.  |
| `F1` (**EXPORT**) | Starts the chosen row.  |
| `F8` (**CANCEL**) | Stops an export. The finished files stay.  |
| `F7` (**TOOLS**), on Pattern | Opens the list with EXPORT PATTERN, and EXPORT SELECTION when a block is selected.  |
| `F6` (**TOOLS**), on Song | Opens the dialog over the selected slots. Its fourth OP is **EXPORT WAV**, and `F1` (**APPLY**) starts it.  |

While an export runs, only `F8` works.

## Good to know

- A WAV file is 16-bit stereo at 44,100 Hz. It plays as the unit plays it: tempo, swing, effects, the delay and reverb tails, and the limiter.
- A WAV file does not hold live input, the USB return, the pads or MIDI notes.
- A project with no folder is exported as `Untitled`; the strip shows it in capitals.
- The stems add up to the MIX only while the limiter does nothing. A mix the limiter works on is not the sum of its stems.
- If an export fails, the strip says `EXPORT FAILED` and the reason. No file is left under its final name, and no temporary file either. The files you already had are not touched.
- Holding `Power` during an export does not stop it at once. The strip says **EXPORT RUNNING - HOLD POWER AGAIN TO STOP IT**. A second hold within 10 seconds stops it, and the finished files stay. See [The panel](panel.md#power). **Not yet checked on the unit.**
- The EXPORT page stays open when you leave the File screen.
- Not yet checked on the unit: the WAV files on a computer, and the stem lengths. The simulator has no card. The host tests pass.

**OG PROJECT** has its own rules:

- The original firmware's format is checked byte for byte against reference files. Whether an official unit opens the folder is not yet verified. This is an open research question.
- The OS opens its own export again. It does not restore the pattern names.
- Channel Pan is dropped, and the export counts it.
- A sample at 22,050 Hz, 16,726 Hz, 8,287 Hz or in the Amiga engine is written at 44,100 Hz, with its pitch kept.
- A project made on the older level law keeps the gain of its instruments. Under -24 dB, the level is limited and the question counts it.
- The question can name 15 kinds: sample instruments with no file, instruments with no sample memory ready, 12 bit and 8 bit engine instruments, Amiga engine instruments, instruments too long for a file, levels clamped, module instruments, effect and volume columns, steps on tracks 13 to 16, track settings (pan, solo, bus), MIDI instruments and settings, sample instruments in slots 49 to 64, Sine LFO shapes, names cut short, and other settings, names and rates.  A Sine LFO is written as Triangle, and the question counts it as `1 SINE LFO`.  The list shows up to three kinds, one line each. With more, it shows every kind in a short form, run together; FX and modules are always named.
- After an export, `diag ogexp status` also says where its time went: the slowest step with its stage, then the time of each stage. It changes no file and no screen.

## See also

- [File](file.md): saving, opening and the project folder on the card.
- [Pattern](pattern.md): the Pattern screen, where EXPORT PATTERN and EXPORT SELECTION start.
- [Song](song.md): the Song screen, where EXPORT WAV of slots starts.
- [Fill and tools](pattern_tools.md): the TOOLS list in full.

# Effects in the pattern

Status: draft

Each step has two effect cells, FX1 and FX2, next to the note, and an effect changes how that note plays: a chord, an arpeggio, a slide, a drive or a volume change. The list holds effects 0 to 42, which are the original layout's ids (Chord, Arp, Tune, Slides, Overdrive and Bit Depth among them), and at its end 17 tracker effects. A tracker effect starts at a sensible default, and the info line reads the value in words. New in track3r-os: the 17 tracker effects.  Not checked against the original firmware: how the first 43 read and behave.

## What it is for

Use a step effect when one note needs its own treatment and a new instrument would be too much. You come here from [Pattern](pattern.md): press `Rec` for **STEP**, then `Fx`.

## How it works

### A step FX: live, stored and ended

A step FX is a mark on one step, like "slide here" on a score. Two cells mean two effects can work together on one note.

- **Live:** the effect acts when the sequencer reaches the step, and the grid shows its name, letter or mark and its value in hex.
- **Stored:** in the pattern, on that step, exactly as written. The FX stay as written even when the instrument is a module.
- **Ended:** most effects end with their step. **Panning** ends with its step. **Channel Pan** stays on the track until another Channel Pan, or until you stop and play again. Stop also gives channel and global volumes back, so the pads sound at full level.

### The value

The value sets how strong the effect is. The grid shows it in hex and the info line reads it in words, for example `DRIVE 40 %`. A new effect starts at its own default: Tune starts at 0 semitones. If a cell has an effect and you change its type, the value stays, cut to the new range.

(Picture: Pattern, STEP mode: the info line reads CHORD 5A for the effect under the cursor, in words.)

### Two effects that work together: Chord and Arp

A **Chord** on a MIDI track sounds all its notes at once. An **Arp** plays them one at a time, a note every 8 steps down to every 1/8 step. Example: a C note with Chord 5 (major) in FX1 and Arp 6 in FX2 plays C, then E, then G, one a step. With no Chord, an Arp changes nothing. On a sample track the Arp restarts the sample at each new pitch.

## Try it

1. Press `Pattern`, then `Rec` (**STEP**), then `Fx`. The cursor is on FX1 of step 1.

   (Picture: Pattern, STEP mode: the cursor is on the first effect cell of step 1.)

2. Hold `Vol`. The effect list opens with a description under it. Turn the encoder 14 detents to **Reverse**.

   (Picture: Pattern: the FX list is open and Reverse is highlighted, with its description under the list.)

3. Let go of `Vol`. The cell shows the effect's three-letter name, **REV**.
4. Turn the encoder up. The value stops at its last value, 01, and does not wrap.

   (Picture: Pattern: FX1 of step 1 reads REV01.)

5. Press `Fx` again. The cursor moves to FX2, and FX1 keeps its effect.

   (Picture: Pattern: the cursor is on the second effect cell, FX1 reads REV01.)

6. Press `Play` and listen to step 1: Reverse sets the direction the sample plays in. Not yet checked on the unit.

## The screen at a glance

| Area | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Fx column | Two effect cells per step, FX1 and FX2. Each shows the effect and its value in hex. At the 5-track zoom the effect is its three-letter name, for example `CHD` for Chord. An effect without a name, and the cells of the older zooms, show a letter or a mark.  |
| Info line | The effect under the cursor, in words, after the mode chip. For example `CHORD 5A`. |
| Effect list | The list of effects, shown while you hold `Vol`. The newest effects are at the end. |

## More tasks

### Set a big value

1. Hold `Shift` and turn the encoder. The value moves 16 at a time.

The value stops at its first and last value. It does not wrap around.

### Clear an effect

Start on the Pattern screen, in **STEP**, on the step with the effect.

1. Hold `Vol`. The effect list opens.
2. Turn the encoder to **None**.
3. Let `Vol` go. The cell is empty.

To clear the effects of several steps at once, put the cursor on **FX1** and press `Shift` + `Down` for each extra step. Press `Shift` + `Right` once more to add **FX2**, then `Delete`. The note and volume stay, and one `F8` (**UNDO**) takes it back. New in track3r-os. Not yet checked on the unit.

### Play a chord as an arpeggio

Start on the Pattern screen, in **STEP**, on a step with a C note. Use a MIDI track or a sample track.

1. Put **Chord** in FX1 with the value 5. The value 5 is a major chord, 4 is a minor chord.
2. Put **Arp** with the value 6 in the other effect cell. The value 6 plays the chord up, one note a step.
3. Press `Play`. The notes C, E and G play one after another, one a step.

### Look up an effect with words for its value

These effects read their value in words on the info line.

| Effect | What it does | Info line, with an example value |
|---|---|---|
| Chord | Plays the note as a chord. Value 5 is major, 4 is minor. | `CHORD 5A` for value 8  |
| Arp | Plays a chord one note at a time. It needs a Chord in the other cell. | `ARP DOWN 4 STEPS` for value 14  |
| Tune | Moves the note in semitones. Value 24 is no change. | `TUNE +7 ST` for value 31  |
| Slide Up, Slide Down | Slides the pitch over the step. The value is sixteenths of a semitone. | `SLIDE UP 2.19 ST` for value 35  |
| Glide | Slides from the last note on the track to this one. Value 0 is off. | `GLIDE 240 MS` for value 12  |
| Overdrive | Drives the sound. Value 0 is clean. | `DRIVE 40 %` for value 40  |
| Bit Depth | Lowers the bit depth. The range is 1 to 16, and 16 is off. | `BITS 8` for value 8  |
| Panning | Pans the note. Value 100 is hard right. It ends with its step. |  |
| Volume LFO, Panning LFO, Finetune LFO, Position LFO | Start the track's LFO for the volume (tremolo), the pan (auto-pan), the pitch (vibrato) or the wavetable window or granular position, on a sampler instrument. These four did nothing before; they act now, as Filter LFO does. The value is the LFO's speed in the same list as the instrument's own LFO speed, from the slowest at 0: 0 to 23 for Volume LFO, 0 to 28 for the others. The shape and amount are the instrument's LFO for that target (an instrument with none: triangle, 50 %). Position LFO moves only a wavetable or granular instrument and does nothing on a plain sample. While a Perform LFO row is held on the track its speed wins, and the FX comes back when the row ends or is at 0. Panning LFO and Panning (31) on one track: while the LFO runs it wins, because it sets the pan every block (a Panning step after it is overridden too); when the LFO ends the instrument's pan is back, and Panning acts again at its next step. The LFO stops at the next transport start. Stop does not end it: a pad note played after Stop still gets the LFO until the next Play. |  |

### Look up a tracker effect

The tracker effects are at the end of the list, after Bit Depth. Each has a mark in the grid. Their values are hex.

| Effect | Mark | Value | Info line, with an example value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tracker Arp | `@` | 37 | `ARPEG +3 +7`. Value 00 is `ARPEG OFF`.  |
| Volume Slide | `^` | 04 | `VSLIDE -4`. Value 40 is `VSLIDE +4`.  |
| Fine Volume Slide | `~` | 30 | `FVOL +3`  |
| Fine Porta Up | `<` | 10 | `FINE UP 4.00 PER`  |
| Fine Porta Down | `>` | 01 | `FINE DOWN 0.25 PER`  |
| Pan Slide | `=` | 04 | `PANSL R 4`  |
| Vibrato Wave | `"` | 02 | `VIB SQUARE`. Waves are 0 sine, 1 ramp, 2 square, 3 random.  |
| Tremolo Wave | `'` | 07 | `TREM RANDOM NORETRIG`  |
| Glissando | `;` | 01 | `GLISS ON`. Value 00 is `GLISS OFF`.  |
| Retrigger | `/` | 23 | `RETRIG EVERY 3 VOL -2`  |
| Tremor | `:` | 21 | `TREMOR ON 3 OFF 2`  |
| Channel Pan | `\|` | 4B | `CHPAN 75`. 50 is the centre.  |
| Channel Volume | `[` | 20 | `CHVOL 32`. 64 is full.  |
| Channel Vol Slide | `]` | 04 | `CHVSL -4`  |
| Global Volume | `(` | 30 | `GVOL 48`. 64 is full.  |
| Global Vol Slide | `)` | 40 | `GVSL +4`  |
| Panbrello | `{` | 3A | `PANBR SPD 3 DEP 10`  |

## Keys on this screen

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Fx` | Selects the Fx column on FX1. Press it again to move to FX2.  |
| hold `Vol` | Opens the effect list. Let go to enter the effect that is highlighted.  |
| encoder | Changes the value of the effect in the cell. While `Vol` is held, it moves through the list.  |
| `Shift` + encoder | Steps the value by 16. It stops at the first and last value.  |
| `F8` (**UNDO**) | Takes back the last change, with the other Pattern edits. A Song or Params edit stays. When nothing is left, the strip says **NOTHING TO UNDO HERE**.  |

## Good to know

- Not yet checked on the unit: how the effects sound. The simulator and host tests pass for the effects in this chapter. The unit check is still open.
- New in track3r-os: the tracker effects, from Tracker Arp to Panbrello.

- Writing a note by hand over a step that has a note replaces the note and its instrument with the ones in force. The volume and both effect cells stay. New in track3r-os. Not yet checked on the unit.
- The tracker effects run once a tick and are built to add only a few tenths of a percent of processor time. Not yet measured on the unit.
- Stop gives the channel and global volumes back, so the pads sound at full level after a stop.
- The effect list has 60 entries.
- Not checked against the original firmware: the Chord and Arp readings. This is an open research question.

## See also

- [Pattern](pattern.md): notes, the record modes and the Fx column keys.
- [Fill and tools](pattern_tools.md): fill a track with notes by a rule.
- [Modules and apps](modules.md): which effects a module instrument obeys is in [Step FX on module instruments](module-instrument-fx.md).
